decisions_taken.lint_robustness_group_bind_shape_lint: F-unconditional-group-bind-on-base was closed as not-reproducible with the measurement recorded, and the closure note asked that a lint keep it false rather than leaving it to be re-measured by hand. That lint is visibility_lint.rs::no_spliced_statement_binds_the_unconditional_group_array: no repo function may contain both a SPLICED statement and an unconditional group_bind()/writable_bind()/bypass_bind().unwrap_or(..) bind. Hosted in visibility_lint.rs rather than locked_decisions.rs because it reuses repo_fns()'s existing walk; a third scanner duplicating that walk was the alternative and was rejected. Granularity is the FUNCTION, an over-approximation stated in the doc: it can refuse a legitimate mixture but can never permit an illegitimate one, and today no function has both. Non-vacuity floors on BOTH populations (180 spliced fns and 30 unconditional-bind fns when written; floors set at 120 and 20), because the claim is that two large populations are disjoint and it is worthless if either is empty. MUTATION PROOF: rewriting repos/edge.rs::list_current_claim_targets's conditional bind as `.bind(viewer.group_bind().unwrap_or(&[]))` on its spliced statement fails the lint by name on its own assertion message; restored byte-identically and green.
decisions_taken.lint_robustness_repos_is_not_a_stripping: The scope recon proposed comment-stripping inside visibility_lint.rs::repo_fns() as 'probably the highest-leverage single edit'. MEASURED WITH THE REAL SCANNER AND NOT DONE, in either direction. Upside: exactly two phantom declarations exist (doc-example signatures in claim.rs and lineage.rs) and neither reaches any register, so the mechanism is live but inert. Downside: EXPECTED_EXEMPTIONS falls 9 -> 7 and two functions become offenders, because the VISIBILITY-EXEMPT convention is carried in COMMENTS BY DESIGN and two of its markers are Rust line comments rather than the in-SQL spelling the other 37 use. CORRECTION, re-measured after the lifetime defect below was fixed in this same diff: an earlier revision of this entry added 'stripping whole repo files loses 5 of 196 PgExecutor occurrences, because a lifetime toggles the stripper's string state -- which would silently drop functions out of the executor register'. Both halves are false against the SHIPPED stripper. Causal half: the lifetime no longer toggles string state; that is precisely what this diff fixed. Consequence half: re-measured over crates/epigraph-db/src/repos/ with the shipped stripper, `E: sqlx::PgExecutor` 191 -> 191 and `conn: &mut PgConnection` 52 -> 52 -- ZERO declarations lost. The bare token PgExecutor does go 196 -> 191 and all five losses are prose mentions in comments, i.e. correct stripping. The decision itself is unchanged and stands on the other measurement alone: VISIBILITY-EXEMPT goes 40 -> 32 under stripping, which is what would actually move a register. The general rule this establishes: the idiom-counting path and the marker/exemption path are different scans over the same file, and a stripper belongs only on the first. crates/epigraph-db/src/repos/ is therefore not a scan root for strip_comments, and both lint_text modules say so in place.
decisions_taken.lint_robustness_stripper_lifetime_defect: FOUND AND FIXED WHILE ADOPTING IT, and it is the reason the api half of this batch actually works. no_redaction_sentinel.rs::strip_comments entered string state on ANY single quote, so a Rust LIFETIME -- which has no partner tick -- left the scanner in string state from that point until the next apostrophe anywhere in the file, and the string arm copies bytes verbatim. Every comment in between survived unstripped. Measured, under a NAMED counting rule because an earlier revision of this entry gave the triple 137 / 52 / 34, which no single classification rule produces. Rule: a line whose first non-whitespace is `//` and which the shipped stripper blanks while the pre-fix one left intact. On that rule: 122 such lines under crates/epigraph-api/src/routes/, 52 under crates/epigraph-mcp/src/tools/, and 29 in routes/webhooks.rs -- the file whose doc comment produced F-PR10-fail-open-lint-counts-comments in the first place. The mechanism is unaffected by the correction; only the magnitudes were unstated-rule numbers, and they appear at three sites (this key and the strip_comments doc comment in BOTH lint_text modules), all three corrected together. THE DANGEROUS PART IS THAT IT MEASURES AS A CLEAN ADOPTION: registers are byte-identical stripped and unstripped on a clean tree whether the stripper works or is a partial no-op, so the 'no number moved' check cannot tell the two apart, and a mutation proof planted in a file with even tick parity passes either way. FIX: `'` is treated as a delimiter only in the char-literal SHAPE (bounded lookahead for the closing tick, escapes included); a lifetime emits its tick and stays in code. That is the rule visibility_lint.rs::balanced and viewer_route_table_lint.rs::balanced_block already used correctly in the same files, so this aligns the stripper with the in-tree precedent rather than inventing one. DIRECTION CORRECTED, also re-measured: an earlier revision said 'no_redaction_sentinel now sees strictly MORE code than before, which is the safe direction for a sentinel'. That is backwards. Old stripper vs new over all 818 .rs files under crates/: input falls from ~9.80M to ~9.63M bytes, strictly LESS in 106 files and strictly MORE in 20. Seeing less is safe here for a different and better reason: the reduction is entirely COMMENT TEXT. Token census old vs new across the same 818 files shows `pub fn ` 960 -> 960, `pub async fn ` 1381 -> 1381, `PgConnection` 116 -> 116, `PgExecutor` 194 -> 194, `#[test]` 2502 -> 2502; the handful of moving tokens (`struct ` -11, `fn ` -1, `impl ` -1, `sqlx::query` -1) are each prose -- 'Construct the signed message', 'Pure fn =>', '`sqlx::query` (not the macro)'. No declaration is lost crates-wide. MUTATION PROOF, end to end: the PR-10-shaped doc comment planted in routes/webhooks.rs at a line the unfixed stripper was blind at reproduces the original failure verbatim -- `webhooks.rs: expected 0, found 1 [REGRESSION]` -- with the lifetime fix reverted, and is GREEN with it. Regression fixtures for both directions (odd-parity `&'a` and `'static` must be stripped; `'/'` and `'\\'` char literals must not swallow the code after them) are pinned in the_scanner_detects_the_sentinel_it_is_looking_for, which now tests the shared helper.
decisions_taken.lint_robustness_deliberate_non_adoptions: The scope recon required this batch to triage the six scanners with zero comment stripping and SAY WHICH IT DELIBERATELY LEFT, because a blanket sweep is scope creep and a silent omission is indistinguishable from an oversight. Two roots were adopted (viewer_route_table_lint.rs::route_files, tool_viewer_coverage.rs) and crates/epigraph-db/src/repos/ was measured and refused -- see lint_robustness_repos_is_not_a_stripping_root. The remaining three, left deliberately, each with its reason: (1) crates/epigraph-db/tests/no_unscoped_pool.rs -- its `code_lines` helper ALREADY filters `!l.trim_start().starts_with("//")`, so whole-line comments are excluded by its own documented rule; the residual is trailing and block comments only, and HIGH_WATER / HIGH_WATER_FILES were correctly left untouched rather than re-baselined. (2) crates/epigraph-api/src/state.rs and (3) crates/epigraph-mcp/src/server.rs -- both in-crate lints assert EXACT EQUALITY on a needle split with concat! inside #[cfg(test)], so a comment quoting the needle fails LOUDLY rather than silently. Loud is the direction that does not need a stripper. Incompleteness against the recon's wording was flagged by review; this key is the durable record, which the implementer's hand-off message was not.
decisions_taken.lint_robustness_needle_completeness_cens: ADDED IN RESPONSE TO REVIEW, in the same commit as the needle widening it bounds. The widened AUTH_CTX_NEEDLES is proved SOUND by the_needle_set_finds_every_spelling_and_nothing_prescribed (each spelling matched once, pairwise non-substring, the prescribed let-else shape not charged). Nothing proved it COMPLETE, and measure_verbatim_auth_ctx_idiom defines the verbatim total AS the needle sum -- so the_registers_sum_to_the_verbatim_idiom is tautological with respect to coverage: a fifth spelling contributes zero to both sides. Every needle hard-codes the binder name `auth`, and this tree already binds others: routes/claims.rs::create_claim binds `ctx`, and two handlers bind `a` in a match arm. Both alternative binders are idiomatic here, not hypothetical. FIX: every_auth_ctx_occurrence_has_a_recognised_shape takes a census over the BINDER-AGNOSTIC substring `Some(axum::Extension(` and classifies each occurrence from the SURROUNDING SYNTAX, never consulting the needle set -- so `if_let == verbatim` compares two independent measurements of one set. MEASURED over comment-stripped src/routes/: 53 occurrences = 35 `if let` + 16 prescribed `let .. else` + 2 refusing `match` arms, with zero unclassified; 35 is exactly the needle-derived verbatim total. NOT PINNED at 53, against the reviewer's suggestion and for this file's own stated reason: `let .. else` and the refusing `match` are the CORRECT shapes, so a conversion raises them and an exact pin would redden the build for the fix -- the same trap the needle set itself refuses when it declines to widen to the bare substring. The load-bearing half is the equation plus `Unknown == 0` with a named remainder; the floors (40 / 12 / 1) are floors, well under the measurement. A `match` arm is counted as a refusal ONLY when the match refuses -- a non-refusing arm files as Unknown and reddens the build, because classifying every match arm as safe would itself be a control that reports safety it does not check. Self-tested over synthetic fixtures by the_auth_ctx_shape_classifier_is_not_vacuous, including the decisive pair: an `if let` with binder `ctx` classifies as IfLet AND is matched by zero needles, which is the case that makes the equation fire. NO REGISTER MOVED: the census is a new assertion over the existing population, not a re-baselining.

behaviour_changes.note: Everything PR-08 changes about what an existing caller observes. No in-repo client calls this endpoint and it has no OpenAPI entry (both verified by grep over *.py, *.sh, *.ts, *.js, *.json, *.yaml and crates/epigraph-api/src/openapi.rs), so the blast radius of all six is nil.
behaviour_changes.1_epsilon_default: 0.0 -> 1.0. A caller that omits the parameter now gets noised counts and `noise_applied: true` where it previously got exact counts and false.
behaviour_changes.2_new_403: epsilon in {0, negative, NaN, inf, > 1.0} now returns 403 without claims:admin. Previously epsilon was ungated entirely.
behaviour_changes.3_visible_set_aggregates: All nine aggregates are now visible-set aggregates. A caller that could previously read another tenant's whole-subgraph counts now reads only its visible part. This is the point of the PR.
behaviour_changes.4_agent_and_orphan_rows_excluded: ownership rows with node_type = 'agent', and rows whose node_id names no surviving row, now drop out of node_counts, temporal_bins, degrees and clustering_coefficients - for EVERY principal, including the owner. `agents` carries no tenancy columns so no predicate can decide it, and ownership has no FK to the tables it points at. This NARROWS THE OWNER'S OWN ANSWERS, which no acceptance line asks for; it is fail-closed per D1 (cannot classify is not public) rather than a fail-closed regression of the §R2 shape, because the rows are excluded rather than erroring. Asserted for both principals by owner_sees_the_whole_subgraph_and_a_stranger_only_its_public_part so the exclusion stays visible.
behaviour_changes.5_clustering_and_conflict_errors_now_500: Both statements used to end .unwrap_or_default(), rendering a query failure as an empty distribution. They now propagate.
behaviour_changes.6_clustering_stats_was_always_zero: A REAL PRE-EXISTING BUG, fixed here and observable only because of change 5. `2.0` and `1.0` are numeric literals in Postgres, so COALESCE(2.0 * tri_count / (deg * (deg - 1.0)), 0.0) had type numeric, which sqlx cannot decode into f64. EVERY request over a subgraph containing an actual triangle returned Err, and .unwrap_or_default() turned it into {mean: 0, variance: 0, eligible_nodes: 0}. The endpoint has reported zero clustering for exactly the graphs the statistic was written to describe since it existed. Fixed with ::double precision casts.
behaviour_changes.7_counts_and_moments_no_longer_agree: A CONSEQUENCE of fixing critic finding M3, stated so it is not read as a bug. Because the four moment blocks now have their COUNT component noised while their mean/variance/max stay exact, a default-epsilon response can carry degree_stats.total_nodes = 0 beside a non-zero mean and max_degree, or conflict_stats.entries = 3 beside mean = 0.0. The count and the moments in one block are no longer mutually consistent. This is the mechanism behaving correctly - noising a count down to zero is part of what partially mitigates F-structural-support-exact for the scalar fields - and `noise_applied: true` already tells a client not to read the numbers as exact. See F-structural-moments-exact.

scope_addition_epsilon_ceiling.note: PR-08 adds a refusal the plan does not ask for. Recorded as a deliberate scope addition rather than slipped in, because a silent deviation is the failure mode this ledger exists to prevent.
scope_addition_epsilon_ceiling.what: MAX_UNPRIVILEGED_EPSILON = 1.0 in routes/structural.rs, and noise_engages became `epsilon.is_finite() && epsilon > 0.0 && epsilon <= MAX_UNPRIVILEGED_EPSILON`. The default IS the ceiling (default_epsilon() returns the constant, pinned by the_default_is_the_ceiling): a caller may buy more privacy, never less.
scope_addition_epsilon_ceiling.why: The gate closed epsilon = 0, -1, NaN and inf and shipped the fourth member of the same class. 1e300 is finite and positive, so it passed the gate UNSCOPED, while b = 1/epsilon = 1e-300 made the noise term round away and the count come back exact - a claims:read caller obtained the exact counts the claims:admin gate exists to withhold, with "noise_applied": true in the body. The plan's literal acceptance line (epsilon=0.0 -> 403) was still satisfied, which is why the first pass and the verifier both let it stand; its PURPOSE (exact counts are an administrative capability) was defeated by one query-string character.
scope_addition_epsilon_ceiling.why_1_0_and_not_10: A ceiling in the conventional DP range would have closed almost nothing. At epsilon=10, b=0.1 and P(|noise| > 0.5) = e^-5 = 0.0067, so 99.3% of single draws are already exact and the mode over a handful of requests is the exact count. At 1.0, b=1.0 and P(|noise| > 0.5) = e^-0.5 = 0.61.
scope_addition_epsilon_ceiling.residual: This closes the SINGLE-REQUEST exact read only. There is still no privacy budget - see open finding F-structural-no-privacy-budget.

critic_findings_2026_09_02.B1_rand_simple_returns_0_to_2_and_NaN_is: FIXED. THE BLOCKER, and PR-08's own default flip is what made it live. routes/structural.rs::rand_simple was documented `[0, 1)` and returned `[0, 2)`: `>> 16` of a u32 lies in [0, 65536) and it divided by 32768 - the divisor was wrong by a factor of two. maybe_add_noise then computed u = r - 0.5 in [-0.5, 1.5), and for every u > 0.5 the term (1 - 2|u|) was NEGATIVE, ln of it NaN, and (value + NaN).round().max(0.0) returned 0, because Rust's f64::max returns the non-NaN operand. Same launder-an-error-into-a-benign-answer shape this PR removed from clustering_coefficients's .unwrap_or_default(), one function away. MEASURED over 1,000,000 seeds with the two functions compiled verbatim: 500,001 returned 0 instead of 42 (50.00%) and 15 hit the |u| == 0.5 boundary where ln(0) = -inf saturates the cast to i64::MAX. Before PR-08 the path was dead (epsilon defaulted to 0.0, apply_noise false); flipping the default to 1.0 put every caller on it, so the endpoint would have reported roughly half of an owner's counts as 0 - reading as `this owner has nothing`, not as garbage. FIX: rand_simple is DELETED and maybe_add_noise draws from `rand` (already a non-optional dependency of epigraph-api - oauth/authorize.rs, spans.rs), whose Rng::gen::<f64>() is uniform on [0, 1) by contract. That also closes the separate defect that rand_simple reseeded an LCG from SystemTime::now().subsec_nanos() on EVERY call, making draws within one request correlated and predictable from the request time. An explicit `arg > 0.0` guard plus an is_finite check mean no NaN or infinity can reach .max(0.0) again. ThreadRng is !Send, so the generator is constructed and dropped inside the synchronous maybe_add_noise and never held across an .await.
critic_findings_2026_09_02.B1_why_no_test_saw_it: maybe_add_noise_never_negative asserted `noisy >= 0` over 100 draws - which the broken code SATISFIED, because 0 was its failure output. The new acceptance test asserted only `noise_applied == true` and never inspected a count. REPLACED by maybe_add_noise_is_centred_on_the_true_value_and_almost_never_zeroes_it: 2000 draws at epsilon=1 over a true count of 100, asserting the median is within 2 of the true value, that fewer than 1% of draws are zero, and that none saturates i64::MAX. Complemented by no_draw_in_the_unit_interval_produces_a_non_finite_noise_term, a deterministic 10,001-point sweep of the whole draw range including both endpoints.
critic_findings_2026_09_02.B1_falsification: The new assertions were replayed against the OLD rand_simple, compiled verbatim standalone, to prove they are falsifying rather than vacuous. Result over 2000 draws at epsilon=1, true count 100: zeros = 1045/2000 against a threshold of 20, so the zero-rate assertion FAILS on the old code; median = 0 against a required [98, 102], so the centredness assertion FAILS on the old code. In the same run the assertion they REPLACE, `all samples >= 0`, PASSES on the old code - which is the vacuity finding demonstrated rather than argued.
critic_findings_2026_09_02.M2_large_epsilon_bypasses_the_claims_adm: FIXED. See scope_addition_epsilon_ceiling. critic_findings_2026_09_02.M3_moment_count_fields_exact_at_every_ep: FIXED. degree_stats.total_nodes, belief_stats.claims_with_belief, clustering_stats.eligible_nodes and conflict_stats.entries were exact at every epsilon and returned to any claims:read caller in the same response whose five other count fields were gated. total_nodes is the row count of StructuralRepository::degrees - the SAME quantity as the sum of the nominally-noised node_counts - so the gate withheld nothing. FIX: a single noise_all_counts(&mut response, apply, epsilon) applied after the response is assembled, covering all nine count-shaped fields. Noising at each construction site is what allowed four to be missed. The means, variances and maxima are deliberately untouched (F-structural-moments-exact). Covered by noise_all_counts_covers_every_count_and_no_moment (deterministic at epsilon=1e-6, spurious-failure probability ~5e-7 per field), its no-op control, and the HTTP test the_moment_count_fields_are_noised_for_a_caller_without_claims_admin (epsilon=0.001 vs an admin epsilon=0 reference, joint spurious-failure probability ~6e-14, with a non-vacuity check that the exact values are non-zero).

minor_and_nit_fixed.not_db_stub_noise_applied: FIXED. The #[cfg(not(feature = "db"))] stub hardcoded noise_applied: false even when noise_engages(params.epsilon) was true, the only field on which the two builds disagreed. It now mirrors the db handler. noise_all_counts is deliberately NOT called there: every count is a structural zero, and noising them would make the two builds disagree about the NUMBERS, which is worse than the flag mismatch.
minor_and_nit_fixed.viewer_extractor_401_backstop_doc_was_fa: FIXED AS A DOC. The handler doc claimed ViewerExtractor is the fail-closed 401 backstop `if the registration ever moves`. axum::Extension<AuthContext> is declared FIRST and FromRequestParts extractors run in declaration order, so ExtensionRejection::MissingExtension would fire first and that is a 500, not a 401. The doc is corrected rather than the extractors reordered: viewer_route_table_lint.rs reads handler signature shape, and re-baselining a lint in the same change that fixes a blocker would hide one behind the other.
minor_and_nit_fixed.edge_counts_double_counts: FIXED AS A DOC. `JOIN ownership o ON (e.source_id = o.node_id OR e.target_id = o.node_id)` counts an edge once per OWNED ENDPOINT, so a both-endpoints-owned edge counts twice. Pre-existing and carried over verbatim, but PR-08 is the first thing to pin it as expected output (SUPPORTS == 4 for two seeded edges), so edge_counts's doc now states it. Its Laplace sensitivity is therefore 2, not the 1 maybe_add_noise assumes - open finding F-edge-count-double-counts.
minor_and_nit_fixed.module_docs_restated_as_a_rule: The module doc said `The Laplace mechanism covers FIVE of the nine outputs` and listed four blocks as exact at any epsilon. Both statements are now false, and a false doc comment is what hid B1 for a full implement-verify cycle. Restated as a RULE - every count-shaped field is noised; means, variances and maxima are not - so it cannot drift back into a stale count.

behaviour_changes.1_request_viewer_hard_refuses_an_agentle: An HTTP AuthContext with agent_id: None is now refused outright (was a.agent_id.or(owner_id).unwrap_or(client_id), a type confusion between oauth_clients.id and agents.id that happened to yield public-only). behaviour_changes.3_ensure_personal_group_is_an_authority_: The call sits after the if/else, so it runs on BOTH branches - required, since every existing deployment takes the found branch. Its membership insert is ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET revoked_at = NULL, role = 'admin', so an operator who revoked the MCP server agent's personal-group membership sees it revived at admin role on the next process boot. The reviving form was kept rather than adding a DO NOTHING variant: repos/agent.rs documents at length why DO NOTHING was wrong (a pre-existing revoked epoch-0 row makes the insert a permanent silent no-op), and this is already what every API principal gets on every oauth/token.rs mint. It is also a WRITE ON A READ PATH - reject_if_read_only is a per-tool gate, so a --read-only server performs it on its first tool call - and it FAILS CLOSED (a failure warns and leaves a public-only viewer). All three properties are now stated at the function.
behaviour_changes.4_system_stats_cardinalities_are_now_vis: 'rows this viewer can read', not 'rows that exist'. Inert until PR-12.
behaviour_changes.5_list_events_and_graph_snapshot_are_vie: An event is dropped when some uuid ANYWHERE in its payload names a claims row the viewer cannot read. graph_snapshot's event_count is therefore viewer-dependent too. An event naming a uuid that resolves to NO claims row is deliberately KEPT, so snapshot fidelity does not depend on referential integrity - an earlier revision dropped these and that was reverted.
behaviour_changes.6_list_candidates_excerpts_now_include_s: Unchanged from base, but only because it was caught. The inline read it replaced had no is_current filter; contents_by_ids has one. match_candidates rows outlive the claims they name, so every superseded pair would have rendered as the literal '(claim not found)'. list_candidates now calls the new contents_by_ids_any_version.
behaviour_changes.7_get_cross_source_matches_404s_for_an_i: The existence probe is viewer-scoped, so a claim the caller cannot read 404s exactly as a nonexistent one does (8.5). Previously it was an existence oracle for every private claim id.
behaviour_changes.8_two_new_inner_joins_narrow_row_sets_fo: scan_candidates adds JOIN claims ct ON ct.id = s1.target_id, and corroborates_edges_for_claim adds JOIN claims far. Both are required for the stated property (filtering only the supporters still leaks the target id, which the `reason` string interpolates). Side effect: a `supports` edge whose target is not a claims row, and a CORROBORATES edge whose far endpoint is not a claims row, are now dropped rather than returned. edges carries source_type/target_type, so non-claim endpoints are representable. Recorded here because no tenancy test will ever show it.
behaviour_changes.9_suggest_alternative_sets_filters_its_e: s1, s2 and contr all carry a predicate now - edges IS in migration 062's tier_a. Three public claims joined by a group-private contradicts edge are no longer returned to a stranger, because the response's own `reason` asserts that edge exists. The `existing` alternative_of LEFT JOIN is deliberately NOT filtered: its role is suppression, so filtering it would let a viewer re-accept a link that already exists and write a duplicate. Leaving it unfiltered can only NARROW a result set, which is fail-closed and discloses nothing.
behaviour_changes.10_submit_ds_evidence_refuses_outright_o: REACHABLE TODAY, independently of PR-12, and the only such change besides #6. The per-id belief read went from `fetch_one` to `fetch_optional(..)?.ok_or_else(|| invalid_request("claim {id} not found"))`, so (a) a NONEXISTENT claim_id now yields invalid_request where it previously yielded RowNotFound -> internal_error, and (b) an INVISIBLE claim is refused identically, which is plan 8.5's indistinguishability property. Unlike the other three per-id oracles PR-09 hardened - ds_auto, link_epistemic, workflows, which all DEGRADE (no prior / skip the recompute / skip the cascade child) - this one aborts the call, so it DOES decide the write half for this tool: a viewer that cannot read a claim cannot submit evidence against it. Correct under D3 (you may not assert about what you may not read), but a decision rather than a side effect, which is why D-PR16-per-id-claim-oracles-write-half is scoped to the other three.
behaviour_changes.11_two_uuid_extractors_are_deliberately_: epigraph-api's `payload_uuids` is a SUPERSET of the SQL's regexp_matches, not an exact mirror. Postgres returns non-overlapping matches (it resumes after the end of each); the Rust scanner slides over every byte offset and collects overlapping windows. So the in-memory half can only drop MORE events than the persisted half - fail-closed. The property to preserve is `rust superset-of sql`, NOT `rust == sql`: narrowing Rust to match Postgres would make the in-memory half the more permissive of the two, which is the direction that leaks. Stated at `payload_uuids` so nobody later 'fixes' the asymmetry.

critic_findings_2026_09_03.note: 33 findings, 14 blocker/major. Every blocker and major is either fixed or rejected with reasoning; none was silently dropped.
critic_findings_2026_09_03.B1_event_list_was_default_open_for_every: FIXED, and it was a real blocker. The filter keyed on payload->>'claim_id' while the live emitters do not use that key: routes/conflicts.rs writes conflict.resolved with claim_a_id/claim_b_id/winner_id, routes/gaps.rs writes challenge_id, and both MCP publish_event and POST /api/v1/events accept arbitrary payloads - so any key allowlist is a rule the next emitter escapes. The rule is now 'an event is returned unless some uuid appearing ANYWHERE in its payload names a claims row this viewer cannot read', implemented as regexp_matches(payload::text, '<uuid>', 'g') over the whole serialised document (nested objects, arrays, keys and uuids inside free text all included). Over-collection is safe by construction: a token naming no claims row cannot suppress anything, because the inner EXISTS requires the row first. Both doc blocks were rewritten to describe the property the SQL has. The regex guard the previous revision needed (Postgres does not short-circuit AND, so a sibling-conjunct guard would not stop 'not-a-uuid'::uuid raising 22P02) is no longer needed and its absence is explained: regexp_matches yields only substrings that already matched.
critic_findings_2026_09_03.B1_falsification: M3 - the SQL was mutated back to the narrow rule (regexp_matches over COALESCE(payload->>'claim_id','')). Result: the pre-existing list_events_hides_an_event_naming_a_private_claim PASSED and the new list_events_hides_an_event_whose_payload_names_a_private_claim_under_another_key FAILED. acceptance.2_list_webhooks_requires_auth: MET, but the plan's phrasing understates the defect and the fix. Neither read route was ever ANONYMOUS - both have always been on the `protected` chain in both create_router variants, which the plan's own 4.9 row 11 concedes ('anonymity was never the vector'). What they lacked was a PRINCIPAL and an OWNERSHIP FILTER: list_webhooks returned every subscription in the process (id, url, event_types, created_at) to any authenticated caller and get_webhook was a straight IDOR by uuid. Both now take middleware::bearer::RequirePrincipal and answer only for the caller's own rows. tests/webhook_tenancy.rs::{the_webhook_read_routes_require_a_token, list_webhooks_returns_only_the_callers_own_subscriptions, get_webhook_refuses_another_principals_subscription}.

PR-10 changes its signature in BOTH cfg arms (the db arm now takes a `sqlx::PgPool` it clones into the `'static` subscriber closure) and changes its call site in bin/server.rs. No test runs it: `build_app_for_tests` never calls it - only bin/server.rs does - and webhook_tenancy.rs deliberately calls `deliver_event` directly rather than putting an HTTP-POSTing background task into every one of the ~40 integration binaries that use spawn_app. The dispatcher is a `tokio::spawn` around `deliver_event`; the RULE is in `deliver_event` and `agent_may_receive`, and that is what the ten tests and the three mutation probes exercise. behaviour_changes.1_get_api_v1_webhooks_returns_fewer_rows: Previously every active subscription in the process, to any authenticated principal, with NO webhooks scope required (a claims:read-only token could read the instance's whole delivery topology). Now the caller's own only. Operator tooling that enumerated all subscriptions through this endpoint STOPS WORKING. Deliberate; there is no admin-wide variant and adding one is a new route + allowlist entry + scope, not a fall-through. No secret was ever exposed (#[serde(skip_serializing)] on both secret and the owner field) - the leak was URL/topology inventory.
behaviour_changes.2_get_api_v1_webhooks_id_answers_403_for: Was an IDOR. 403 rather than 404 so that the answer to 'you do not own this' is identical to delete_webhook's, which webhooks_auth_test.rs::delete_webhook_by_different_caller_returns_403 pins. The existence disclosure traded away is bounded: the id is an unguessable v4 uuid and the caller is already authenticated.
behaviour_changes.3_fan_out_delivers_fewer_events_and_the_: An existing external subscriber silently receives fewer deliveries. This is the fix, but it is a live integration contract and the failure mode is silence, not an error, so every suppression emits a warn/error on the `webhook.delivery.suppressed` tracing target with a `reason` field (no_agent_id | viewer_resolve_failed | payload_names_invisible_claim | visibility_probe_failed | no_db_feature). A database outage now STOPS webhook delivery rather than broadcasting every tenant's claims - the intended trade, stated on the function. CAVEAT, stated rather than implied: NO TEST ASSERTS THE LOG LINE FIRES. The `webhook.delivery.suppressed` target is instrumentation, not a control, and it is unverified instrumentation - the crate has no `tracing-test` harness and PR-10 did not add one. An operator whose only signal that tenancy suppressed a delivery is a log line nobody proved emits should read this as 'best effort', not as a guarantee. Adding the harness is a reasonable follow-up; claiming the observability without it would be the asserted-but-false shape this series exists to avoid.
behaviour_changes.4_post_api_v1_webhooks_becomes_db_depend: register_webhook was pure in-memory and could not fail on I/O. It now has a 500 path, including the agent_id FK violation raised when a token names an agent that no longer exists. It also 401s on a token carrying no agent_id, which it previously accepted (storing client_id as the owner).
behaviour_changes.5_admin_stats_webhook_count_semantics:
GET /api/v1/admin/stats computes WebhookStats { webhook_count } from state.webhook_store.len() (routes/admin.rs::system_stats), UNCHANGED as code. Its MEANING changed, and this PR is what changed it: it used to count subscriptions registered in this process since boot; with boot hydration it now counts the cardinality of webhook_subscriptions ACROSS EVERY TENANT, and it survives a restart.

This matters more than a stats field normally would, because `system_stats` takes NO auth extractor and NO check_scopes call - only `State(state)` - and is registered on the `protected` router in both the db and no-db chains, so any authenticated principal with any scope reads it. It discloses a COUNT, never a url, a secret or an owner. But it is also a counterexample to the invariant repos/webhook.rs::list_active's doc originally asserted (`every path out of that store to an HTTP response is ownership-filtered by the handler`), and a written justification whose named invariant the same commit falsifies is worse than the leak. That doc is corrected in the land phase to say what is true - CONTENT-serialising paths are ownership-filtered, system_stats discloses cardinality only - and the scope gate is left to F-PR10-admin-stats-unscoped rather than bolted on here: SystemStats is a fourteen-field aggregate and two of its tests assert on webhook_count.

Its own test (admin.rs::test_system_stats_reflects_webhook_store) is inside a `#[cfg(all(test, not(feature = "db")))]` module that, as MEASURED in gate.no_db_all_targets_EXTRA_NOT_PART_OF_THE_GATE, does not compile in any configuration - so nothing would have caught a regression here either way. That is now a measurement rather than the inference it was.
behaviour_changes.6_subscriptions_survive_a_restart:
The first deploy after this lands resurrects nothing (the table starts empty); every subsequent one preserves state. This was previously recorded as pure upside. IT HAS TWO COSTS, and both rest on a SINGLE-INSTANCE ASSUMPTION that the code makes nowhere and documented nowhere until now.
  (a) REVOCATION IS NOT PROCESS-WIDE. delete_webhook removes the row and its own process's cache entry. Any other api instance that hydrated that row at boot keeps subscriptions_matching returning it and keeps POSTing HMAC-signed payloads to an endpoint the owner revoked, until that instance restarts. Before PR-10 this could not happen: a subscription existed only in the process that registered it, so `store.remove` in that process was complete revocation.
  (b) DUPLICATE DELIVERY. Before PR-10 one event produced one delivery, because only the registering process held the subscription. After hydration every instance holds every subscription, so a subscriber receives N copies per event on an N-instance deployment.
Neither fires on a single instance, which is what this host runs. Filed as F-PR10-webhook-store-no-cross-process-invalidation and D-PR-webhook-store-invalidation rather than fixed: a read-through cache with TTL or an event-bus invalidation channel is a mechanism, not a tenancy filter, and adding one inside a security PR is the kind of scope growth this series avoids. NOTE the related asymmetry recorded under open_findings: a delete routed to a process that never saw the row 404s from the cache BEFORE the repo call, so on a multi-instance deployment the row can be unreachable. delete_webhook was NOT reordered to delete-then-404, because deriving 404 from rows_affected is a behaviour change on a single instance for a multi-instance-only benefit; instead the discarded rows_affected is now bound and a `rows == 0` divergence is logged at warn.
behaviour_changes.7_delete_webhook_no_longer_stalls_the_we: LAND-PHASE FIX to code this PR wrote. The handler took `state.webhook_store.write().await`, then awaited the repo delete WHILE STILL HOLDING THE GUARD, and only then called `store.remove(&id)`. tokio's RwLock is fair, so a pending writer blocks new readers: for the whole duration of the DB round trip, deliver_event's per-event read lock, list_webhooks, get_webhook and register_webhook all blocked. A hung Postgres would therefore have stalled the very fan-out this PR exists to make correct - and on this host a wedged Postgres is not hypothetical (pgBackRest ENOSPC crash-looped prod for hours; the static-IP boot race recurs on every reboot). This was an oversight against the file's OWN discipline, not a considered trade: register_webhook deliberately persists BEFORE taking the write lock, and start_webhook_dispatcher's doc explicitly claims the store lock is not held across an await. Clippy cannot see it (`await_holding_lock` fires only on std::sync::MutexGuard). Now: the owner's agent_id is copied out under a READ guard which is dropped at the end of the block, the ownership decision runs on the copy, the DB delete runs with NO guard held, and the write guard is taken solely for `store.remove(&id)`. The observable 401/403/404/204 ordering is unchanged, which webhooks_auth_test.rs (5/5) and webhook_tenancy.rs (10/10) both still pass on.
behaviour_changes.8_the_two_new_500_bodies_no_longer_echo_: register_webhook and delete_webhook build ApiError::InternalError, and errors.rs's IntoResponse serialises `message` straight into the JSON body. Both were `format!("...: {e}")`, which would hand an API client Postgres constraint names, relation names and driver text (e.g. `violates foreign key constraint "webhook_subscriptions_agent_id_fkey"`). register_webhook could not fail on I/O at all before PR-10, so this was a brand-new disclosure surface introduced by this PR rather than an inherited one. The bodies are now fixed strings; the `tracing::error!` one line above already carries the full error for the operator. No test asserted on the old body text (grepped).

critic_findings_2026_09_03_land.MAJOR_unknown_claim_id_delivers_and_batc: PARTLY FIXED, PARTLY REJECTED-WITH-REASONS, and filed. The critic's FACTS are all correct and were re-verified: routes/batch.rs::batch_create_claims has zero db_pool / sqlx:: / ClaimRepository references, inserts only into state.claim_store, and then publishes one EpiGraphEvent::ClaimSubmitted per claim, so those claim ids name no `claims` row, hidden_claim_ids returns empty, agent_may_receive returns true, and the payload reaches every active subscription. BOTH SUGGESTED FIXES ARE WRONG, which is why the code is unchanged. (i) 'treat named-but-absent as suppression' would suppress nearly every event, because payload_uuids also collects agent, frame and workflow ids and none of those name a claims row - it is not a stricter filter, it is an off switch. (ii) 'narrow the scanner to the ids the event declares as claim ids' is exactly the key allowlist PR-09's commit body rejected verbatim ('any key allowlist is a rule the next emitter escapes'), and re-adopting it here would fork the one scanner into two. WHAT WAS FIXED IS THE FALSE CLAIM: agent_may_receive's 'Everything here fails closed' heading enumerated three branches and did not name this fourth, so the doc asserted a property the function does not have. Both webhooks.rs's module doc and agent_may_receive's doc now name it explicitly, with the reasoning above. NOT A PR-10 REGRESSION - before this PR every event went to every subscriber unconditionally, so the change is strictly in the closing direction. batch.rs is untouched: it takes no auth extractor at all and widening into it is a different PR. Filed as F-PR10-unknown-claim-id-delivers.
critic_findings_2026_09_03_land.MAJOR_no_claim_content_to_leak_is_false_: FIXED AS A DOC/TEST DEFECT; the deny is filed, not invented. The module doc called the four claim-less variants 'a non-case: they contribute no claim uuid, so no claim content can leak, so they are delivered.' The inference is wrong: the property the fan-out needs is NO CROSS-TENANT CONTENT, which is strictly stronger. epigraph_core::domain::agent_identity::SuspensionReason has three variants carrying `details: String` (PolicyViolation, SecurityConcern, Administrative) plus AgentSuspended carries suspended_by, and ReputationChanged carries per-agent scores - none of which payload_uuids or hidden_claim_ids can see. AgentCreated and WorkflowCompleted really are inert (AgentRole and WorkflowState are unit-only enums). MEASURED AND LOAD-BEARING: zero production publishers - every construction site of AgentSuspended and ReputationChanged is inside epigraph-events' own tests and its event_type() round-trip fixture (grep over crates/ excluding epigraph-events returns nothing). done.summary: PolicyGate stops being a dead struct field and becomes an enforced, fail-closed, resource-aware write gate. epigraph-interfaces/src/policy.rs is rewritten around `ResourceRef` (Option owners, unauthorizable when both are absent), `Decision` (no Default, no From<bool>) and an infallible `PolicyGate::authorize` that maps every `Err(_)` to a denial in one place; `NoOpPolicyGate` (allow-all, `is_active()==false`, never called by anything) is replaced by `DenyAllPolicyGate` as the type-level floor and `AllowAllPolicyGate` behind `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "insecure-allow-all"))]`. The durable decision function lives in the NEW crate crates/epigraph-authz (`GroupPolicyGate`), which holds no SQL, no pool and no epigraph-db dependency - which is what lets epigraph-api name it under --no-default-features. It is installed at all six AppState constructors and both EpiGraphMcpFull constructors, and consulted at four write sites: HTTP routes/ownership.rs::{assign_ownership,update_partition} and MCP tools/perspectives.rs::{assign_ownership,update_partition}. EncryptionProvider and OrchestrationBackend are deleted outright, as the plan's Files line prescribes.

acceptance.1_a_reader_role_member_cannot_write_to_t: MET, against a REAL membership row rather than a hand-built Principal. crates/epigraph-authz/tests/fail_closed.rs::a_reader_role_member_cannot_write_to_their_own_group seeds an agent with role='reader' in a group, builds the Principal through `Viewer::resolve` (NOT `Viewer::test_scoped`, which would let the fixture assert the property it is supposed to measure), and asserts the gate denies a write to that group. Paired with a writer-role positive control in the same file, so the denial is evidence about the ROLE and not about the fixture failing to seed anything.
acceptance.2_a_fresh_appstate_denies_by_default: MET, and now BOTH ways round. The mechanism half is state.rs::extension_wiring_tests (the value all six constructors install, asserted behaviourally) plus the_default_gate_is_installed_at_every_constructor (a six-literal source count, so the behavioural tests stay connected to the constructors they describe). The plan's phrase 'the inverse of today's `default_gate_allows_all`' names a test that EXISTS NOWHERE IN THE REPO; the negative test was WRITTEN, not inverted - see corrections. NOTE the honest limit, unchanged from the implement phase: no AppState is constructed by these tests, because every constructor needs a live PgPool. What IS now constructed end-to-end is the ROUTER, by write_gate_denies_at_the_route.rs, which drives real HTTP requests through spawn_app -> create_router and gets a real 403 out of the real state.policy_gate.

files_line_reconciliation.1_the_13_write_call_sites_do_not_exist: The plan's Files line ends with 'the 13 write call sites', which reads as 'rewire thirteen existing PolicyGate checks'. THERE WERE ZERO. Verified independently at this base: `git grep -l policy_gate -- crates/` returned exactly one file, state.rs, where the gate was constructed six times (:364,410,441,532,565,600), stored as `pub policy_gate: SharedPolicyGate` and made swappable by `with_policy_gate` - and never consulted. No handler, repo function or MCP tool called `.check(`. The number 13 is real but belongs to a DIFFERENT set: it is plan S4.6's thirteen production `INSERT INTO claims` statements, assigned to PR-16 at plan :3714. PR-11 therefore INTRODUCES authorization at write paths for the first time, at FOUR sites derived from the code.
files_line_reconciliation.2_allowallpolicygate_did_not_exist: The plan says to put `AllowAllPolicyGate` behind `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "insecure-allow-all"))]`. No such type existed; the real one was `epigraph_interfaces::policy::NoOpPolicyGate`, whose own doc called it 'Kernel-default allow-all policy gate'. The plan's substance was right and only the name was wrong, so `AllowAllPolicyGate` is created under exactly that cfg. The feature IS declared in epigraph-interfaces/Cargo.toml and NO manifest in the workspace enables it, pinned by a workspace-wide Cargo.toml walk in epigraph-db/tests/locked_decisions.rs. See decisions_taken.PR11_insecure_allow_all_guards_a_name for what that control does and does not buy.
files_line_reconciliation.3_default_gate_allows_all_exists_nowhere: The Acceptance line asks for 'the inverse of today's `default_gate_allows_all`'. That identifier appears nowhere in the repository except FINAL-PLAN.md itself. There was no test to invert; policy.rs::tests::the_kernel_default_denies_every_action is the negative test written from scratch.
files_line_reconciliation.4_the_authz_crate_is_stricter_than_the_p: Plan S2.8 says 'GroupPolicyGate (no SQL, repo calls only)', which PERMITS repo calls. This crate makes none and takes no pool at all. That is a DIVERGENCE from the plan, not conformance to it, and the manifest comment now says so - an in-code comment that reads a plan as prescribing what it merely allows is the same class of defect as trusting a plan count, with the sign flipped. The reason for the stricter shape is the dependency direction: epigraph-db would have to depend on epigraph-authz to call it and epigraph-authz would have to depend on epigraph-db to resolve roles, so the caller resolves a Viewer once per request and hands the gate the already computed writable_groups.
files_line_reconciliation.5_no_migration: PR-11 is code-only. migrations/README.md - authoritative over the plan - assigns PR-11 no number, and none was added. `git status --short migrations/` is empty; the live DB head is 91, the highest file.
files_line_reconciliation.6_action_read_is_deleted_and_the_plan_do: The Files line prescribes a policy.rs rewrite for ResourceRef and Decision and says nothing about the Action enum. `Action::Read` is DELETED anyway. Plan :146 says reads are never gated by PolicyGate; deleting the variant makes a read-side check inexpressible rather than merely discouraged, which is the same 'unconstructible, not un-chosen' discipline epigraph_db::visibility uses. A workspace-wide grep (including the excluded epigraph-harvester) finds no remaining consumer, so nothing in-tree breaks. Residual risk is out-of-tree: Action is a published kernel extension point re-exported by epigraph-core, and a downstream crate matching on it will fail to compile. Recorded as decisions_taken.PR11_action_read_deleted so PR-19 (which reborns EncryptionProvider as ContentSealer and re-opens this file) inherits the rationale.
files_line_reconciliation.7_the_write_group_count_in_tool_viewer_c: The base EXPECTED_TOOLS_WITHOUT_A_VIEWER doc said '(18)' while the base array held 17 write-group entries. PR-11 removed two names, so the correct new figure is 15 and the array agrees. The pre-existing off-by-one is corrected in the doc rather than silently absorbed.

scope_substitution.four_gate_call_sites_not_thirteen: HTTP routes/ownership.rs::{assign_ownership,update_partition} and MCP tools/perspectives.rs::{assign_ownership,update_partition}. These are the DECLASSIFICATION surface - what turns a private node public - which is the operation the PR title names and the one S9's leak table rates blocker. epigraph-api/tests/write_gate_call_sites.rs pins exactly that set, in both directions.
scope_substitution.mcp_assign_ownership_was_claims_write_wh: scope_map.rs gates HTTP update_partition at claims:admin but MCP assign_ownership at claims:write, so a claims:write token could set partition_type on any node over MCP. Widening the scope entry would have been the smaller change; it would also have been a scope check, which cannot say 'this principal, this node'. The gate is not redundant with the scope map even where the scope map is stricter, because server.rs::call_tool runs enforce_tool_scope ONLY for HTTP calls.
scope_substitution.the_no_db_ownership_stubs_are_deliberate: The four handlers are cfg-twins. The `not(feature = "db")` arms take no gate, with the rationale written at the stubs: epigraph-db is optional=true there, so that build has no OwnershipRepository, no `ownership` table and therefore no owner of record to authorize against - assign_ownership echoes the request back and writes nothing. The two arms' signatures already differed before PR-11 (the db arm carried RequireScopeAdmin and the stub did not), so the asymmetry cannot break the --no-default-features build the way a mismatched SHARED signature would - the hazard that cost PR-08 18 CI errors. Verified COLD in a freshly rm -rf'd dedicated target dir.

behaviour_changes.1_claims_admin_is_no_longer_sufficient_f: BREAKING. Before PR-11 a claims:admin token could assign ownership of any node to any agent and change any node's partition. The new rule, over BOTH HTTP and MCP: a node that has an `ownership` row may be changed only by the owner that row records; a node that has none may be claimed only TO YOURSELF. Because ownership.community_id references `communities` and not `groups`, no owner_group is ever supplied at these four sites, so the gate's group arm never fires here and the owner-of-record arm is the whole decision. OPS IMPACT: any provisioning or ingestion runbook that records a document's author as its owner on the author's behalf now gets a 403 with a deliberately reason-free body. No existing test exercised a SUCCESSFUL call to these handlers before PR-11, so the suite could not have told you whether anything depended on it; write_gate_denies_at_the_route.rs::assign_ownership_on_an_unclaimed_node_is_self_only now pins the narrowing deliberately, in both directions.
behaviour_changes.2_mcp_assign_ownership_with_owner_id_omi: BREAKING on the HTTP MCP transport, and a bug fix. The tool previously defaulted an omitted owner_id to EpiGraphMcpFull::agent_id() - the SERVER's own signing-key agent row, not the requester. On stdio the two are the same identity, so the difference was invisible; over HTTPS 'claim this node' silently meant 'give this node to the server'. Once the gate landed it meant 'denied for everyone except the server', a false denial of the tool's most ordinary call, on a production-reachable path with no test. It now defaults to viewer.principal(), which is a PROVABLE no-op on stdio (the stdio viewer resolves server.agent_id()) and makes the HTTP arm mean what the tool's own schema description - 'defaults to current agent' - always said. Found by the land-phase critics; pinned by write_gate_denies_at_the_tool.rs::assign_ownership_with_no_owner_id_claims_the_node_for_the_caller and verified by mutation probe 1.
behaviour_changes.3_encryptionprovider_and_orchestrationba: Both traits, both NoOp implementations, both AppState fields, both Shared* aliases and both with_* builders are deleted, along with the two epigraph-interfaces modules. Zero residual references anywhere in the tree. Any downstream that called with_encryption_provider or with_orchestration_backend will not compile. Plan lines :316-:317 prescribe exactly this.

done.locked_decisions: PR-11 DOES touch a locked decision, and it is the FIRST PR in this series to do so - every prior entry recorded '...its rejection trigger is not met'. D1 ('nothing is authorized by absence') was, until now, a statement about READS: access_control.rs's `None => ContentAccess::Full`. PR-11 extends it to WRITES at the type level: `Decision` has no Default and no From<bool>; `PolicyGate::authorize` maps every Err(_) to a denial once, inside epigraph-interfaces, so no call site can get the mapping wrong; and a `ResourceRef` that names no owner is refused rather than treated as unowned-therefore-writable. epigraph-db/tests/locked_decisions.rs carries a 'Status at PR-11' block and d1_the_kernel_write_gate_is_not_an_allow_all. NOTE the precision that block now states: that test asserts source strings about DenyAllPolicyGate, which has ZERO production install sites - the runtime default at every constructor is GroupPolicyGate, and the test that pins THAT is state.rs::the_default_gate_is_installed_at_every_constructor. D3 is untouched: no new Viewer constructor and no new SystemReason.

done.summary: Write-side tenancy stamping is armed in the database and the corpus is given an explicit declaration. Migration 070 installs four trigger arms — (a) supersede/evolve_step inheritance plus the undeclared-write counter, (b) the edge endpoint meet, (c) statement-level claim-derived inheritance on 17 tables, (d) statement-level propagation from claims to those 17 plus harvester_fragments and edges. Migration 071 demotes `ownership` to a write-through shim that transcribes partition_type into the tenancy columns and ledgers every write. `epigraph-tenancy-backfill` (a [[bin]] in epigraph-cli, named exactly as the plan and migration 066's header invoke it) stamps every pre-existing row ('public', author's personal group) in resumable batches and carries the `verify` subcommand whose exit code is the deploy pre-flight. A per-table `epigraph_tenancy_undeclared_writes` Prometheus gauge exports the week-11b gate's instrument. CommunityRepository's R7 projection drift is closed in all three directions.

plan_corrections.1_migration_numbers_are_070_071_not_066_: The plan's Files line says 066/067. Both are taken (066 = PR-04's idx_claims_world_owned, 067 = PR-04's session functions). migrations/README.md's post-shift table — self-declared authoritative — pins 070/071, and 067's own applied, checksum-frozen comment already names 'migration 070' as the file that creates these trigger bodies. Used 070/071.
plan_corrections.2_the_propagation_trigger_AS_SPECIFIED_C: Plan S3/066 specifies `AFTER UPDATE OF owner_group_id, visibility ... REFERENCING NEW TABLE AS changed`. PostgreSQL rejects it outright: 'ERROR: transition tables cannot be specified for triggers with column lists'. A column list and a transition table are mutually exclusive, so the migration would have ABORTED on the last statement of the file. Found by executing it. Replaced with `AFTER UPDATE ... REFERENCING OLD TABLE AS prev NEW TABLE AS changed` plus an OLD/NEW comparison as the function's FIRST statement, ahead of the epigraph_definer_bypass() assertion — which restores the intended firing condition and is strictly stricter (a column list fires on a write of the same value; this fires only on a real change). Putting the gate ahead of the assertion is load-bearing: without it every ordinary UPDATE of claims would 42501 on a deploy that had not re-owned the function.
plan_corrections.3_arm_c_ctid_predicate_is_a_SILENT_TAUTO: Plan S3/066 restricts arm (c)'s UPDATE with `AND t.ctid = ANY (SELECT ctid FROM newrows)`. A transition table HAS NO ctid — `SELECT n.ctid FROM newrows n` is a hard error. The plan's form is UNQUALIFIED, so the bare `ctid` resolves OUTWARD to `t.ctid` and the predicate degenerates to `t.ctid = ANY (SELECT t.ctid ...)`, a tautology over the WHOLE BASE TABLE. Measured with a counting probe: a 2-row insert into a 4-row table reported the predicate matching 4 rows; the preceding 2-row insert reported 2. It tracks table size, not the statement. So the plan's arm (c) re-stamps every row of the table on every insert — correct output, O(table) cost, on the highest-volume write path in the system, and invisible to any correctness test. Replaced with a `claim_id` join, the same key arm (d) uses. NOTE: an earlier probe of mine 'confirmed' the ctid form worked (3 of 3 rows matched) — a false positive caused by the base table having exactly 3 rows.
plan_corrections.4_arm_c_trigger_set_must_be_a_literal_ar: Plan S3/066 says 'one trigger per member of the generated set that carries claim_id'. 21 relations carry claim_id and a naive loop ABORTS the migration: alternative_set and alt_set_decisions are VIEWS (PostgreSQL rejects a statement-level AFTER INSERT trigger on a view), and claim_encryption / claim_version_encryption carry claim_id but have NO tenancy columns. The correct set is 062's tier_a INTERSECTED with has-claim_id = 17 tables, identical to arm (d)'s `derived` array.
plan_corrections.5_re_owning_the_functions_needs_a_GRANT_: Arm (d) refuses to run unless epigraph_definer_bypass() is true, and that function keys on CURRENT_USER, which inside a SECURITY DEFINER frame is the FUNCTION OWNER — so the bodies must be owned by epigraph_maintenance. Two things the plan does not say follow, both measured on a throwaway: (i) 067 did `REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM PUBLIC` on epigraph_definer_bypass(), so re-owning without `GRANT EXECUTE ... TO epigraph_maintenance` gives 'permission denied for function epigraph_definer_bypass' on the first batch; (ii) migration 060 says in its own words '(060 itself issues no GRANT.)' — epigraph_maintenance is a bare NOLOGIN role with NO table privileges, so a re-owned body cannot read or write anything, and the first thing to fail is arm (a) with 'permission denied for table tenancy_undeclared_writes'. 070 now issues both grants, guarded on role existence the way 067 guards its EXISTS.
plan_corrections.6_the_recon_is_wrong_about_the_seed_grou: /home/jeremy/pr12-scope-recon.md item 3 says 'Stamp the SEED group, not world'. That is wrong for PR-12's backfill and wrong in the dangerous direction. Seed is migration 074 arm 4's `epigraph_seed`-ROLE escape hatch for fixture inserts, and 074 is PR-16 — migration 062's own comment says 'Migration 074 arm 4 stamps THIS'. Plan D2 requires the AUTHOR'S PERSONAL GROUP. Stamping seed would still satisfy acceptance A4 literally (seed != world), so no acceptance query in the plan would have caught it, while leaving every claim owned by a group with zero group_memberships rows BY DESIGN — unreadable by its own author at PR-17. The recon's derived criterion (never leave world) survives; it just is not satisfied by stamping seed.

decisions.apply_070_BEFORE_running_the_backfill: The plan leaves 070/071 unplaced and puts the backfill at weeks 4-5, so the order is undetermined and it decides who propagates to the 17 derived tables. Decided: 070 FIRST. The backfill's own `UPDATE claims SET owner_group_id = ...` IS arm (d)'s firing event, so the derived tables, harvester_fragments and edges are stamped by the trigger in the same transaction and the backfill owes them no arm of its own. Had the backfill run first it would have owed its own propagation walk, and PR-12's 'each of the eight S2.4 tables inherits correctly' test would have been testing the backfill instead of the trigger it exists to pin. The binary REFUSES TO START if claims_propagate_tenancy is absent or disabled — running without it is a silent half-backfill that still reports every entity complete.
decisions.the_shim_MATERIALIZES_rather_than_refusi: An earlier revision RAISED when the owner had no personal group. That is the wrong trade and 26 test failures made it visible: refusing leaves the claim PUBLIC when the caller asked for private — failing OPEN dressed up as strictness. Minting the agent's own personal group is not a fallback to some other principal's group; it is the same idempotent act ensure_personal_group performs on the OAuth path, yielding a real group whose only live member is the owner. What remains forbidden is stamping world, stamping seed, or stamping any group the owner is not a live member of.
decisions.NEITHER_070_NOR_071_MAY_WIDEN: Both found by red tests, not by reasoning, and both are the single most important behavioural decision here. (i) The shim's 'public' arm DECLASSIFIED an already-group-private claim: structural_features_authz.rs stamps 'public' ownership rows over all three of its claims for bookkeeping, including the one seeded ('group', G), and a stranger saw 3 claims where it must see 2. (ii) Plan arm (b) is UNCONDITIONAL — no equivalent of arm (a)'s world-default gate — so an edge explicitly declared ('group', G) between two public endpoints was rewritten to ('public', world). Both now refuse to widen. Derivation for an UNDECLARED row is unchanged, so the plan's 'edges need no call-site edits' property survives intact. This anticipates PR-16's migration 074 claims_block_widening trigger; a compat shim for a table on its way out must not be able to disclose content.
decisions.the_community_arm_does_NOT_project_the_d: Tempting — it would guarantee the declaring agent can read back what it declared — and it would have silently overturned a reviewed decision. community_partition.rs::community_owner_who_is_not_a_member_is_redacted says in its own assertion: 'ownership alone does NOT grant access once a community resolves ... If you are changing this, change it on purpose.' The black-hole risk that made it tempting is handled instead by DECLINING to use a community group that nobody is in, and falling back to the owner's personal group (still 'group', still not public).
decisions.the_five_entities_the_plan_assigns_no_de: frames, contexts, perspectives, communities and recall_events are tier_a and seeded into tenancy_backfill_progress, but the plan gives them nothing. Decided from the columns: communities -> its own id (068's projection is ID-preserving); perspectives -> personal group of owner_agent_id; recall_events -> personal group of agent_id; frames and contexts have NO owner column of any kind and stay ('public', world). That last is legal and the constraint is narrow enough to name: the deferred strong `owner_group_id <> world` CHECK is scoped to CLAIMS (plan Q5), acceptance A4 counts claims only, and 062's _group_needs_real_group forbids only ('group', world). It also matches arm (b), which stamps ('public', world) for an edge between two public endpoints. NULL agent columns leave their rows world-owned for the same reason.
decisions.the_ledger_is_last_write_wins_and_that_i: tenancy_transcription_log is node_id uuid PRIMARY KEY, so a node reclassified twice keeps only the last transition. It cannot be fixed inside PR-12: adding a sequence changes the shape schema_contract.rs pins exactly and in order, and 072-084 are all allocated. It does NOT block the consumer — migration 080's pre-flight reads this table for the EXISTENCE of a row per non-public ownership row. History is lost, the gate is not. Pinned by a test so PR-18 does not rediscover it.
decisions.personal_groups_are_identified_TWO_ways: The canonical id is ensure_personal_group's deterministic 'did:epigraph:personal:<uuid>' key. But that is a convention; the semantics are kind='personal' created by this agent, and every copy of viewer_fixture.rs::seed_agent_with_group mints one as 'did:epigraph:test:<label>:<agent>'. Matching only the did_key would have made the shim raise on groups that plainly exist, and would have made the backfill mint SECOND personal groups. Both the shim and the binary resolve on `did_key OR (kind='personal' AND created_by_agent_id)`, canonical key first.
decisions.epigraph_maintenance_gains_schema_wide_S: DEPLOY-VISIBLE PRIVILEGE CHANGE, called out here because a reviewer scanning for 'what does this PR change about who can read what' would otherwise find it only in a migration comment. Migration 070 issues `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO epigraph_maintenance` (plus USAGE on the schema and sequences, and EXECUTE on epigraph_definer_bypass()). It is REQUIRED, not convenient: migration 060 creates the role with no privileges at all ('060 itself issues no GRANT.'), and the trigger bodies must be OWNED by it for epigraph_definer_bypass() to be true — so without the grant a re-owned body cannot read or write anything and arm (a) fails immediately with 'permission denied for table tenancy_undeclared_writes'. DELETE and TRUNCATE are deliberately NOT granted: the tenancy maintenance role stamps and reads, never destroys. The role is NOLOGIN and is already the designated RLS bypass at PR-17, so this widens what an existing escape hatch can do rather than creating a new one. Guarded on role existence, so a managed Postgres without the role is a no-op rather than a failed migration. NOTE for a later migration: `ON ALL TABLES` binds the tables existing at 070's run time — a migration that adds a tier-A table must re-issue it.

unlisted_work.materializing_personal_groups_for_orphan: The single largest item the Files line does not mention. D2 derives every claim's owner from claims.agent_id, but a personal group is only ever created by ensure_personal_group, called from the OAuth mint path and the MCP server's agent resolution. Migration 057 documents ~1,198 one-shot orphan agents that have never authenticated. Phase 0 of `run` materializes them in bulk before the first batch.
unlisted_work.harvester_fragments_insert_order_hole: Arm (c) cannot cover it (no claim_id) and arm (d) fires only on a claims UPDATE, so a fragment inserted BEFORE its harvester_claim_provenance row is stamped by no trigger. The backfill closes it for existing rows with an explicit provenance-join arm. NEW rows in that order remain a live gap — see open findings.
unlisted_work.the_gauge_needs_a_sampler_task_not_a_Col:
prometheus_client::collector::Collector::encode is SYNCHRONOUS and cannot await an sqlx query, so a custom Collector is not an option and the value must be pushed. The Family<TenancyTableLabel, Gauge> sits on Metrics UNCONDITIONALLY (pure prometheus_client, nameable under --no-default-features) and only the sampler task is #[cfg(feature = "db")] — exactly the asymmetry the no-db gate exists to catch. The SQL is a repo function with NO Viewer parameter: tenancy_undeclared_writes carries no content and no owner_group_id, so it is not a read that ignores a viewer and needs no -- VISIBILITY-EXEMPT: marker (adding an unnecessary one would redden visibility_lint.rs's exact EXPECTED_EXEMPTIONS set). /metrics stays off both app routers.

VERIFIED BEHAVIOURALLY, not just by `cargo build`. The full server binary could not be booted in this environment (it requires EPIGRAPH_JWT_SECRET, a providers.toml and OAuth provider credentials), so the sampler's exact composition — repo read -> Family::get_or_create -> .set() -> registry encode — is driven against real rows by the NEW crates/epigraph-api/tests/tenancy_gauge.rs (3 tests). It asserts that an undeclared write made through migration 070 arm (a) reaches the scrape as `epigraph_tenancy_undeclared_writes{table_name="claims"} 1`, that it is exported as a GAUGE, that it follows the table DOWN to zero (the property the 24-hour flat-at-zero gate depends on, and why it is not a Counter), and that a historical row is not exported. Not covered: the tokio::spawn + interval wrapper in bin/server.rs, which carries no logic beyond the loop.

One finding from writing it: a registered `Family` ALWAYS emits its `# HELP` / `# TYPE` header even when it holds no series, so 'does the scrape mention the metric name' cannot distinguish 'no undeclared writes' from 'the sampler never ran'. The tests count LABELLED SERIES lines instead.

behaviour_changes.redaction_becomes_UNREACHABLE_on_the_tra: The headline consequence, and it discharges Q6's gate. Before PR-12, `seed_private_ownership` wrote an ACL row that only check_content_access consulted while every claim stayed visibility='public', so a stranger got 200 with content '[REDACTED]'. Migration 071 transcribes that row into the tenancy columns, so the Viewer predicate now excludes the row and it is ABSENT, not blanked. That is STRICTLY LESS DISCLOSURE — a stranger no longer learns the claim exists — and it is the end state plan PR-14 formalises ('delete redaction; a non-visible row is absent, not blanked'). The `REDACTED` constant is now dead in BOTH epigraph-mcp/tests/community_partition.rs and read_path_redaction.rs and was deleted from each with a comment saying why. PR-12 does NOT delete check_content_access — PR-14 owns removal; PR-12 makes its remaining branches unreachable, which is exactly what Q6's `gated_on: PR-12 transcription completing` asked for.
behaviour_changes.an_edge_touching_a_private_claim_is_now_: Arm (b)'s meet. structural_features_authz.rs's two SUPPORTS edges touch a group-private claim and are now group-private, so a stranger sees neither where before it saw each at its one visible endpoint. Correct, not incidental: an edge ATTESTS THAT ITS ENDPOINT EXISTS and stands in a named relationship to a public one — a structural leak no content-redaction test would ever notice.
behaviour_changes.POST_ownership_and_MCP_assign_ownership_: Writing an ownership row now changes claims.visibility / owner_group_id and cascades to 17 derived tables plus edges via arm (d). Before, it wrote an ACL row with no effect on claims. Both writers are deleted by PR-14, but they ship with this side effect for one release.
behaviour_changes.test_fixtures_must_resolve_a_Viewer_for_: Several MCP/API tests built ONE empty-group `public_viewer` and passed the acting agent separately as the `requester` wire parameter — faithful before PR-12, because the Viewer predicate matched every row. It no longer is: an empty-group viewer cannot see a private claim AT ALL, not even as its OWNER. In production Viewer::resolve runs on the authenticated agent, so viewer and requester are the same principal; the fixtures now do the same and therefore exercise the real composition (Viewer filter, THEN redaction).
