done.theme_cluster_carry_over: FIXED WITH A HOLDING GATE, AND THE OLD SAFETY ARGUMENT WAS WRONG. The previous entry said 'PROCEEDING IS SAFE - the argument is that PR-12 does not increase the exposure'. That is FALSE in the direction that matters. Before PR-12, `ownership` writes landed in a table no read path consulted, so the corpus was uniformly public and `run_theme_kmeans`'s INPUT contained no private content - the leak was real but EMPTY. Migration 071 changes that on its first firing: every ownership write now transcribes into claims.owner_group_id / visibility and 070 propagates it, so from this PR onward the kmeans job's input includes group-private claim content while its output (claim_themes.centroid / .centroid_3072) has no owner_group_id, no visibility, is not in 062's tier_a, gets no arm (c) trigger and is not covered by `verify`. A centroid is a mean of its members' embeddings, and viewer_route_table_lint.rs already treats claims.embedding as approximately invertible to content, so a nearest-neighbour probe against a published centroid is an information channel about the private text - not noise. THE FIX: `AND visibility = 'public'` on the corpus read inside run_theme_kmeans itself. Fail-closed, costs nothing while the corpus is still overwhelmingly public, needs no Viewer (which matters because the scheduled epigraph-jobs rebuild has no principal to supply one), and lands ALL THREE callers together by construction, so it cannot cause the MCP/HTTP parity break plan S8.4 #16 exists to catch. WHAT REMAINS: this is a holding gate, not the control. D-PR16-theme-cluster-viewer-scope stays open and stays PR-16's, with the both-callers-together constraint intact. The two structural corrections from the implement phase stand and are worth keeping: claim_theme_members does not exist, and run_theme_kmeans has THREE callers - the omitted one, epigraph-jobs' scheduled rebuild, being the one the hazard actually names.
done.uncompensated_inline_reads_triage: F-inline-claim-content-reads carries a `deadline: PR-12` for the UNCOMPENSATED set — 13 statements across 8 files under routes/ with no check_content_access anywhere. DISPOSITION: triaged, NOT fixed, and the register is unchanged (viewer_route_table_lint.rs's exact counts still pass). The reason they were called live-exposure-on- PR-12 is that the backfill would write the first visibility='group' row; it does not — D2 makes every row the backfill touches explicitly 'public'. The rows that DO become group-visible come from the 071 shim, i.e. only for nodes an operator or test explicitly marked private, and S9.1 asserts prod has none. So these reads are not live-exposed BY PR-12. They must still close before PR-14 deletes their compensating control, and before PR-18 privatizes at scale. Left open with this reasoning rather than silently absorbed.

land_phase_fixes.context: 28 critic findings (18 blocker/major) were raised against the implement-phase tree. Everything below was FIXED in the land phase and is covered by a new or amended test unless the entry says otherwise.
land_phase_fixes.B1_071_shim_blocked_widening_but_not_TRA:
The shim's only guard was `NOT (visibility='group' AND v='public')`, so group -> DIFFERENT-group was open. Composition, every link verified: (1) require_declassify_authority resolves `(None, Some(requested)) if requested == principal.id()` to ALLOW, so an ownerless node may be self-claimed (PR-11's F-PR11-assign-ownership-self-claim-is-a-seizure, filed as a DoS because the row landed in an ACL table nothing read); (2) 071 makes that write land on the LIVE tenancy columns; (3) PR-12 MANUFACTURES the victims - supersede writes no ownership row so arm (a) stamps the successor ('group', G) with owner_of_record = None, and no production path ever gives `evidence` an ownership row while arm (c) stamps it from its parent and evidence.raw_content is a full second copy of the claim text; (4) node_type is caller-supplied and unvalidated, ownership.node_id has no FK, and MCP assign_ownership is gated at claims:write not claims:admin. FIX: every one of the six UPDATE arms now also carries `AND NOT (visibility='group' AND owner_group_id IS DISTINCT FROM g AND NOT EXISTS (<the declarer holds a live group_memberships row in the node's CURRENT owner_group_id>))`. The membership escape hatch is REQUIRED, not a softening: a bare no-transfer rule would forbid the legitimate private -> community re-declaration 071's own header describes and two fixtures perform. Pinned by tenancy_triggers.rs::the_shim_refuses_to_transfer_a_private_node_into_a_strangers_group (claim AND evidence) and ::a_live_member_of_the_current_group_may_still_re_declare. This DOWNGRADES PR-11's residual from a confidentiality break back to the DoS it was filed as; it does NOT close it (self-claiming an ownerless PUBLIC node still works, still PR-14's).

THE GUARD NEEDED A SECOND ESCAPE HATCH, AND A RED TEST FOUND IT. The first revision allowed a transfer only when the declarer was a live member of the node's CURRENT group. `community_partition.rs::demoting_out_of_community_clears_the_gate` went red: the OWNER demoting its own claim from `community` to `private` must move it from the community group to its personal group, and the owner is deliberately NOT projected into the community group (test 7 pins that as a reviewed decision). Blocking it left the demoted node readable by every member of the community it had just left — a WIDENING dressed as strictness, i.e. the exact failure mode the guard exists against. Second hatch: `may_transfer := (TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND OLD.owner_id = NEW.owner_id)` — the owner of record re-declaring its own row. The attack stays closed because it is an INSERT: `require_declassify_authority` permits a self-claim ONLY when there is no owner of record, so an attacker's write can never be an UPDATE preserving owner_id; and with an owner of record present, that same function denies (Some(victim), Some(attacker)) before the trigger runs. Pinned by `the_owner_of_record_may_move_its_own_node_between_groups`.
land_phase_fixes.B2_arm_d_edges_copied_one_endpoint_inste: `UPDATE edges SET (owner_group_id, visibility) = (ch.owner_group_id, ch.visibility) FROM changed ch` never read the other endpoint, while its own comment said 'Edges are the MEET of their (possibly changed) endpoints'. Measured twice on the throwaway in rolled-back transactions: (1) declassifying ONE endpoint rewrote the edge to ('public', world) while the other stayed group-private - a public edge attesting a private claim exists and stands in a named relationship, which is exactly the leak arm (b) exists to close and which this same PR asserts on the INSERT side; (2) one statement privatizing two claims into DIFFERENT personal groups made the edge take whichever join row Postgres matched first. FIX: the arm now recomputes the meet through `epigraph_node_tenancy` on BOTH endpoints via CROSS JOIN LATERAL, carries arm (b)'s no-widening guard, and LEAVES A CROSS-GROUP EDGE UNCHANGED rather than raising - arm (d) fires on every claims UPDATE including the backfill's own, so an exception there is a total write outage, and stale-but-still-private is fail-closed. `edges` is the only two-parent relation, which is why the 17 derived tables and harvester_fragments can legitimately copy their single parent. Pinned by tenancy_triggers.rs::arm_d_recomputes_the_meet_rather_than_copying_the_changed_endpoint and ::arm_d_leaves_a_cross_group_edge_unchanged_rather_than_picking_a_side. This also subsumes the minor 'edges left ('public', <arbitrary personal group>) after the backfill': two public endpoints now meet at ('public', world). SUPERSEDED BY PR-13: migration 072 replaces "LEAVES A CROSS-GROUP EDGE UNCHANGED" with the three-CASE co-ownership meet, and the test named above was renamed to ::arm_d_co_owns_a_cross_group_edge_rather_than_picking_a_side. The "must not RAISE" half of that test is unchanged and still load-bearing for the reason stated here.
land_phase_fixes.B3_the_definer_ownership_control_could_s: 070/071 wrap their `ALTER FUNCTION ... OWNER TO epigraph_maintenance` in `IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles ...)`, and migration 060 creates that role inside a DO block that catches insufficient_privilege and only RAISE NOTICEs - so on a managed cluster the migrations apply SUCCESSFULLY with the control absent. Two opposite silent failures: 070's bodies become RLS-filtered at PR-17 and arm (b) then stamps a private endpoint PUBLIC (a leak, not an error, as 070's own comment says), while 071's shim raises 42501 on every ownership write (a total outage). FIX: `verify` now hard-fails if any of the six SECURITY DEFINER bodies is missing or not owned by epigraph_maintenance, naming the function and the required owner. Kept OUT of the migration deliberately: a failed migration records no row, so a hard failure there turns a missing role into a permanent restart loop. Pinned by backfill_idempotence.rs::verify_fails_when_a_definer_body_is_not_maintenance_owned, which re-owns the oracle to epigraph_app and asserts exit 1.
land_phase_fixes.B5_pre_existing_ownership_rows_were_neve: 071 installs only `AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE`, and neither migration nor binary performed a one-time pass - yet `verify` counts exactly those rows in two checks ('map to a still-public claim', 'have no transcription log row'), so on any database holding ownership rows before 071 the deploy gate was UNCLEARABLE and `run` (which calls verify) exited 1 forever. The acceptance line 'every ownership row it transcribes writes a tenancy_transcription_log row' was true only vacuously. The test suite was structurally blind: every fixture inserted AFTER the migration, so the trigger fired. FIX: `transcribe_legacy_ownership` re-fires the trigger (`UPDATE ownership SET owner_id = owner_id`) over every row with no ledger entry, batched and cursored, with a per-row retry so one 23514 does not kill the walk. Pinned by backfill_idempotence.rs::a_legacy_ownership_row_is_transcribed_and_clears_verify, which DISABLES the trigger for one INSERT to reproduce the legacy shape, asserts verify=1 before and 0 after, and asserts a second run is a no-op.
land_phase_fixes.B6_the_gauge_could_never_go_back_down: The sampler called get_or_create(..).set(n) only for rows the query RETURNED and never reset the family. `undeclared_writes_today` filters `day = current_date` and arm (a) creates a new (table_name, day) row per day, so the day after an undeclared write the query returns nothing for that table and the long-lived process keeps yesterday's value forever - the exact failure the current_date filter was written to prevent, reintroduced one layer up. The gauge became a function of process uptime: stuck high means the week-11b gate can never pass, and an API restart makes the same corpus read clean. All three existing tests built a FRESH Metrics, so none could observe it. FIX: the loop body was lifted out of tokio::spawn into `epigraph_api::tenancy_gauge::TenancyGaugeSampler`, which remembers every table it has exported and explicitly .set(0) on any absent from the current pass. It does NOT invent zeros for tier-A tables it has never seen (arm (a)'s trigger exists only on `claims`; 074 widens it), which would assert a coverage this release does not have. The module is #[cfg(feature="db")] while Metrics::tenancy_undeclared_writes stays uncfg'd, so the no-db build is unaffected. Two new tests, both sampling TWICE against the SAME Metrics.
land_phase_fixes.B7_the_content_hash_confirmation_oracle_: PARTIALLY REJECTED, THEN FIXED. The critic said the guard is now 'unguarded'; that overstates it - `epigraph-mcp/src/tools/redaction.rs::redact_content_blanks_hash_in_lockstep_with_content` is a live unit test on the helper all eight call sites go through, and it asserts exactly the lockstep. What WAS genuinely lost is any INTEGRATION-level assertion on a handler that reaches the branch. FIX: get_claim.rs::get_claim_blanks_the_content_hash_when_it_redacts constructs the still-live blanking path - the LEGACY shape, an ownership row written with the 071 trigger disabled, so the tenancy columns stay public and the Viewer admits the row while check_content_access says Redacted - and asserts content == [REDACTED] AND content_hash == "". Its precondition assertion fails loudly if the shape ever becomes an absence case, so it cannot silently become vacuous. The four stale doc comments the critic listed (get_claim.rs, query_claims_by_label.rs, read_path_redaction.rs, query_claims_redaction.rs) were all corrected to describe absence rather than blanking.
land_phase_fixes.B10_the_strangers_edge_map_became_all_ne: After arm (b)'s meet made both SUPPORTS edges group-private, every assertion about `sedges` in structural_features_authz.rs::owner_sees_the_whole_subgraph_and_a_stranger_only_its_public_part was `!contains_key(..)`, so an edge_counts statement returning {} for every principal would have passed. FIX: a fourth edge (CITES, pub_a -> pub_b, both endpoints public) whose meet leaves it ('public', world), with `sedges.get("CITES") == Some(&2)` restoring a positive. Deliberately a new relationship between the EXISTING pair, so no node count moves: degree_stats.total_nodes, temporal_bins and belief_stats are untouched and the stranger's clustering_stats.eligible_nodes stays 0 (one public edge still leaves both visible nodes at degree 1).
land_phase_fixes.B12_PR12_moved_the_self_service_communit: F-PR11-community-membership-is-self-service was deferred by PR-11 to 'the PR that owns community authorization'. PR-12's projection is what makes it load-bearing: the membership becomes a live group_memberships row and Viewer::resolve pushes every live membership into group_ids regardless of role, so it survives PR-14 (which deletes check_content_access) and is armed by PR-17. GATING ONLY THE PROJECTION WOULD NOT HAVE CLOSED IT - 071's shim replays the projection out of community_members on every community-partitioned ownership write, so the community_members row itself is the grant; the authorization therefore sits on the whole operation. FIX: CLOSED MEMBERSHIP in the repo layer - if the community's projected group has any live membership the acting agent must hold one too; if it has none the operation is allowed (bootstrap, because 068 left every projected group with ZERO administrators by design and refusing would be a permanent dead end, not a control); remove_member additionally always permits removing your own perspective. add_member/remove_member/create take `Option<Uuid> acting_agent` and return a MembershipOutcome the route maps to 403/404. `remove_member`'s handler, which previously extracted NOTHING, now takes a ViewerExtractor; `create_community` does too and passes the creator, so a community created through the route is never in the bootstrap state. Deliberately weaker than 'only an admin may add members' - community groups have no admins to require. Five new tests in community_projection.rs. Route-level authorization proper is still PR-16's, and community.rs appears in NEITHER of viewer_route_table_lint.rs's registers, so nothing was ratcheted.
land_phase_fixes.B14_the_eight_table_inheritance_test_was: Its end-to-end leg was `sqlx::query("INSERT INTO claim_clusters (id, claim_id, cluster_label) ...").execute().await.ok()` followed by `assert count(*) WHERE owner_group_id <> group == 0` - trivially true when no row exists, and no row DID exist: `claim_clusters` has no `cluster_label` column, so the INSERT failed silently on every run and the catalog loop was the whole test. FIX: all EIGHT tables are now inserted for real, every INSERT is .expect()ed, and each table's row is asserted to EXIST (count == 1) before its tenancy is asserted, so a schema drift fails the test instead of vacuously passing it. Writing it exposed four real schema facts the old form had hidden: graph_neighborhoods.run_id FKs to graph_cluster_runs and .theme_id to claim_themes; reasoning_type is a CHECK'd enum ('deductive', not 'deduction'); claim_signature_revocations CHECKs octet_length(previous_signature)=64 and (previous_content_hash)=32.
land_phase_fixes.B15_the_community_module_doc_asserted_so: It said 071's shim 'resolves a community partition to groups WHERE id = community_id AND kind = community and RAISES if it is absent'. 071 does neither: it INSERTs the group on demand, replays 068's membership projection, and falls through to the owner's personal group when no live membership results - which two tests IN THIS PR already pin. The same false claim was in HANDOFF.md. Both rewritten to 071's actual behaviour, and the `create` projection re-justified on its real grounds (a standing invariant tenancy_coverage.rs structurally cannot observe, because it replays 068 before asserting).
land_phase_fixes.B16_README_said_applied: migrations/README.md annotated 070/071 '**applied 2026-09-03**' when they had only ever touched the throwaway. That table is what the next PR's agent reads to decide whether a file is frozen, and this PR's own gate notes record a live VersionMismatch(71) from editing a file the throwaway had recorded - so the annotation was exactly the evidence a later agent would cite to refuse a still-needed edit. Rewritten to 'drafted PR-12; validated on a throwaway DB only, NOT applied to any deployed database'.
land_phase_fixes.B17_the_claims_cursor_stepped_over_rows_: The batch UPDATE is guarded by `personal_group(agent_id) IS NOT NULL`, but the cursor advanced to the last id SELECTED. claims.agent_id has NO foreign key to agents (plan S9.1 records that routes/claims.rs trusts a caller-supplied request.agent_id), so dangling authors are expected in production and phase 0 - which joins agents - cannot fix them. A re-run then found nothing past the stale cursor, broke on batch 1, and exited 1 again: 'resumable' and 'every entity reaches complete' were unreachable with no documented remedy. FIX: backfill_claims re-measures the residual after its walk and RESETS last_id to NULL when anything is left, logging the remedy; docs/tenancy.md gains a 'When the backfill leaves rows behind' section with the manual rewind. ALSO corrected: verify's comment claimed 'A4: the derivation is total, because claims.agent_id is NOT NULL' - NOT NULL does not imply RESOLVABLE without an FK, and that was the stated rationale for the headline acceptance criterion.
land_phase_fixes.B18_phase_0_re_promoted_every_claim_auth: The membership INSERT selected every agent that has ever authored a claim with `DO UPDATE SET revoked_at = NULL, role = 'admin'`, so a deliberately revoked or demoted personal-group membership was silently restored to live admin - and whether it ran at all depended on the `missing == 0` early return, i.e. on unrelated state. FIX: scoped by `NOT EXISTS (<a live membership>)` to the set the phase is actually for, `role` dropped from the DO UPDATE so an existing demotion survives, and the early-return gate widened to measure BOTH conditions it guards. Reviving a MISSING live membership is kept - that is ensure_personal_group's documented semantics and the reason its ON CONFLICT targets the composite.
minors_fixed: Arm (c) has no no-widening gate and the surrounding comments assert the opposite principle three times: documented as INTENTIONAL (a derived row has no independent tenancy; a derived row stricter than its parent is a row nobody can read attached to a claim everybody can) and pinned by the now-real eight-table test, so PR-16 cannot come to rely on the opposite by accident.

The module doc's `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` concurrency claim ('two operators divide the work') was FALSE - both share one last_id and the cursor advances to the last id returned. Corrected in the binary and in docs/tenancy.md to 'single-operator'.
`rows_done` reset to 0 on resume (now seeded from the persisted value) and settle_remaining stored whole-table `count(*)` (now count(*) - residual, i.e. rows DECLARED).

verify's blanket `edges` exemption removed and replaced with the sharper predicate it was hiding: a world-owned edge is legitimate only when BOTH endpoints are public, written against claims/evidence directly rather than through epigraph_node_tenancy (which carries REVOKE EXECUTE FROM PUBLIC, so verify must not depend on being its owner).

Arm (b)'s cross-group RAISE now carries ERRCODE 23514 instead of plpgsql's P0001 default, so the API/MCP layer can map it to a 4xx rather than a bare 500. The mapping itself is PR-13's, alongside 072.
Stale `migrations/066` references in the binary and in backfill_idempotence.rs corrected to 070.

Stated-vs-actual: the implement phase's summary said 071 leaves `frames`/`contexts` at ('public', world). It does not - `g` is resolved to the owner's personal group BEFORE the frame/context arms run, so the shim writes ('public', <owner's personal group>). Not a leak (visibility is what the read predicate binds to, and the strong owner_group_id <> world CHECK is claims-scoped per plan Q5), but recorded because this series' whole method is recording these. The BACKFILL's own arms do leave frames/contexts world-owned; only the shim path differs.
land_phase_fixes.B11_the_cross_group_edge_RAISE_is_docume: Arm (b)'s cross-group branch is effectively unconditional: for PERSONAL groups one principal can never be a live member of two distinct ones, so `sg = ANY(session_groups) AND tg = ANY(session_groups)` is unsatisfiable and the satisfiable case (sg = tg) was already taken above. It is NOT reachable from the backfill's own output (backfill_claims writes visibility='public', so arm (b) takes the both-public branch - verified by probe); it becomes reachable once 071's transcription makes two claims with different owners genuinely ('group', G), at which point any cross-owner link_epistemic / link_hierarchical / decomposition edge hard-fails. PR-13's migration 072 closes the window. Shipping the RAISE first is the fail-CLOSED order - silently picking one side leaks the other. Documented at length in the migration; ERRCODE added; no behaviour change.

done.summary: The endpoint meet becomes EXPRESSIBLE. `edges.owner_group_id` is a single uuid and cannot name two owning groups, so migration 070 resolved a cross-group edge by RAISING on write (arm b) and by leaving the row unchanged on privatization (arm d). 071's transcription made the first of those reachable — every cross-owner link_epistemic / link_hierarchical / decomposition write would hard-fail. Migration 072 adds `edges.co_owner_group_id` (+ `edges_co_owner_fkey` and `edges_co_owner_shape`, both NOT VALID) and CREATE OR REPLACEs both 070 arms: arm (b)'s RAISE becomes a co-ownership stamp, arm (d) gains the three-CASE meet. 073 is the partial index, `-- no-transaction`, one CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY. On the read side `Viewer::edge_predicate_fragment` is an INTERSECTION — a co-owned edge is visible only to a principal in BOTH groups — spliced through a new `/* {EDGE_VISIBILITY:<alias>} */` marker, because the alias is a text substitution and not a dispatch key (`e` is `edges` in structural.rs and `evidence` in evidence.rs). 23514 is finally classified: `DbError::CheckViolation` -> HTTP 400.
done.read_path_conversion_counts: MEASURED ONCE, with an explicit definition, because three different numbers reached the review (75/60/65 sites, 20/17 files). DEFINITION: a 'marker token' is one `/* {EDGE_VISIBILITY:<alias>} */` occurrence on a NON-COMMENT line. By that definition: **62 marker tokens across 17 repo files**, plus **15 static `sqlx::query!` / `query_as!` transcriptions across 4 files** (edge.rs 8, paper.rs 4, claim.rs 2, provenance_chain.rs 1) — **19 repo files touched in total**. The 15 static transcriptions are exactly the 15 deleted + 15 added `.sqlx/` files. Counting marker OPENINGS instead gives 67; the extra 5 are prose in doc comments (`{EDGE_VISIBILITY:...}` / `{EDGE_VISIBILITY:<alias>}` placeholders in the module docs of alternative_set.rs, semantic_link.rs, structural.rs and evidence.rs). Several statements carry two or three edge markers (aliases e1/e2/e3 in structural.rs::clustering_coefficients, orig/amp in political.rs::amplification), which is why 'sites' meaning STATEMENTS is a smaller number than 'sites' meaning TOKENS. Tokens is the number used here and in the PR body.
plan_corrections: MIGRATION NUMBERS. Plan §3 calls this file 068 and §3.1 calls it '069 (planned 068)'. Both are pre-shift text. migrations/README.md is authoritative and pins 072 (transactional) + 073 (-- no-transaction, index only). Confirmed against the reservation table; `git status --short migrations/` shows exactly two new files.

WHICH FILE HOLDS THE ARMS. The plan's *Files* line says CREATE OR REPLACE '066(b) and 066(d)'; §3.1 says '067(b)/(d)'. Both wrong in this tree: 066 is PR-04's idx_claims_world_owned and 067 is the session functions. BOTH arms live in migrations/070_tenancy_triggers.sql. Replacing anything in 066 would have left the live triggers untouched.

THE PLAN'S PRINTED ARM (b) BODY DROPS PR-12'S NO-WIDENING GUARD. It begins straight at `IF sv = 'public' AND tv = 'public'`, which makes the meet unconditional and silently rewrites an edge explicitly declared ('group', G) between two PUBLIC endpoints to ('public', world). PR-12 MEASURED that regression (structural_features_authz.rs: the stranger saw 2 edges where it must see 1). The guard is kept verbatim from 070.

ARM (d) IS A PROSE STUB IN THE PLAN ('identical to 066(d) except the final edges UPDATE'), so there is no SQL to copy and both of 070's guards were easy to lose. Kept: the no-widening `AND NOT (e.visibility = 'group' AND m.v = 'public')` and the `m.g IS NOT NULL` guard.

'THE edges_tenancy POLICY CLAUSE PRE-STAGED FOR 073' IS A NUMBER COLLISION. README pins 073 as the index-only no-transaction file and 077 as PR-17's RLS policies. Read literally the plan would put a CREATE POLICY in the index migration. Neither 072 nor 073 creates a policy; the clause 077 must carry is written out as a comment in 072's header so PR-17 cannot re-derive a non-matching one.
'tests/privatization_boundary.rs' IS A NEW FILE, not an extension of an existing one.

NO `ORDER BY e.id` IN THE TRIGGER. Plan §6.5's `ORDER BY e.id -- ops F12: fixed lock order` belongs to `repos/privatization.rs::seal_boundary_edges`, a batched resumable multi-batch UPDATE where lock order across batches is real. Arm (d) is a single statement-level trigger already scoped to `changed`, and an ORDER BY inside a subquery of UPDATE ... FROM does not establish lock acquisition order in PostgreSQL.

`co_owner_group_id` ALREADY APPEARED IN NINE FILES at the base commit while the column did NOT exist (information_schema returned 0). Every occurrence was a PR-12 forward-declaration, not existing work.

THE SENTINEL ASYMMETRY IS DELIBERATE. `edges_co_owner_shape` permits the world/dead sentinels where 062's `edges_group_needs_real_group` excludes them for owner_group_id, because this CHECK sits on arm (d)'s path — a statement-level AFTER UPDATE on `claims` that fires on EVERY claims UPDATE — so a violation raised from it is a TOTAL WRITE OUTAGE, not a rejected row.
decisions: READ SEMANTICS ARE AN INTERSECTION, NOT A UNION. A union would defeat the column's purpose: the edge exists so that privatizing into two groups neither loses data nor discloses to G an edge naming H's claim. Membership in G alone must not be enough.

MAPPED 23514 ONTO THE EXISTING `ApiError::BadRequest` rather than adding a variant. `ApiError` is compiled without the `db` feature while `impl From<DbError> for ApiError` is `#[cfg(feature = "db")]`, so a new variant would land in the no-db build with no arm constructing it.

REMOVED ARM (b)'s SESSION-MEMBERSHIP HATCH along with the RAISE it guarded. This is a locked-decisions CLEARANCE, not a violation: locked_decisions.rs forbids ADDING write-side predicates, and this REMOVES one. It never fired (070's own comment records that personal groups make the conjunction unsatisfiable, and every production edge writer reaches the trigger on a bare &PgPool where epigraph_session_groups() is empty), and the acceptance criterion is unreachable with a membership-gated RAISE in front of it. Pinned by tenancy_triggers.rs::arm_b_no_longer_raises_on_a_cross_group_edge.

NO BULK RECONCILIATION INSIDE 072 — see D-PR18-stale-cross-group-edges. 072 holds ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on `edges` for its ADD COLUMN and `SET LOCAL lock_timeout` bounds ACQUISITION, not hold; `edges_co_owner_shape` is enforced on new writes despite shipping NOT VALID, so a bad CASE would raise 23514 mid-migration, record no sqlx row and re-run on every restart; and plan §6.5 already assigns this exact meet to `repos/privatization.rs::seal_boundary_edges`, a BATCHED, RESUMABLE function scoped to `batch_ids`. It became a `verify` pre-flight gate instead.

A cross-group privatization now CO-OWNS the edge instead of leaving it stale. tenancy_triggers.rs::arm_d_leaves_a_cross_group_edge_unchanged_rather_than_picking_a_side was CONVERTED (not deleted) into arm_d_co_owns_a_cross_group_edge_rather_than_picking_a_side: its assertion inverted from (WORLD, 'public') to (group_a, 'group', Some(group_b)) because 072 changes the behaviour it pinned. A CHECK violation is HTTP 400, not 500, on every route. Previously 23514 fell through to QueryFailed -> ApiError::DatabaseError.

`DbError::CheckViolation` now carries the driver's `message` in Display. This matters most on MCP, whose errors.rs::internal_error renders DbError with to_string(): migration 071's memberless-group RAISE reports NO constraint name, so without the message an operator calling assign_ownership would see `Check constraint <unnamed> violated` and nothing else.

done.migration_state_on_the_throwaway: CORRECTING A CLAIM THE IMPLEMENT PHASE MADE. The report told the Land agent that 072/073 were applied via psql, so `_sqlx_migrations` held NO row for them and there was NO checksum that could mismatch if Land edited them. That is FALSE, and it was measured: `SELECT version, description, checksum IS NOT NULL FROM _sqlx_migrations WHERE version IN (70,71,72,73)` against epigraph_tenancy_pr13_test returns four rows, including `72 | edge co ownership | t` and `73 | idx edges co owner | t`. The verifier's `cargo sqlx migrate info` reporting every version `installed` with zero mismatch lines is only consistent with rows existing. Editing either file therefore requires re-migrating a fresh throwaway (or deleting those two rows) — it is NOT free. The land phase edited NEITHER migration file, precisely so the throwaway's checksums stay matching and the verifier's byte-verified .sqlx state is preserved. Throwaway head = 91; edges.co_owner_group_id exists.

findings_rejected: REJECTED THE PREFERRED FIX FOR THE STALE-EDGE FINDING (not the finding itself, which is real and is now gated). The critic's preferred fix was 'add the one-time reconciliation UPDATE to 072, copying plan §6.5's three CASE expressions'. Read in full, §6.5's block is headed `-- repos/privatization.rs :: seal_boundary_edges(tx, plan_id, batch_ids, target_group)` — it is a BATCHED, RESUMABLE application function scoped to `batch_ids`, which the plan assigns to the privatization work, not to a migration. Copying it into 072 would contradict the plan's own assignment and add three hazards 072 currently has none of: an unbounded ACCESS EXCLUSIVE hold on `edges` (lock_timeout bounds acquisition, not hold), a 23514 outage mode in a file whose own header argues that a failed migration records no sqlx row and becomes a permanent deploy outage, and expensive whole-table work that locked_decisions.rs keeps out of these files. The critic's own stated 'minimum acceptable alternative' — the verify predicate, the recorded obligation and the documented remediation — is what shipped, plus a behavioural test the critic did not ask for.
what_the_fail_open_review_cleared: The new fragment is strictly NARROWER than the old one in every rendering context, including the three that could have inverted: political.rs::claim_genealogy and ::amplification place the edge marker in LEFT JOIN ON clauses and claim.rs::count_all_evidence_for_claim does the same for `ed` — all three return FEWER rows under a narrower predicate, never more.
alternative_set.rs's `existing` LEFT JOIN is the one place where ADDING a filter would itself be the fail-open (it is a suppression join). It is correctly left unfiltered, with a written reason.

Multi-alias statements are fully converted, not partially: structural.rs::clustering_coefficients (e, e1, e2, e3), political.rs::amplification (orig, amp), alternative_set.rs (s1, s2, contr) and sheaf.rs (both statements) got the edge spelling on EVERY edges alias, with sibling `claims` aliases correctly left on the plain fragment.
No caller-facing read was newly annotated VISIBILITY-EXEMPT: EXPECTED_EXEMPTIONS is byte-identical in the diff, and the three `edges` exemptions are write-internal dedup/migration probes.

No error branch falls back to public. 23514 -> CheckViolation -> BadRequest is a REFUSAL, matched AFTER the existing FK/unique helpers so no classification changed. epigraph_node_tenancy's ('public', world) fallback IS a fail-open-on-error, but it is pre-existing to 070, documented in 072's header and gated by verify_definer_ownership — inherited, not introduced here.

edges_co_owner_shape genuinely protects the read predicate rather than being decorative: the fragment LEADS with `visibility = 'public'`, so a (visibility='public', co_owner=H) row would leak past the intersection entirely. The CHECK forbids that pairing for new writes.

splice's two substitution passes are order-independent: `/* {VISIBILITY:` is not a substring of `/* {EDGE_VISIBILITY:` (the fourth character diverges) and neither rendered fragment contains either prefix. A `.splice(` body carrying NEITHER spelling is still an offender.

No no-db regression: the whole `impl From<DbError> for ApiError` is `#[cfg(feature = "db")]`, no ApiError variant was added, and only one file under crates/epigraph-api/src changed (errors.rs — no route, router or middleware).

done.the_spec_contradiction_and_how_it_was_re:
The plan wants the constructor to fall back to `DATABASE_URL` WITH A WARN and to assert `epigraph_bypass()` is true, REFUSING otherwise. Those cannot both hold: the refusal makes the fallback dead code. Resolved EXPLICITLY, not silently, as a CONDITIONAL rule that is safe today and self-arming at PR-17: `maintenance_verdict` refuses only when row security is ACTIVE on a protected `public` table, and WARNs otherwise; the `DATABASE_URL` fallback stays live.

THE ARMING SIGNAL IS `ENABLE`, NOT `FORCE`, and getting this wrong was the land phase's blocker finding. An earlier revision keyed the refusal on `pg_class.relforcerowsecurity` alone. In PostgreSQL a policy filters every role EXCEPT the table owner and holders of `BYPASSRLS`; `FORCE` only ADDITIONALLY subjects the owner. Measured on the throwaway at head 91: every protected table (claims, edges, recall_events, group_memberships, agents) is owned by `epigraph` (superuser, rolbypassrls=t), and `epigraph_app` / `epigraph_admin` / `epigraph_maintenance` are all non-owner with rolbypassrls=f. So for every role a background writer can plausibly connect as, `relrowsecurity` alone is what starts truncating results and `relforcerowsecurity` is irrelevant. A FORCE-only probe would have been DISARMED in exactly the two moments it exists for: the window between the migration that applies policies (074, ENABLE only) and the one that adds FORCE (076), and after an operator pulls the documented `ALTER TABLE ... NO FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` kill switch, which drops FORCE and leaves the policies enabled. The predicate is now `AND (c.relrowsecurity OR c.relforcerowsecurity)`, the field is named `rls_active` rather than `rls_forced` (the old name WAS the claim), and it counts relkind 'r' AND 'p' so a partitioned table's parent does not leave it false forever. Pinned by a LIVE CATALOG test, not prose: `the_probe_observes_enable_row_level_security_not_only_force` creates a scratch table, asserts the probe reports false, issues plain `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, and asserts it flips to true -- which the earlier FORCE-only predicate fails.

done.land_phase_fixes:
Twenty-one critic findings, eleven blocker/major, all fixed. The land phase re-confirmed each fix present in the tree and then found ONE MORE, which is the entry worth reading:

L1. THE SUITE CAUGHT A REAL DEFECT IN A LAND-PHASE FIX. `pool::tests::the_endpoint_comparison_folds_loopback_and_nothing_else` FAILED on the first full re-run: `normalized_endpoint` folded `"localhost" | "127.0.0.1" | "::1"`, but `PgConnectOptions::from_str` keeps the RFC 3986 bracket form an IPv6 authority must be written in, so `get_host()` returns `[::1]` and the bare `"::1"` arm never matched. An operator whose two DSNs differed only in IPv6-loopback spelling would have got a spurious endpoint-divergence WARN -- and a warning that fires on ordinary local configuration is the one operators learn to skip, which is the whole reason the fold exists. Fixed by adding the `"[::1]"` arm, keeping the bare spelling for a DSN built via `PgConnectOptions::new().host("::1")`, which does not add brackets. Recorded because the test was written in the same land phase as the code it falsified: it was not decoration.

L2. THE BLOCKER: the privilege probe keyed on FORCE alone. See the_spec_contradiction_and_how_it_was_resolved. The fix is not just the SQL predicate -- the field was renamed `rls_forced` -> `rls_active`, its doc rewritten, both unit tests renamed and re-asserted, and `docs/deploy.md` §1c-bis restated, because a patch stopping at the predicate leaves the wrong rule asserted in four other places.

L3. THE HYBRID THE PR ALMOST SHIPPED IN THE API. `routes/claims.rs::find_claims_needing_embeddings` acquired a maintenance connection and then ran its statement on `state.db_pool` -- the application pool. Before PR-15 that was not a hybrid (the lease and the query came from the SAME pool); after the repoint it became one. The statement now runs on `&mut *maint_conn`, which required widening `ClaimRepository::find_claims_needing_embeddings` to an executor-generic form. This was the difference between the new maintenance pool being load-bearing and being an idle two connections bought with a documented budget increase.

L4. The `server.rs` comment named 'the belief recompute route' as a second consumer of the maintenance pool. No such route exists. Rewritten to name the single real consumer and to state the check (`grep -rn maintenance_viewer crates/epigraph-api/src`) and what to do if it ever returns zero: delete the pool rather than leave it idling.

L5. THE LIFETIME OBLIGATION IS RECORDED AS OPEN, NOT CLAIMED AS DISCHARGED. An earlier draft of the type doc was headed 'The lifetime, which the old template got wrong' and HANDOFF.md said the constructor 'fixes' it. Neither was true: `MaintenancePool::viewer` returns an OWNED `Viewer` while the `MaintenanceLease` is a local that drops at return, so a caller can drop `_maint_conn` and keep a bypass viewer with no privileged connection behind it. The improvement over `maintenance_pool_and_viewer` (which dropped the connection INSIDE the constructor) is real, and every converted bin binds it for the whole run -- but that is a convention, not a type-level guarantee. Both wordings now say so, and the remainder is `D-PR17-maintenance-lease-coupling-is-a-convention`. An obligation recorded as discharged when only a convention is in place is how it stops being tracked.

L6. THE `scoped()` ACCESSOR WAS DELETED. It handed out a `ScopedPool` whose `inner` is the PRIVILEGED pool, and its doc advertised as intended consumers the two constructors (`AppState::with_scoped_pool`, `EpiGraphMcpFull::with_scoped_pool`) that clone `inner()` into the pool serving callers -- which would put the whole request path on a connection RLS never filters. That is a fail-OPEN, not the fail-closed no-op the rest of the type guards against, and it is the one genuinely dangerous surface the new API added. It had zero callers, so it was pure hazard; the reasoning is kept in the type doc so it is not re-added without a call site.

L7. `BANNED_CONSTRUCTIONS` broadened from `PgPool::connect(` to `PgPool::connect` (no trailing paren) so `connect_with`, `connect_lazy` and `connect_lazy_with` are caught. Nothing uses them today; they are the obvious spelling a future edit reaches for.

L8. THE PYTHON HALF GAINED THE DATABASE-NAME GUARD, in `scripts/maintenance_dsn.py`. Giving `MAINTENANCE_DATABASE_URL` precedence in ~21 scripts whose fallback default is a hardcoded PRODUCTION DSN, several of which write, is a footgun the PR would otherwise have introduced. The guard mirrors `resolve_maintenance_url`'s `db_of` exactly (path, else username, because libpq defaults the database to the role name). One module rather than 19 inline copies, importing nothing outside the standard library so that seventeen scripts do not acquire numpy and psycopg2 as a side effect of a DSN change.

L9. `resolve_maintenance_url` now compares HOST AND PORT as well as the effective database name, and WARNs on endpoint divergence rather than refusing. Refusing on host equality would boot-fail every deployment where `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and a container DNS name denote the same server. The residual is stated rather than hidden, in the docstring, in `maintenance_dsn`'s docstring and in §1c-bis: a maintenance DSN copied from staging beside a production application DSN names the same database `epigraph` on a different cluster and produces a warning, not a refusal.

L10. `docs/deploy.md` §1c-bis gained the job-path GRANT requirement: `assert_maintenance_privilege` probes bypass and row security and does NOT probe table grants, CI connects as the superuser, so the role dimension is exercised by no test. Whatever role `MAINTENANCE_DATABASE_URL` names must hold the API's full job-path INSERT/UPDATE grants, not merely `epigraph_maintenance` membership.

L11. `backfill_idempotence.rs`'s `stderr.contains("postgres")` -- near-tautological, since `postgres` is also the DSN scheme -- replaced with an assertion on the quoted form the error actually emits.

security_fixes_from_review.summary: Adversarial review found that three policy arms written as 'structural, self-certifying' predicates referenced only ROW columns and therefore filtered nothing. All three are FIXED in this PR, not deferred. Detail is at mechanism level only: this repository is public.
security_fixes_from_review.the_general_property: A policy arm that references none of epigraph_session_groups(), epigraph_writable_groups(), epigraph_principal_id(), epigraph_bypass() or epigraph_definer_bypass() is not a narrowing, it is an unconditional grant. Because an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT requires the SELECT side, such arms had to sit in USING as well as WITH CHECK, so they granted READ.
security_fixes_from_review.mechanism_of_the_fix: The provisioning bootstraps moved out of the policies and into SECURITY DEFINER WRITERS - epigraph_ensure_personal_group() and epigraph_provision_oauth_agent() - so the policies need no personal-group or NULL-principal arm in either direction. agent.rs::ensure_personal_group and ::ensure_for_client now call them.
security_fixes_from_review.oracles_removed: epigraph_is_group_admin and epigraph_is_group_creator lost their p_agent parameter and bind the subject to the calling principal inside the body; every policy call site already passed the principal. epigraph_is_personal_group is deleted outright. This removes three membership/authority oracles that were EXECUTE-able by epigraph_app over arbitrary (group, agent) pairs.
security_fixes_from_review.returning_under_rls: PostgreSQL applies a table's SELECT policy to the rows a RETURNING clause produces. SecurityEventRepository::log's INSERT ... RETURNING was refused 42501 for any event not attributed to the session principal, while the identical INSERT without RETURNING succeeded - so the audit trail would have stopped being written, silently, since both call sites swallow the error. The RETURNING is removed and the input row echoed back. Same class as F-PR17-on-conflict-is-checked-against-the-using-clause, and the sweep for that one did not cover it.
security_fixes_from_review.attribution: security_events_append was WITH CHECK (true), which argued anti-suppression correctly and said nothing about attribution. It now refuses cross-attribution from any session that HAS a principal, while staying permissive when there is none so a pre-authentication failure is still recorded. THREE arms, and the third is not redundant: `agent_id IS NULL` is its own arm because `NULL IS NOT DISTINCT FROM <uuid>` is FALSE, so an attribution arm written with IS NOT DISTINCT FROM does NOT admit an unattributed row - and oauth/providers/provision.rs::record_oauth_event hard-codes agent_id: None. A first draft got this wrong and its COMMENT asserted the opposite of what the predicate did; caught by re-reading the predicate against the comment, which is the same failure mode as the three blockers. MEASURED on a re-migrated throwaway, all four cases: principal+NULL succeeds, principal+foreign is refused, principal+own succeeds, no-principal+any succeeds. FULL binding rides the acquire_as precondition; see explicitly_not_done.
security_fixes_from_review.boot_probe: AppState::assert_rls_posture propagated PROBE errors as well as verdict refusals, and the caller .expect()s it - so a failure to READ the posture was a boot panic. Staging the verdict buys nothing if the probe is unconditionally fatal. Probe errors now warn and continue; only a verdict refusal is returned.
security_fixes_from_review.grant_gap: 077's GRANT ... ON ALL TABLES binds only tables existing at version 077, so a fresh migrate missed every later migration's table - measured, webhook_subscriptions (085) was the one relation epigraph_app could not SELECT. Both halves now ship: ON ALL TABLES for the deployed database (where later tables already exist) and ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES for fresh migrates. The rule is in migrations/README.md.

MEASURED on the throwaway at head 91 with FORCE live, and then re-measured THROUGH THE ACCEPTANCE TEST ITSELF by temporarily building that exact shape: it satisfies three of the four acceptance properties and fails the second, in the opposite direction. With only the existence arm in the frame, the viewer-filtered arm is still narrowed by claims_tenancy to visibility='public' whatever the spliced bind carries, because the policy keys on epigraph_session_groups() and not on the bind -- so on an UNSTAMPED epigraph_app connection holding a MEMBER viewer, a group-private claim the viewer may read comes back reported hidden. critic_findings_fixed.cap_probe_measured_after_the_join: REAL DEFECT, FIXED. select_closure asked the SQL function for node_cap + 1 rows and then compared node_cap against the row count AFTER an inner JOIN to claims. Every id the function emits consumes a LIMIT slot whether or not it resolves to a live claim row, so a probe window that was full -- meaning the function may have discarded real rows -- came back looking like a selection that fits, and the caller received an arbitrary subset reported as complete. That is precisely what the module's own 'caps REFUSE, they do not truncate' header and FINAL-PLAN §3.1's 'a 400, not a truncation' forbid. Fixed by making it a LEFT JOIN with the visibility predicate in the ON clause, so rows.len() equals the function's own cardinality, comparing the cap against that, and discarding unresolved rows in Rust afterwards. New test: privatization_closure.rs::the_node_cap_refusal_is_not_defeated_by_ids_that_resolve_to_nothing, built so the discrimination does not depend on which rows the un-ORDER BY'd LIMIT chose (5 live claims + 3 unresolvable seeds at node_cap 5: the post-join count can never exceed 5 and the function's own count is always 6). MUTATION-CHECKED: reverting only the measurement point to the filtered count fails that one test and no other.

done.a_measured_environment_finding_about_the: THE CAUSE OF THE E0432/E0463-CLASS FALSE FAILURE IS NOW ESTABLISHED, AND IT IS NOT WHAT THE PREVIOUS GUESS SAID. Symptom: cargo clippy reports 'could not find privatization in repos' and 'no variant named NotImplemented' for a module and a variant that are present in the source, while cargo check and cargo test on the SAME tree compile 390 binaries cleanly. Evidence: pgrep -af cargo showed a SECOND WORKTREE of this repository building the same package names, at the same versions, in the same profile, into the same CARGO_TARGET_DIR. Correlated three times with the failure and absent from every clean run; the failure clears by touching the two lib roots so the libs are forced to rebuild. Cargo's build lock SERIALISES the writes to a shared target directory; it does not NAMESPACE the artifacts, so two worktrees of one repository overwrite each other's lib output and the next invocation resolves against the other worktree's code. The earlier record's reasoning -- 'cargo takes a build lock, so concurrent invocations serialize rather than corrupt' -- is therefore the wrong inference from a true premise. Mitigation for a future slice: give a gate run its own CARGO_TARGET_DIR, or verify no other cargo process is active before trusting a compile failure that names a symbol you can see in the file.

(2) AN ITEM STATE NOW MEANS 'THIS PLAN CHANGED THIS ROW' RATHER THAN 'THIS PLAN LOOKED AT IT'. restrict_claims_conn's `IS DISTINCT FROM` guard -- the thing that makes a re-processed batch fire no trigger -- also makes it a no-op on a row already in the target group, which a plan frozen while that row was public meets as an ordinary matter and with NO race: privatization_one_active_per_group excludes only CONCURRENT running plans, so two plans against one group with overlapping frozen sets simply run one after the other. run_batch discarded the row count and marked the whole batch `applied`, and Direction::Revert consumes `applied` -- so half (1)'s stamp check would have PASSED on such a row and published it. restrict_claims_conn now RETURNS the ids it moved, run_batch marks those `applied` and the remainder `skipped` (migration 080's own vocabulary), and a batch that decides fewer items than it selected is an error rather than a wedge. privatization_revert.rs::a_revert_unapplies_only_the_items_this_plan_actually_moved runs two sequential plans over one overlapping claim and asserts both the item state and the tenancy; a_revert_leaves_a_claim_another_decision_now_owns_alone covers half (1) on its own. commit_one_batch in privatization_resume.rs marks `&changed` too, so the fixture's batch body stays call-for-call identical. done.what_shipped:
THE CLIENT-SIDE SEALING PRIMITIVES, AND THE TWO KEY-EXCHANGE FIXES THEY DEPEND ON.

crates/epigraph-privacy is new and DB-free: an encryptor whose AAD binds entity_id || epoch || field_tag, a two-state Confidentiality, GroupRole, a trimmed error enum, and a new rewrap module. FieldTag carries the six values 6.5.6 pins; every ciphertext is now bound to the FIELD it came from as well as the entity and the epoch, which is the one change this port makes to a construction 5.1 otherwise calls the best crypto in either repo.

crates/epigraph-crypto/src/key_exchange.rs: ecdh_shared_secret now returns blake3::derive_key("epigraph-key-wrap-v2", dh_output || sorted(pk_a, pk_b)) and refuses a non-contributory exchange; wrap_group_key and unwrap_group_key take (group_id, epoch, member_agent_id) and authenticate the triple as AAD instead of a fixed literal. AES-GCM authenticates AAD without transmitting it, so the wire payload is still exactly 60 bytes and routes/groups.rs::add_member's WRAPPED_KEY_SHARE_BYTES check is unaffected -- asserted, not assumed, by a test in key_exchange.rs.

crates/epigraph-cli/src/bin/group.rs is the epigraph-group binary: the --init-group ceremony the group routes document and which existed nowhere, plus wrap / unwrap / rotate / epoch-key / rewrap. It constructs no pool, reads no DATABASE_URL and names no database type. init-group mints an Ed25519 GROUP keypair -- create_group derives groups.did_key from group_public_key with the Ed25519 multicodec and that column is UNIQUE, so the ceremony had to mint a keypair the ported symmetric-only key generator does not produce.

NO MIGRATION, no sqlx macro, no repo-layer SQL, no route handler, no Viewer, no write path.
done.acceptance_clause_disposition:
Clause 1 -- 'the same (uuid, epoch) in content, labels, properties, version and evidence produces five different AADs': DISCHARGED, and strengthened to six. encryptor.rs::every_field_tag_produces_a_distinct_aad_for_one_entity_and_epoch asserts pairwise distinctness across all six tags, which strictly implies the five-field clause; a_ciphertext_does_not_transplant_between_fields then shows the property at the ciphertext level rather than only at the AAD, and two named-helper tests cover the pairs a copy-paste would actually produce. The AAD byte layout is pinned by a known byte vector, not a round trip, because a round trip stays green through an endianness flip.

Clause 2 -- 'a wrapped share transplanted to another group/epoch/member fails to unwrap': DISCHARGED as THREE assertions, one per axis (a_share_does_not_transplant_to_another_{group,epoch,member}), not the two test FUNCTIONS the Tests line budgets. The clause names three axes; the number of #[test] functions is not the requirement.

Clause 3 -- 'ecdh_shared_secret output is a KDF result, not the raw DH point, and rejects a non-contributory exchange': DISCHARGED. ecdh_output_is_a_kdf_result_not_the_raw_dh_point computes the raw Diffie-Hellman output independently and asserts the returned key differs from it -- 'it is 32 bytes' would pass on the unfixed code. kdf_context_string_is_pinned asserts the literal and reconstructs the whole derivation. non_contributory_exchange_is_refused supplies a low-order peer key and requires CryptoError::KeyExchangeFailed. test_ecdh_shared_secret_symmetric was kept rather than replaced: after the change it is the test that proves the two public keys are ORDERED before they enter the KDF, which is what makes both parties derive one key.

plan_corrections.PR19_five_aads_vs_six_tags: The PR-19 *Acceptance* line says 'five different AADs'; 6.5.6's code block enumerates SIX FIELD_TAG values (content 0x01, labels 0x02, properties 0x03, version_content 0x04, evidence_content 0x05, evidence_properties 0x06). SIX IS RIGHT and 6.5.6 is the authority: the acceptance clause's 'evidence' is one field name covering two sealed evidence fields, visible in 6.5.6's own seal-commit body ({id, ct_b64, props_ct_b64}). Implemented and tested as six; pairwise distinctness across six implies the five-way clause.
plan_corrections.PR19_edge_properties_shares_tag_0x03_and: 5.1 states the present-tense defect as 'encrypt_claim_content and encrypt_edge_properties emit byte-identical AAD for the same UUID+epoch'. The tag fixes exactly that pair (0x01 vs 0x03). 6.5.6 defines no edge-properties tag, so encrypt_edge_properties uses Properties (0x03) and the separator between an edge's properties and a claim's is the entity id, which is the edge's own UUID. No 0x07 was improvised; the recon's 'do not improvise a construction' governs.
plan_corrections.PR19_members_list_position: 5.1 says crates/epigraph-privacy joins Cargo.toml members 'between epigraph-crypto and epigraph-db'. SATISFIED, and an earlier wording of this correction claiming otherwise is RETRACTED. MEASURED on the shipped list: interfaces, authz, core, crypto, PRIVACY, ds, db -- epigraph-privacy does sit between the two crates the plan names. It is placed immediately AFTER epigraph-crypto, whose primitives it composes, rather than immediately BEFORE epigraph-db, because epigraph-ds sits between those two and only one of the two readings can be the literal one. The retracted wording said the instruction was 'not literally satisfiable'; that was false, and the Cargo.toml comment carrying the same claim was rewritten with it. A ledger entry that tells a later run a plan line is impossible, when it is not, is worse than no entry.
plan_corrections.PR19_tier_is_a_three_to_two_collapse_not: 5.1 and the recon both say 'the Public variant is dropped'. MEASURED: the ported enum is {Public, EncryptedContent, FullyPrivate} with as_db_str/from_db_str/requires_encryption. So the transform is 3 -> 2 with a rename AND a collapse: Public is dropped, EncryptedContent and FullyPrivate collapse into Sealed, and Plaintext has no ancestor. requires_encryption() has no meaning under the new pair (Sealed IS encrypted) and did not survive.
plan_corrections.PR19_confidentiality_is_derived_and_ther: 2.6 makes confidentiality orthogonal to visibility and 299 defines its state source as 'claim_encryption row present/absent' -- DERIVED, not stored. Confidentiality therefore ships with no as_db_str/from_db_str and a from_encryption_row(bool) constructor instead. This is not tidying: migration 060's claim_encryption_privacy_tier_check admits exactly one value, and a Sealed.as_db_str() -> "sealed" would collide with a live, three-way-pinned persisted vocabulary and tempt an unplanned migration. It never touches those repos.
plan_corrections.PR19_errors_port_as_is_is_stale: 5.1 says errors.rs is a 'port as-is'. MEASURED, three variants could not be carried: a #[from] sqlx::Error arm (the ported crate's ONLY sqlx contact -- carrying it makes 'DB-free' false in the manifest with zero queries in the crate); an invalid-MPC-parameters arm (5.2 puts mpc/ permanently out of scope, and porting its error vocabulary ports the vocabulary of the excluded thing); and a re-encryption-key-expiry arm naming a repository 5.3 marks DELETE and which this workspace does not carry. The remaining six are what the ported code raises.
plan_corrections.PR19_cli_source_path_follows_the_crates_: 5.1's Files line spells the source file crates/epigraph-cli/src/bin/epigraph-group.rs. That contradicts this crate's documented convention -- snake_case path, kebab-case [[bin]] name -- which PR-12 and PR-18a both applied and both recorded in crates/epigraph-cli/Cargo.toml. Source is src/bin/group.rs; the BINARY NAME epigraph-group, which is what the group routes' documentation invokes, is preserved exactly.
plan_corrections.PR19_no_required_features_on_the_group_b: The sibling maintenance bins carry required-features = ["db"]. epigraph-group must not: it is DB-free by design. Note precisely what that buys, because the plan's 'never linked into the server' is stronger than anything the manifest can state. The SOURCE is DB-free -- no pool construction, no DATABASE_URL, no database type named -- which is why epigraph-db/tests/no_unmaintained_dsn.rs (keyed on pool construction, and which scans epigraph-cli/src/bin) passes it with NO EXEMPT row. The CRATE is not: epigraph-cli's default = ["db"] links epigraph-db and sqlx, and Cargo dependencies are per-crate rather than per-target.
plan_corrections.PR19_group_role_is_defined_and_given_a_c: 5.1 says GroupRole 'becomes the single canonical vocabulary and its can_write() is finally enforced'. MEASURED: the vocabulary is stringly-typed at five server-side sites (routes/groups.rs::add_member's valid_roles and default_role, middleware/group_authz.rs, visibility.rs::Viewer::resolve, repos/community.rs's projection literal), and PR-19's Files line authorizes NONE of them. Adopting GroupRole in visibility.rs would additionally create an epigraph-db -> epigraph-privacy edge and change the subject of group_lifecycle.rs::the_four_role_vocabularies_agree. So the type ships with a real caller inside PR-19's own scope -- epigraph-group parses --role through from_db_str and refuses an unstorable role before a key share is produced for it -- and the convergence of the five server-side sites is recorded as D-PR19-A rather than done halfway. can_write() is exercised, not yet enforced at a write gate; that gate is 16b's.
plan_corrections.PR19_from_db_str_rejecting_member_and_cr: 5.1's 'from_db_str rejects member and creator' is a property the ported code ALREADY had -- it only ever accepted reader/writer/admin. It is not a change to make. It is now asserted (group.rs::the_two_unstorable_spellings_are_refused) so it stays true.
plan_corrections.PR19_unwrap_group_key_is_not_named_by_5_: 5.1 item 2 names only wrap_group_key's fixed literal AAD. unwrap_group_key carried the same literal and takes the same change; a fix to one alone would produce a share nothing can open.
plan_corrections.PR19_wrap_signatures_widen_and_the_plan_: The new AAD needs group_id, epoch and member_agent_id, and NONE of the three appeared in the ported wrap_key_for_member / unwrap_key_as_member signatures. They are passed as a single ShareBinding value rather than three positional arguments, so that the three components of ONE binding cannot be transposed by position. Stated precisely, because an earlier wording of this entry AND the type's own doc comment both claimed more: the newtype does NOT prevent transposing a re-wrap's SOURCE binding with its DESTINATION one -- `from` and `to` are the same type and swapping them at a call site compiles. Such a call fails closed, at the unwrap under `from`. Distinct source/destination wrapper types would close it structurally and are budgeted by no Files line here; both the doc comment and this entry were corrected to say what the type does. Separately: the ported code assumed an infallible ecdh_shared_secret; the kernel's returns Result, so every ported call site gained a `?`.
plan_corrections.PR19_the_init_group_ceremony_needs_a_key: The ported create_group_keys returns symmetric material only (base key, epoch key, epoch). MEASURED: routes/groups.rs::create_group requires a 32-byte hex group_public_key, derives groups.did_key from it via DidKey::from_public_key -- which prefixes the Ed25519 multicodec -- and that column is UNIQUE. So the key is an Ed25519 public key and the ceremony must mint a GROUP keypair, not reuse an operator's identity key. epigraph-group init-group does, and a test asserts the emitted key is 32 bytes, is a valid Ed25519 public key, reproduces the did the route would derive, and is the public half of the secret it emits alongside.
plan_corrections.PR19_rewrap_takes_an_ed25519_verifying_k: 5.1 describes rewrap.rs as re-wrapping 'under B's real X25519 public key'. Every agent in this system is identified by a 32-byte Ed25519 public key (agents.public_key, with a length CHECK and a UNIQUE index); the X25519 key is derived from it by the birational map already in epigraph-crypto. Taking a raw X25519 parameter would mean asking callers for a key the directory does not hold, or re-implementing the agreement and its KDF beside the one canonical implementation -- the improvisation the recon forbids. rewrap goes through ecdh_shared_secret and wrap_group_key, and the doc comment says why.
plan_corrections.PR19_the_ninth_ported_key_manager_test_w: The ported key manager had a get_epoch_key wrapper that only called derive_epoch_key, and a test for it. The wrapper is not carried across (the binary calls derive_epoch_key directly), and without it that test asserted a function equals itself. Dropped rather than kept green; the comment in its place says so. Eight of the nine ported tests remain, three of them widened with the new binding.
plan_corrections.PR19_5_1s_rls_row_had_already_landed: 5.1's table is headed 'PR-19 only' and contains a row moving rls.rs into crates/epigraph-db/src/pool.rs. MEASURED: pool.rs exists with ScopedPool::acquire_as / begin_as / unscoped_for_maintenance, a session-vs-transaction GUC split and an after-release scrub, delivered by PR-15/0.5, and it stamps epigraph.* GUCs rather than the enterprise app.group_id. NOT PORTED, and no set_group_context was added. The three routes/claims.rs comments telling a reader to add an epigraph-privacy dependency 'to restore RLS group context' were DELETED rather than amended: the crate now exists and still does not contain that function, so an amended comment would point at a real crate and still be wrong.
plan_corrections.PR19_no_content_sealer_trait_is_owed: 316 and decisions_taken.PR11_action_read_deleted both say PR-19 'reopens epigraph-interfaces/src/policy.rs to reborn EncryptionProvider as ContentSealer'. PR-19's Files line names no trait and no epigraph-interfaces edit, and 316's own argument is that a trait taking key_id: &str HAS NOWHERE TO PUT AN ENTITY ID -- which is the whole point of the AAD. The free-function port with an explicit entity_id parameter satisfies the rebirth; a trait would reintroduce the shape 316 rejects. epigraph-interfaces/src/policy.rs is NOT TOUCHED, and no read-side gate concept is reintroduced (F2).
plan_corrections.PR19_ed25519_to_x25519_publics_errors_co: The shipped # Errors section claimed the function returns InvalidPublicKey 'if verifying_key encodes an invalid (low-order) Edwards point that cannot be decompressed'. Small-order Edwards points are VALID encodings and DO decompress. Left as written, the comment argued that the contributory check added by this change is redundant, when it is the only thing that rejects exactly that peer. Corrected in the same change as the fix.
plan_corrections.PR19_redaction_placeholder_respelled_not: The ported redacting Debug impls put a bracketed upper-case placeholder in STRING position, and epigraph-api/tests/no_redaction_sentinel.rs walks crates/*/src/ for every crate, strips comments only, and scans string literals -- so a verbatim port fails a source lint. That lint's own doc pre-authorises the fix: 'A crate with a legitimate unrelated use (masking a secret in a log line, say) is not what this lint is about: give the placeholder a different spelling, or narrow the walk'. Respelled. The walk was NOT narrowed -- that would trade a whole-tree property for one crate's convenience. The matching test asserts the PROPERTY (no rendering of the struct contains the key bytes) rather than the placeholder's spelling, so it can never itself reopen the banned literal in a file outside the scan root.
plan_corrections.PR19_two_of_the_six_field_tags_ship_with: FieldTag carries six values and only FOUR have named encrypt_*/decrypt_* pairs -- Content, Properties, VersionContent, EvidenceContent. Labels (0x02) and EvidenceProperties (0x06) ship reachable only through the generic encrypt_content / decrypt_content with the tag passed explicitly. Deliberate, and it matches the plan: 5.1's Files line names the content, edge-properties, version and evidence helpers and no others, and neither missing pair has the shape the named helpers take (claims.labels is text[], evidence properties are JSON -- both serialise before sealing, like edge properties). No acceptance clause is affected: clause 1 is about AAD distinctness and is discharged pairwise over all SIX tags (field_tag_all_is_exhaustive, every_field_tag_produces_a_distinct_aad_for_one_entity_and_epoch, a_ciphertext_does_not_transplant_between_fields). done.what_shipped:
ATOMIC KEY ROTATION, GATED ON A RECOVERABLE RETIRING EPOCH, AND THE OBLIGATION A MEMBER REMOVAL LEAVES.

GroupKeyEpochRepository::rotate_conn takes a borrowed connection, locks the live roster and then the epoch row, refuses unless the RETIRING epoch is recoverable (its own wrapped_key, or groups.properties->>'kms_key_ref' -- the request carries NO key material), requires the submitted shares to cover exactly the locked roster, then retires N and creates N+1 and re-wraps every live member in place. Nothing is partially applied: every refusal returns before the first write and the caller's transaction rolls back.

POST /api/v1/groups/:id/rotate runs its ENTIRE body -- the group-admin membership check included -- on one ScopedPool::begin_as transaction. The REASON is correctness, not lint compliance: rotate_conn writes group_key_epochs and group_memberships, both FORCEd by 079 with policies keying on the connection's tenancy GUCs, and this is the first group route where the authorization decision and the writes it authorises provably run on the same stamped connection. On the raw pool it would write correctly today and write nothing from 9.2 step 11d onward, with no error. That it also reaches AppState::db_pool nowhere, leaving routes/groups.rs at the exact 12 sites no_unscoped_pool.rs records, is a consequence. The other four group routes -- including the removal that now writes groups.reseal_required_at -- remain unstamped, as all 391 unconverted sites do; the asymmetry is stated rather than claimed away.

GroupMembershipRepository::revoke_member_unless_last_admin now sets groups.reseal_required_at and moves the group's current key epoch to status='rotating', in its existing transaction and on the Revoked arm only. It MARKS and does not enqueue -- 6.7 is explicit that an automatic re-seal cannot work, because the server holds no group key.

GroupRow gained reseal_required_at and all three of its SELECTs project it; GET /groups/:id surfaces it. GroupRepository::count_reseal_required_older_than feeds a new epigraph_groups_reseal_required gauge, sampled on the existing 30s tenancy tick and counting only obligations older than 7 days.

The 6.7 sentence is ONE pub const (epigraph_api::tenancy_disclosure) with three readers: docs/tenancy.md, the rotate response body, and the privatization preview's new side_effects.revocation. A test asserts all three agree.

done.what_shipped:
SEAL MODE -- CLIENT-DRIVEN SUBGRAPH ENCRYPTION OVER THE FULL 6.5.4 TCB, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.

FOUR ROUTES. GET .../plans/:id/seal-manifest serves the plaintext TCB for a plan's frozen items (the one response in the system that discloses plaintext the caller may not otherwise read, authorised by 6.6 and dual-logged to security_events and privatization_audit). POST .../seal-commit takes client ciphertext. GET .../unseal-manifest serves ciphertext only. POST .../unseal-commit takes restored plaintext back. create_plan's 501 arm for mode='seal' is gone.

THE SEAL MUTATION IS THE WHOLE TCB, NOT claims ALONE. PrivatizationRepository::seal_claims_conn writes claim_encryption (content, labels, properties), sentinels claims.content, nulls BOTH vector columns (embedding and embedding_3072 -- the second is absent from 6.5.4's table and is live in this schema), empties labels/properties, seals the complete claim_versions history and every evidence row (raw_content, properties, both vectors), DELETEs the six derived extraction tables, and blanks harvester_fragments source text through the provenance join. content_tsv needs no statement: it is GENERATED ALWAYS and follows content, in both directions.

A COMMIT MISSING ANY TCB MEMBER IS REFUSED, NOT PARTIALLY APPLIED, in BOTH directions. The seal side reads seal_tcb_shape_conn from the database at commit time (not from the manifest it served) and runs require_full_cover per table; the unseal side reads unseal_tcb_shape_conn -- the ciphertext shape, bound to the plan's target group -- and does the same. The asymmetry is deliberate and documented: seal covers every PLAINTEXT row that exists, unseal covers every CIPHERTEXT row that exists, so a version inserted after a seal is neither demanded nor touched.

LENGTH PADDING. epigraph-privacy::padding pads to the plan's pad_to bucket so a 1-byte and a 200-byte plaintext are indistinguishable at pad_to=256. The acceptance line's reading (the stored blob is a multiple of pad_to) is the one implemented, because it is the only one the SERVER can verify: seal is client-driven and the server never sees a plaintext. See plan_corrections 2.

PrivatizationResealHandler, the third handler 6.5.5 names and the ONLY writer that clears groups.reseal_required_at. It does no cryptography by design (6.7: the server holds no key); it measures whether any ciphertext row is still bound to a retired epoch and clears the flag only at zero. It is enqueued by BOTH commit routes -- a group answers a rotation either by re-sealing or by unsealing, and before the review round only the seal path enqueued it, so a group that unsealed everything stayed flagged forever with the gauge climbing.

epigraph-privatize (a new [[bin]] in epigraph-cli, no required-features) is the key-holding client: seal, unseal and reseal subcommands that page the manifest, pad, encrypt/decrypt with epigraph-privacy, and commit.

REVIEW ROUND (land phase). The unseal DIRECTION was under-scoped and is now fixed. unseal_commit checked 6.6 against the plan's target group and then mutated whatever the request body named, scoped only by 'is sealed'; the seal direction had always checked plan membership. Four changes: (a) unseal_commit calls plan_contains_conn and refuses a body naming any claim outside the plan; (b) the head UPDATE requires a claim_encryption row bound to the plan's target group, so plan membership alone cannot reach a claim sealed under another group's key; (c) the version and evidence UPDATEs carry the parent claim id through the unnest and match on it, so a row id is addressable only through the claim it belongs to; (d) unseal_commit runs require_full_cover over the ciphertext shape and the ciphertext DELETEs are keyed on what was actually restored, so a commit that omitted a version row can no longer delete the only remaining copy of its plaintext. The server cannot check the plaintext it is handed -- content_hash on this path is BLAKE3 over the caller's own supplied string and the key is one the server never holds -- so those predicates carry the whole weight, and visibility_lint.rs's justification for unseal_claims_conn was rewritten to say that instead of the EXISTS-claim_encryption bound it used to cite. A plan-state check was added too (applied | applied_with_drift | reverting); reverting is admitted deliberately, because a revert is refused while any item is still sealed and the 4h TTL is not applied to the reverse direction.

Also from the review round: one correlation id per commit request, threaded into the item.seal / item.unseal audit rows and the reseal job (they were NULL); the module doc's absolute pagination invariant now records the two manifest routes as a carve-out with its justification; and the harvester_fragments over-reach is now stated in SEAL_UNRECOVERABLE, in docs/tenancy.md and in a test.

Migration 084 drops public.ownership and, EXPLICITLY and in their own statements, the ownership_key_id_quarantine VIEW (068) and public.epigraph_ownership_transcribe() (071). DROP TABLE takes ownership_pkey, the four idx_ownership_* indexes, the six CHECK/FK constraints and BOTH triggers (ownership_updated_at from 001, ownership_transcribe from 071) with it; it does NOT take the SECURITY DEFINER body behind the second trigger, so that is dropped by name. TWO PRE-FLIGHTS, BOTH `RAISE EXCEPTION`, BOTH BEFORE ANYTHING IS DROPPED. (1) ownership_key_id_quarantine must be EMPTY. (2) zero rows with partition_type <> 'public' whose tenancy_transcription_log entry does not record the partition the row CURRENTLY holds -- the predicate migration 062's header states from the other side ('Migration 084 REFUSES to DROP TABLE ownership unless every non-public ownership row has a row here'). A migration that logged and proceeded would convert a data-loss guard into a log line.

PRE-FLIGHT (2) IS DELIBERATELY STRONGER THAN A BARE `NOT EXISTS` ON node_id, AND THE REASON IS A REVIEW FINDING. tenancy_transcription_log is `node_id PRIMARY KEY` written `ON CONFLICT (node_id) DO UPDATE SET from_partition = EXCLUDED.from_partition` (071), and it is written for EVERY partition_type including 'public'. So a presence-only check is satisfied by a ledger row recording an OLDER partition: a node whose last trigger firing happened while it was public, and which then moved to a non-public partition without the trigger firing, would pass a presence check while its non-public declaration had never reached a visibility column -- verbatim the harm the guard exists to prevent, on a one-way door. The guard therefore joins on `l.from_partition = o.partition_type`. from_partition is `text NOT NULL` (062) and the trigger is its only writer, so the added conjunct refuses exactly one state: a row whose partition changed without the trigger seeing it. Any database that satisfies docs/deploy.md steps 1-2 satisfies it, because the transcription pass wrote `owner_id = owner_id` to re-fire the AFTER trigger, which stamps from_partition = the row's then-current partition_type. crates/epigraph-db/tests/retire_ownership_preflight.rs pins both polarities.

done.what_this_shape_does_not_cover:
STATED AS A BOUNDARY, NOT A STRENGTH.

(1) THE PREDICATE IS ADDITIVE TO MIGRATION 077, NOT A REPLACEMENT. 077 section 2a already generates `WITH CHECK (... OR owner_group_id = ANY((SELECT public.epigraph_writable_groups())::uuid[]))` across its owned set. What 077 structurally CANNOT express is the other half: its policies are FOR ALL, so Postgres applies no WITH CHECK to DELETE at all, and the OLD-row half of an UPDATE is selected by USING -- which reads epigraph_session_groups(), i.e. READ authority. An in-query WHERE predicate is the complement that closes old-row selection. This is the semantics argument for choosing a Rust-side predicate, and it is not a matter of taste.

(2) WHY THE DB-SIDE GATE COULD NOT BE THIS PR'S MECHANISM, as a Rust-measurable code fact: AppState exposes read_as and NO write equivalent, and every route write executes on the plain state.db_pool. A control reading epigraph_writable_groups() therefore has to either allow-when-unset (gating nothing on the request path -- a second PolicyGate, the outcome this PR exists to prevent) or deny-when-unset (failing every route write). The blocker is the STAMPING GAP, not the connecting role. That distinction matters because the role argument alone does NOT dispose of the alternative trigger-based frame -- a row trigger still fires on a connection for which row-level security is inert -- so the frame has to be rejected on the stamping gap, which is what this records.

(3) NO INSERT IS COVERED, AND CANNOT BE BY THIS SHAPE. `INSERT ... VALUES` has no WHERE clause for a marker to splice into. Every INSERT candidate also has its owner_group_id chosen by a trigger in the same statement (evidence_inherit_tenancy, edges_tenancy, claims_propagate_tenancy), so an INSERT-side gate would check a value the server just picked.

(4) THE PREDICATE CONSTRAINS WHICH ROW, NEVER WHAT VALUE. `SET owner_group_id = <a group I write to>` still succeeds at a converted site. Only the old-row half closes, and only where converted.

(5) THE SUITE PROVES THE APP-LAYER PREDICATE. It says nothing about the behaviour of 077's policies in an environment where they are not bypassed.

WHY THE ADDITION IS SOUND RATHER THAN A LOOSENING. The lint's stated rule is that a viewer-taking fn running SQL must be shown to put a PREDICATE in the query -- which is exactly why the constant names query text and mechanisms and REFUSES to accept group_bind()/bypass_bind(). Viewer::splice_write satisfies that rule by the same construction Viewer::splice does: it PANICS on an input carrying no {WRITABLE:} marker, so reaching it proves a predicate was substituted. writable_bind() was deliberately NOT added for the same reason the other two accessors are refused.

THE ALTERNATIVES WERE BOTH WORSE.
