Dropping the &Viewer parameter would delete the gate to satisfy the lint. The doc comment on the constant now records all of this, and notes that the two splice functions are NOT interchangeable: each panics on the other's marker, because they bind different arrays.

ONE FURTHER THING THE DOC COMMENT NOW SAYS, BECAUSE THE FIRST DRAFT OVERCLAIMED. SPENT_MARKERS is matched by a SUBSTRING SCAN OVER THE FUNCTION BODY, so it establishes that a predicate-installing mechanism was CALLED and NOT that the string it returned is the one that reaches sqlx::query. deferred_obligations.resolution:
All eight functions were rewritten. PR-08's objection was correct and is CONCEDED rather than answered: after migration 084 there is no relation that can express a node_type breakdown across six tables. Measured against the schema at 084, exactly TWO tables name an owning agent -- claims.agent_id and perspectives.owner_agent_id. evidence, frames, contexts and communities carry (visibility, owner_group_id) and no agent column at all. So the owned-node set is a two-arm UNION ALL over those two tables, and four node_type values that ownership_node_type_check used to admit -- evidence, community, context, frame -- can no longer appear in any count. THAT IS A NARROWING OF THE ENDPOINT'S CONTRACT and it is stated in the PR body, in the module doc and in docs/tenancy.md.

AND THE DOMINANT DIRECTION IS A WIDENING, WHICH AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS ENTRY RECORDED ONLY AS A NARROWING. Nothing ever auto-populated `ownership`: zero `INSERT INTO ownership` across all 90 migration files, and on the base ref the only writers were OwnershipRepository::assign / assign_with_community, whose HTTP route and MCP tools PR-14 deleted. So the OLD owned set was 'nodes for which someone explicitly wrote an ownership row' -- in practice near-empty -- and the NEW one is the agent's entire authored corpus. node_counts, degrees, edge_counts, temporal_bins, clustering_coefficients, belief_intervals, frame_coverage and conflict_coefficients all move in that direction. The DIRECTION is certain; the MAGNITUDE is exactly what M1 would have said. An operator's numbers can go from near-zero to full-corpus in one release. No existing test can catch it, because structural_features_authz.rs::seed_corpus called seed_ownership for every node in its corpus, so old and new SQL agree exactly on that fixture.

SECOND HALF OF THE CONTRACT CHANGE: NODE IDENTITY MOVES FROM PER-LINEAGE TO PER-VERSION. The claims arm carries no is_current filter, so every version of a superseded lineage is its own node and a deep-lineage author reports MORE nodes. No filter was added, deliberately: edges.source_id / target_id name a specific claim VERSION, so counting rows is what keeps degrees, edge_counts and clustering_coefficients internally consistent, and an is_current restriction would make a superseded claim's edges incident on nothing.

THE NEW KEY IS NOT A CREDENTIAL, AND THAT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN GLOSSED. claims.agent_id is inserted from the REQUEST BODY by routes/claims.rs::create_claim, whose own comment says at length that it 'is NOT a credential and never was, and nothing downstream may treat it as one'. GET /api/v1/structural-features/:owner_id is now a downstream consumer of it: a caller holding claims:write who posts a public claim with agent_id = <victim> has that claim counted in every subsequent structural read for <victim>. THAT IS ATTRIBUTION INJECTION INTO A CALLER-FACING READ, NOT A CONFIDENTIALITY LEAK -- every statement is still AND-ed with a correctly spliced viewer predicate, so no private row and no private existence is disclosed. It was accepted anyway because there is no alternative key that preserves the subject: :owner_id is an agent uuid and claims.owner_group_id is a GROUP uuid, so substituting it would silently make this a different endpoint. The honest framing of the change is dead-but-not-caller-settable -> live-but-uncredentialed. Re-owned onto the write-side gate as a NEW CONSUMER of the open half of D-PR16-claim-authorship-is-not-a-credential. It is the same fail-closed rule the module already applied to node_type='agent': a node whose owner cannot be determined is not counted, because D1 forbids treating 'cannot classify' as public. The response SHAPE is unchanged -- node_counts is a list of (node_type, count) pairs, so a type with no rows simply produces none. Deriving evidence ownership through its parent claim's author was considered and REJECTED: it would attribute to the owner evidence a DIFFERENT agent attached, which is a wrong answer rather than a missing one. temporal_bins binned ownership.created_at and now bins the node's own created_at; for a corpus whose ownership rows were written at node creation the two agree, and for one where a node changed hands they do not. belief_intervals, frame_coverage and conflict_coefficients became plain claims.agent_id joins, and they changed in the SAME way as everything else rather than 'with no semantic change' as an earlier draft of this entry said: all three were INNER JOINs onto ownership, so they only ever matched claims that HAD a row. Every rewritten statement still takes a &Viewer and still spends it: both union arms carry /* {VISIBILITY:<alias>} */ and the edges legs keep /* {EDGE_VISIBILITY:<alias>} */, bind indices unchanged (2, and 3 for edge_counts), the guarded `if let Some(g) = viewer.group_bind()` preserved at every site, and NO new VISIBILITY-EXEMPT entry taken.

deferred_obligations.owner: PR-20 (rotation's server half: repos/group_key_epoch.rs::rotate_conn and POST /groups/:id/rotate) -- enforceable half discharged by PR-20; the residual is unassigned
deferred_obligations.what: An epoch advance MUST be accompanied by a fresh base key and a re-wrapped share for every live member, in the same transaction.
deferred_obligations.detail: PR-19's client tool holds this by construction and by convention alone. rotate_group_key mints an INDEPENDENT base key alongside the incremented epoch and takes the outgoing base key as no input -- its doc comment says so -- while epoch keys are derive_epoch_key(base_key, epoch) for any epoch the caller names. Nothing outside that one function requires the pairing: MEASURED, group_key_epochs (migration 060) carries id, group_id, epoch, wrapped_key, status, created_at, retired_at with a UNIQUE index on (group_id, epoch) and NO column tying an epoch to a base-key generation, so neither the schema nor the library enforces it. PR-20 owns the server half and must carry the invariant across rather than inherit the convention. The wrap AAD's epoch component binds the wrap message and is not a substitute for it. Raised now because PR-19 is where the surface ships.
deferred_obligations.disposition:
DISCHARGED, THE ENFORCEABLE HALF. GroupKeyEpochRepository::rotate_conn reads the live roster FOR UPDATE and refuses unless the submitted shares cover it exactly -- no live member without a share, no share naming a non-member, and no member named twice -- and the re-wraps land in the SAME transaction as the epoch advance. ENFORCED AGAINST THE WRITE AND NOT ONLY THE READ, and that distinction is the whole of the discharge: an earlier revision of this PR checked the submission against the roster the SELECT saw and merely COUNTED the UPDATEs, so a re-wrap loop that affected zero rows would have returned Rotated, committed, and left epoch N retired with every live member still holding a share for it. rotate_conn now refuses unless the affected-row sum equals the submitted roster, so the caller's transaction rolls back instead. Without that assertion the 'enforced rather than conventional' claim was false in exactly the case it exists to catch -- latent under today's row locks, live from 9.2 step 11d, when a FORCEd policy's UPDATE USING clause need not match its SELECT one. Asserted by a_rotation_that_misses_a_live_member_is_refused_and_changes_nothing, a_rotation_naming_a_non_member_is_refused and a_rotation_naming_one_member_twice_is_refused.

RE-DEFERRED, THE UNENFORCEABLE HALF, AND IT IS UNENFORCEABLE BY DESIGN RATHER THAN BY OVERSIGHT: nothing server-side can verify that the submitted shares wrap a FRESH base key rather than the outgoing one. The server holds no group key material (6.5.6) and group_key_epochs still carries no column tying an epoch to a base-key generation -- re-measured on this tree against migration 060 and schema_contract.rs, unchanged. Closing this half would need either a schema change binding epoch to key generation or a proof the server cannot check; neither is PR-20's, and both are decisions rather than diffs. Stated in rotate_conn's own doc comment so the residual is visible where the code is read, not only here.

The roster guarantee is over the roster THE TRANSACTION LOCKED. FOR UPDATE does not prevent an INSERT, so a concurrent add_member can still land a member at epoch N after the snapshot; that is the pre-existing check-then-act in add_member and PR-20 did not introduce it and does not claim to have closed it.

open_findings.what: Nothing tracks cumulative epsilon across requests, so every noised count is recoverable by averaging repeated queries
open_findings.detail: The Laplace mechanism is applied per request with no accounting. A caller holding only claims:read issues N requests at the default epsilon and averages; the estimator converges on the true count at rate 1/sqrt(N). MAX_UNPRIVILEGED_EPSILON closes the SINGLE-REQUEST exact read (see the PR-08 entry's scope_addition_epsilon_ceiling) and must not be read as closing this. Recorded because the ceiling could otherwise be mistaken for a full fix. A real budget needs per-principal state and a refusal when it is exhausted, which is a design decision no acceptance line in the plan authorizes.
open_findings.assigned: unassigned - needs a privacy-budget design decision before it can be scoped
open_findings.disposition_note: Head of a group of three. A cumulative-epsilon budget needs per-principal state and a refusal when exhausted; no acceptance line in the plan authorises that shape. One decision resolves this, F-structural-moments-exact and F-structural-support-exact together.

open_findings.what: The means, variances and maxima of the four moment blocks are exact at every epsilon
open_findings.detail: degree_stats.mean/variance/max_degree, belief_stats.mean_interval_width/variance_interval_width/mean_pignistic, clustering_stats.mean/variance and conflict_stats.mean/max are computed in process from unnoised rows and are returned exact. PR-08 fixed the COUNT components of these blocks (see critic finding M3), which was an authorization bypass because degree_stats.total_nodes is the same quantity as the sum of the noised node_counts. The moments are a different problem: the sensitivity-1 count mechanism is not defined for a mean or a maximum, and adding count-shaped noise to a mean would be a worse lie than leaving it exact. max_degree is the sharpest of them - it is an exact order statistic of the visible degree distribution. Bounded: these are all visible-set quantities, so this is a mechanism gap, not a tenancy leak.
open_findings.status: open, documented in the module docs
open_findings.assigned: unassigned - needs the same privacy-budget/mechanism design decision as F-structural-no-privacy-budget
open_findings.disposition_note: Same decision as F-structural-no-privacy-budget. Bounded to visible-set quantities, so it is a mechanism gap and not a tenancy leak; adding count-shaped noise to a mean would be a worse answer than leaving it exact and documented.

open_findings.what: The Laplace mechanism noises histogram MAGNITUDES but never histogram SUPPORT, so the absence of a key is an unnoised exact zero
open_findings.detail: All three statements GROUP BY, so a key whose true visible count is zero produces no row and maybe_add_noise is never called for it. A caller therefore learns exactly which node types the owner owns, exactly which coarse relationship types are present, and exactly which weeks in the last 30 days had activity, at any epsilon. Existence facts are what the visibility predicate protects elsewhere in this PR. NOT FIXED IN PR-08 DELIBERATELY: the fix (enumerate the closed key domains - COARSE_EDGE_TYPES, the six ownership_node_type_check values, the 30-day week bins - and emit a noised row for every key including the zeros) would destroy owner_sees_the_whole_subgraph_and_a_stranger_only_its_public_part's `assert!(!sedges.contains_key("RELATES_TO"))`, which is a load-bearing tenancy assertion. Bounded: the support is still the VISIBLE-SET support, so this is a mechanism gap, not a tenancy leak.

RE-MEASURED 2026-09-02 under a corrected lint (balanced-paren argument region + let-binding resolution + the tier_a column set; see acceptance #1). COMPENSATED (the file contains check_content_access calls, though NOT verified to sit on the return path of the counted statement): claims.rs 3, edges.rs 4. UNCOMPENSATED (the file contains ZERO check_content_access): clusters.rs 2, conflicts.rs 1, cross_source.rs 1, embeddings.rs 1, hypothesis.rs 1, policies.rs 2, political.rs 1, search.rs 1, workflows.rs 4. The previous figure of 23 across 13 files is NOT comparable: it was measured by a scan that both missed format!-built statements and charged false positives from a fixed forward window. Latent, not live, for the tenancy dimension; live for un-owned claims via F-access-control-none-full.

RE-MEASURED AGAIN BY PR-14 (2026-09-04), and the COMPENSATED half of this split is retired because its compensating control was deleted. edges.rs 4 -> 0: all four statements moved into crates/epigraph-db/src/repos/ behind spliced Viewer predicates (EvidenceRepository::detail_by_id, ::by_relationship_for_claim, ClaimRepository::get_by_id, and build_evidence_chains reusing detail_by_id). claims.rs stays 3, but the per-site determination viewer_route_table_lint.rs assigned to PR-14 found they are NOT handler reads at all: lines 2193, 2241 and 2668 are all inside `#[cfg(all(test, feature = "db"))] mod db_tests` (2025..EOF) and are `SELECT properties FROM claims WHERE id = $1` read-backs asserting a write landed. The lint does not exclude cfg(test), so they must stay registered; COMPENSATED_INLINE_READS was renamed TEST_ONLY_INLINE_READS and now holds only ('claims.rs', 3). The UNCOMPENSATED_INLINE_READS ARRAY is unchanged at 8 files / 13 sites, but the constant is not: its doc block was first deleted outright by PR-14's implement phase and then REWRITTEN in the land phase, because deleting the register's only statement of its own severity in the same commit that makes its trigger condition a deploy prerequisite left the largest open disclosure register in the API layer bare. open_findings.fix_batch_measurement: DECREMENTED BY tenancy/fix-security-track, NOT CLOSED. UNCOMPENSATED_INLINE_READS goes 13 sites / 8 files -> 12 sites / 7 files: hypothesis.rs's single counted site is retired and the file is gone from the register entirely. The statement was create_hypothesis's VOI neighborhood scan, and the register DID count it (it names FROM claims and projects embedding, which is in CONTENT_COLUMNS). It mattered more than an id projection would: every number in that handler's voi response object, plus neighborhood_size, is an aggregate over its rows, so the response was a function of claims the caller may not read -- inert only while the corpus is entirely public, which routes/privatization.rs makes false today. It is now ClaimRepository::grounded_neighborhood(pool, viewer, ..), which marks BOTH claims AND the grounding subquery's edges; marking only the outer relation would have left the grounding decision, and therefore neighbor_count, a function of invisible edges. Both markers resolve to one bind index, so the statement binds group_bind() exactly once. The handler's extractor moved RequirePrincipal -> ViewerExtractor in the same change: the principal-only extractor would have kept this read out of every register permanently, which is the argument recorded on D-PR16-claim-authorship-is-not-a-credential. The remaining 12 are untouched and the disposition is unchanged. ACCEPTANCE, WITH THE TRAP IT AVOIDS. hypothesis_ownership_from_principal.rs::hypothesis_voi_neighborhood_excludes_claims_the_caller_cannot_read seeds two grounded neighbours carrying the IDENTICAL vector the handler will embed -- one public, one private to a group the caller is not in -- and asserts the EFFECT (neighborhood_size and voi.neighbor_count are 1, not 2), which carries the over-suppression guard in the same assertion. THE OBVIOUS PLANT IS VACUOUS: migration 070 makes the grounding edge inherit the private claim's tenancy, so the EDGE predicate alone excludes the neighbour and the test would pass with the claims predicate removed. The fixture therefore forces the grounding edge public, leaving the claims predicate as the only thing that can exclude the row. MUTATION PROOF: OR-ing the claims predicate away (arity preserved, real code runs) makes that test FAIL ON ITS OWN ASSERTION -- neighborhood_size 2 -- while the three sibling tests in the same binary, which are the pre-fix checks, all still PASS on the same planted tree. Restored and verified byte-identical by sha256sum.

open_findings.what: atom_count is derived from an `atoms` CTE filtered only on claim_neighborhood_membership, not on claims

open_findings.what: The --allow-unauthenticated-http listener now reads with the MCP server agent's group set, which is plausibly the largest group in the corpus after PR-12
open_findings.detail: Correctly labelled a widening in auth.rs, viewer.rs and server.rs, and genuinely mitigated today: that listener already injects every scope in SCOPE_MAP, so its holder has full write authority regardless, and migration 062 makes every row public. The forward-looking half is the reportable part - the MCP server agent authors every claim ingested over stdio, so under PR-12's ownership backfill its personal group is plausibly the single largest group in the corpus, and it is handed in one step to whoever holds one shared Caddy bearer token in front of a unix socket. 'Operators who do not want that should not run --allow-unauthenticated-http' is a fair position but it is a DIFFERENT bargain from the one the flag advertised. Options: resolve a dedicated zero-membership principal for that listener (public-only reads, fail-closed, flag keeps its old meaning), or refuse content-reading tools on it outright. Either way it belongs in docs/deploy.md, not only in a doc comment.

open_findings.what: graph_snapshot calls EventRepository::list(.., version + 1), which is now a regex plus two correlated EXISTS per row where it was a LEFT JOIN. REVISED BY PR-25: each of those two EXISTS is now a SECURITY DEFINER function invocation, not a primary-key probe.
open_findings.detail: The handler fetches all events up to `version` and filters client-side (a pre-existing shape, flagged in its own comment). PR-09 makes each scanned row pay one regexp_matches over payload::text plus a primary-key probe per uuid found. For a high graph version that is a near-full scan of `events` with per-row work that the previous LEFT JOIN did not have. No measurement was taken - the throwaway test database is not a workload - so this is a note, not a claim. Measure before optimising; the obvious fix is to push the `graph_version <= $n` bound into the repo function so the filter applies to a bounded row set. REVISED BY PR-25 (2026-09-06) -- the mechanism this entry describes is out of date and the correction belongs here, not only in the doc comment. PR-25 routes BOTH arms of the per-match suppression subquery through migration 086's public.epigraph_claim_tenancy_by_ids(uuid[]), so the per-uuid work is no longer 'a primary-key probe' but TWO invocations of a SECURITY DEFINER set-returning function. SECURITY DEFINER blocks SQL-function inlining, so the planner cannot see through either call and has no ROWS estimate for it, falling back to the SRF default for both correlated arms. The per-row cost is therefore strictly higher than when this finding was written, and the suggested fix -- pushing the `graph_version <= $n` bound into EventRepository::list so the predicate applies to a bounded row set -- is now worth MORE, not less. Still unmeasured; the throwaway is not a workload. PR-25 deliberately did not fix it: a ROWS estimate needs a CREATE OR REPLACE (a migration, out of scope, and it would in any case be wrong for hidden_claim_ids, which calls the same function with an N-element array), and pushing the bound down is a signature change.
open_findings.disposition_note: Unmeasured by its own admission, twice: the throwaway test database is not a workload. The entry is more valuable as a measure-before-optimising note than as a speculative optimisation, and the fix it suggests is a signature change that would need a real workload to justify. Accepted as a standing performance note.
open_findings.accepted_because: unmeasured; needs a workload, not a patch

open_findings.owner: every future PR that adds an RLS policy
open_findings.what: `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` is checked against the SELECT-side policy, so a provisioning arm present only in WITH CHECK is not enough. MEASURED, and it is not obvious from the PostgreSQL documentation.
open_findings.detail: On a FOR ALL policy the SELECT policy IS the USING clause. Measured as epigraph_app on the throwaway at head 079: a bare INSERT into group_memberships succeeded and the IDENTICAL statement with `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE` -- and with `ON CONFLICT ... DO NOTHING` -- was refused with 42501, even with NO conflicting row present. `agents` was unaffected because its separate `agents_identity FOR SELECT USING (true)` satisfies the requirement. This is invisible to CI (superuser + BYPASSRLS) and it would have broken every token mint on the day 079 landed. PR-17 swept every ON CONFLICT site against a protected table and recorded the disposition of each; the app-pool ones are covered by arms in 077 and by rls_enforcement.rs, and the maintenance-pool ones (tenancy_backfill.rs, the CLI bins, PostgresJobQueue) are inert because epigraph_bypass() is true there.
open_findings.disposition_note: Not a defect. It is a measured property of PostgreSQL that is not obvious from its documentation, recorded so a future policy author does not rediscover it the hard way. 'Every future PR that adds an RLS policy' is the correct permanent owner and needs no scheduling.
open_findings.accepted_because: a recorded lesson, not a defect

open_findings.what: The converted handler holds ONE pooled connection for 1 + 5 + N sequential round trips against a request pool of 8, and N is uncapped
open_findings.detail: AVAILABILITY, NOT FAIL-OPEN, and it is the cost side of the conversion rather than a defect in it. Before the conversion each of the 1 + 5 + N statements acquired and released, so lineage requests interleaved; now each in-flight request pins one handle for its whole duration. bin/server.rs builds the request pool at max_connections: 8 (the 2-connection pool is maintenance) and it serves EVERY route, so concurrent deep-lineage requests can make unrelated handlers wait at acquire_timeout. max_depth IS clamped (.min(MAX_LINEAGE_DEPTH)), so the walk's DEPTH is bounded, but nothing bounds its BRANCHING and the handler passes max_nodes: None, so N -- the per-node ClaimRepository::get_by_id_conn loop -- is the size of the visible result. Under SessionGucMode::Transaction the hold is an OPEN READ TRANSACTION for all N round trips, which also pins the vacuum horizon. direction=both doubles the walk on the same handle. DELIBERATELY NOT MITIGATED IN PR-26, WITH THE REASON RECORDED: passing a node cap here would truncate the response while `truncated` is computed from depth alone, i.e. it would under-serve SILENTLY -- the same fail-quiet class this series exists to remove -- so a cap needs a truncation signal designed with it. The real repair is to collapse the per-node loop into ONE batched viewer-scoped fetch (WHERE id = ANY($1)), which removes most of the hold time and is new repo surface with its own evidence. MATTERS BEYOND THIS FILE: routes/lineage.rs is the template ~50 shards copy, and a 40-site walk-shaped handler converted the same way multiplies this.

open_findings.where: crates/epigraph-tools/tests/table_graph_{discover,dossier}_tests.rs, and any target whose source expands CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR
open_findings.what: The shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR can hand a worktree a test binary compiled in a DIFFERENT worktree, because the value of CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR is baked in at compile time and is not part of cargo's rebuild fingerprint.
open_findings.detail: MEASURED on tenancy/fix-test-integrity's first full gate run. Four tests failed: table_graph_discover_tests (1) and table_graph_dossier_tests (3), with 'expected to find epigraph.claims', 'missing CREATE TABLE for claims', 'claims should have many call sites' and an unwrap on 'No such file or directory'. Those files compute their scan root as `concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/../..")`. `strings` on the cached binary showed the baked root was `/tmp/verify-448/crates/epigraph-tools/../..` -- a worktree from an earlier PR's verify run that no longer exists on disk. `touch`ing the two test files forced a rebuild and all four passed; the deps directory now holds both the /tmp/verify-448 binary and one rooted at this worktree. || WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE CRATE: the failure is indistinguishable at first sight from a real regression, it lands in a crate the diff never touched, and it is a DIRECT CONSEQUENCE of the shared-target-dir convention this series adopted for disk reasons. It also has the shape this batch exists to remove -- a test result that is about accumulated state rather than about the code under test. || NOT FIXED HERE: the options (add the path to a build.rs rerun-if key, resolve the root at run time, or give path-baking targets their own target dir) are a decision about the harness convention, not a cleanup. WORKAROUND for anyone who hits it: `touch` the affected test sources and re-run, then confirm with `strings <binary> | grep CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR-derived path`. || THE `strings` ARTIFACT WAS TRANSIENT AND IS NO LONGER RE-RUNNABLE, recorded at review rather than left as a standing citation. Re-checked: both surviving table_graph_*_tests binaries under the shared deps directory now carry a root pointing at this worktree, and no file there contains the /tmp/verify-448 string -- the forced rebuild replaced the stale artifact, which is exactly what this finding describes. The baked-path mechanism is primary-source evidence and stands on its own; the citation does not. || DEVIATION FROM THE BRIEF'S SECTION 1, recorded rather than glossed: that section requires non-attribution to rest on a base build in a throwaway worktree, and no base build was performed for the four run-1 failures. The reasoning used instead was the baked path plus a rebuild that fixed it, which is a different and stronger argument than the run-disagreement reasoning section 1 forbids -- but it is not the procedure section 1 prescribes, and the difference belongs in the record. || THIS BATCH ADDED AN INSTANCE OF THIS CLASS: crates/epigraph-db/tests/viewer_fixture_single_source.rs computes its scan root from env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"). It fails in BOTH directions, not only closed. A root baked from a sibling worktree that still holds full copies makes the offender arm fail while the non-vacuity arm passes -- a false red indistinguishable from a real regression. A root baked from a worktree branched AFTER this lands gives a vacuous pass while THIS tree carries a re-fork. A runtime root via current_dir() was considered and NOT taken here: it depends on cargo's working-directory contract and on the file's own location, and adding an unverified failure mode to a brand-new lint during a land is the wrong trade. It belongs with the rest of this finding, as one decision about the harness convention.
open_findings.assigned: unassigned; whoever next owns the shared-CARGO_TARGET_DIR convention
open_findings.disposition_note: A build-hygiene hazard of the shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR convention, not a defect in this tree, and accepted because the alternative is worse HERE: per-worktree target dirs are ~15G each and have twice filled this host's disk, once to within 2.9G of ENOSPC on the filesystem production Postgres shares. The hazard is real and now documented: CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR is baked in at compile time and is not part of cargo's rebuild fingerprint, so a target whose source expands it can be served a binary compiled in a different worktree. Mitigation is procedural -- treat a failure in a crate your diff does not touch as unattributed until it is reproduced on a base build in ITS OWN worktree, which is the discipline this series already requires for shared-database tests.

open_findings.owner: unassigned - needs an operator decision between two resolutions that are not equivalent: widen backfill_harvester_fragments' predicate (repairs the rows, but changes what the backfill does to existing rows), or widen residual() alone (reports them without touching them, but changes what verify prints for every tier-A table).
open_findings.disposition_note: RE-DISPOSED by the parent from OPERATOR-DECISION. open_findings.what: The trigger is AFTER INSERT only. An UPDATE of an existing harvester_claim_provenance row's fragment_id or claim_id runs no stamping trigger at all, and epigraph_app holds UPDATE on that table, so nothing enforces the assumption that no writer does it.

open_findings.owner: unassigned - needs a decision, because the fix is not a one-line widening. open_findings.disposition_note: RE-DISPOSED by the parent from OPERATOR-DECISION. The gap is measured and the constraint is measured — PostgreSQL rejects a transition table on a multi-event trigger, so this needs a SECOND trigger rather than an extra event on this one. A known repair with a known obstacle is work to schedule, not a question to answer. Recorded rather than fixed, and named in migration 089's own 'WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT DO' section so it is not inferable only from this ledger. Measured: PostgreSQL rejects a transition table on a multi-event trigger, which is why 'add AFTER UPDATE to the same trigger' - the cheap-looking option - is not available.

RESOLVED AS TO THE REPOINT, AND RESTATED RATHER THAN FLATLY CLOSED, because a bare 'closed' would overstate what is enforced today and PR-16 reads this file.

WHAT IS NOW CODE-ENFORCED: `unscoped_for_maintenance` draws from `maintenance_inner()`, fed by `with_maintenance_pool()`, not from the application pool. `tenancy_backfill.rs` no longer reads `env::var("DATABASE_URL")` into a raw `PgPoolOptions::new()`; it and 22 sibling bins go through `epigraph_cli::MaintenancePool`, and `crates/epigraph-db/tests/no_unmaintained_dsn.rs` fails the build if a raw pool construction reappears outside the five reasoned exemptions. closed_findings.what: An existence probe whose two arms are subject to the SAME policy cannot distinguish 'absent' from 'invisible' once migration 079's FORCE posture is live on an application role. closed_findings.detail: MECHANISM ONLY, per the public-repo disclosure rule. The function answers 'which of these ids exist but are unreadable' as a set difference between an existence arm and a viewer-filtered arm. That is only informative while the existence arm runs with authority broader than the viewer's, which is true of today's owner DSN and false of epigraph_app. MEASURED on the throwaway at migration head 91 with FORCE live, under SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION epigraph_app, against a fixture of one readable and one unreadable row: the result is empty both when the session GUCs carry the viewer's group and when they are unset, while the same fixture on the owner connection correctly reports one. So this is NOT repairable by stamping the connection and NOT a conversion site - converting its callers onto AppState::read_as would make the no_unscoped_pool.rs ratchet green over a control that had stopped working. closed_findings.pinned_by: POST-086, restated because PR-24 rewrote all three of the artifacts the open-finding version of this field named. (a) crates/epigraph-db/tests/rls_enforcement.rs::hidden_claim_ids_still_classifies_on_the_app_role_under_force -- the acceptance test, and the only instrument in the tree that discriminates, since every other exerciser runs on the superuser harness pool. (b) crates/epigraph-db/tests/locked_decisions.rs::d4_migration_086_installs_no_policy, plus that file's `Status at PR-24` D1 bullet, which states the RESIDUAL failure direction (degraded definer authority is still fail-OPEN; only a missing EXECUTE grant is fail-closed). (c) crates/epigraph-db/tests/schema_contract.rs::migration_086_read_definer_is_revoked_from_public -- the catalog ACL pin, including proacl IS NOT NULL, because a later CREATE OR REPLACE of the body silently restores EXECUTE to PUBLIC. (d) crates/epigraph-cli/tests/backfill_idempotence.rs' three verify cases (gate open -> FAIL on an app-owned body; function absent -> skip and exit 0; function present but migration row missing -> still FAIL). (e) The do-not-convert rule in crates/epigraph-db/tests/no_unscoped_pool.rs, which SURVIVES rewritten rather than removed and is now pointed at F-PR24-event-list-existence-arm-collapses-under-force and D-PR17. (f) hidden_claim_ids' own doc comment, whose `PRECONDITION FOR PLAN 9.2 STEP 11d` section became `BOTH ARMS RUN INSIDE A DEFINER FRAME`. (g) The bin/server.rs EXEMPT reason, which is now a STANDING exemption rather than exempt-until-this-lands.
closed_findings.resolution:
RESOLVED BY MIGRATION 086, AND THE PRESCRIBED REPAIR WAS AMENDED RATHER THAN TRANSCRIBED. This entry's REPAIR line said 'route the existence arm through a SECURITY DEFINER helper returning ids only and no content'. MEASURED on the throwaway at head 91 with FORCE live, that repairs three of the four acceptance properties and breaks the fourth in the opposite direction: with only the existence arm inside the frame, the viewer-filtered arm is STILL narrowed by the policy to visibility='public' whatever the spliced bind carries, so on an UNSTAMPED epigraph_app connection holding a MEMBER viewer a group-private claim the viewer is entitled to read comes back reported hidden and both callers drop its delivery. That is the shape both call sites actually have -- they take a raw &PgPool as a parameter and nothing on the request path stamps it (D-PR17-request-path-never-stamps-session-gucs) -- so an existence-arm-only fix would have traded a fail-open for a silent over-suppression on the same code path.

WHAT SHIPPED: public.epigraph_claim_tenancy_by_ids(uuid[]) RETURNS TABLE (id uuid, visibility text, owner_group_id uuid), LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER, SET search_path = public/pg_temp, REVOKE EXECUTE FROM PUBLIC, and a pg_roles-guarded ALTER FUNCTION ... OWNER TO epigraph_maintenance plus GRANT EXECUTE TO epigraph_app -- all four parts of 077's epigraph_live_memberships idiom. ClaimRepository::hidden_claim_ids calls it ONCE in a CTE and takes the EXCEPT over that, keeping its Viewer::splice marker over the function's output instead of over `claims`. Both arms are then evaluated inside the definer frame and the only filter left is the viewer's own predicate, which is the authority the signature promises and is independent of whether the session is stamped, unstamped, or incoherently stamped. A Bypass viewer still short-circuits through the existing mechanism (splice renders it to a separator, the arms coincide, the difference is empty); nothing hand-rolls that branch.

DEVIATION FROM 'IDS ONLY', STATED RATHER THAN ELIDED. The function returns two tenancy columns as well as the id -- the two columns the policy itself keys on -- and no content, agent, labels, timestamps, truth value or attribution. The ids-only alternative puts the caller's group array inside the definer frame; that shape returns ids only but makes the group array a parameter, which would disclose the owning group by PROBING and would let a caller under-suppress by passing a group it is not in. THE UNDER-SUPPRESSION HALF IS THE DECIDING ONE and the shipped shape does not have it (arm 2's bind comes from the Viewer object, so there is no group parameter to vary). THE DISCLOSURE HALF IS NOT A WIN AND AN EARLIER DRAFT SAID IT WAS: the shipped function returns owner_group_id DIRECTLY, which is equal to or greater than what probing yields. That residual is accepted on the same footing as 077's helper and bounded by the ACL: EXECUTE revoked from PUBLIC, granted only to epigraph_app, pinned in the catalog by schema_contract.rs::migration_086_read_definer_is_revoked_from_public. Enumeration is impossible either way: the body is `= ANY(p_ids)`. Same accepted residual class as D-PR17-live-memberships-is-parameterised-not-principal-bound, which is restated in 086's header; it cannot be principal-bound, because its callers ask 'classify these N caller-named ids'.

INSTRUMENTED, NOT ASSERTED. (a) The acceptance test is crates/epigraph-db/tests/rls_enforcement.rs::hidden_claim_ids_still_classifies_on_the_app_role_under_force, which drives the real repo function on a one-connection pool under SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION epigraph_app, asserts all four properties including the owner-connection calibration arm, carries a premise assertion that the session really is filtered, and adds a GUC-independence arm. Verified to FAIL on the same tree with 086 removed. (b) 086's function is added to epigraph-cli tenancy_backfill.rs::DEFERRED_DEFINER_FUNCTIONS -- a NEW list, NOT the unconditional DEFINER_FUNCTIONS, and the distinction is the design decision this PR argues hardest, because an unconditional entry would print `does not exist` at plan 9.2 step 11c and BLOCK a correctly sequenced deploy. Entries on it are skipped exactly while the FUNCTION IS ABSENT FROM pg_proc (with an explicit stderr NOTE: unchecked, not passing), and checked whenever it is present. The gate reads the OBJECT and not the _sqlx_migrations row: a database can hold the function without the row (a version row deleted to clear a checksum mismatch, a dump/restore, a baselined database) and a bookkeeping gate would have skipped the only catalog check for a silently no-opped OWNER TO there and still exited 0. So the week-11c verify pre-flight now covers the guarded OWNER TO whose silent no-op would reintroduce the collapse -- without that edit the one gate built to catch that failure would have been blind to it. THAT INSTRUMENT IS THE CONTROL, not the statement's shape: because both arms now draw from ONE call to the function, a frame that lost its authority shrinks BOTH arms together, the difference empties, and the callers read empty as `nothing is hidden` and DELIVER. Degraded definer authority is therefore still FAIL-OPEN; only a missing EXECUTE grant (42501 -> Err -> DROP) is fail-closed. Stated that way in locked_decisions.rs' D1 bullet and in 086's header. (c) locked_decisions.rs gains a Status at PR-24 block and d4_migration_086_installs_no_policy, which asserts from the migration source that 086 adds no pg_policy row, no FORCE flip and no tenancy column. (d) schema_contract.rs::migration_086_read_definer_is_revoked_from_public pins the function's ACL in the CATALOG -- has_function_privilege('public', ...) false, proacl IS NOT NULL, and the epigraph_app grant present -- because a later CREATE OR REPLACE of the body silently restores the DEFAULT ACL, which is EXECUTE to PUBLIC, and the source-text grep in d4_migration_086_installs_no_policy would stay green through exactly that.

NOT CONVERTED, DELIBERATELY. routes/webhooks.rs and routes/events.rs stay unconverted and the no_unscoped_pool.rs counters are unchanged (UNCONVERTED 6/3, HIGH_WATER 414, HIGH_WATER_FILES 51, EXEMPT bin/server.rs 3). Closing the probe does not by itself make them safe to convert; the do-not-convert prose and the bin/server.rs exemption reason are REWRITTEN to say what is now true rather than deleted.

closed_findings.raised_by: CI, via crates/epigraph-api/tests/group_lifecycle.rs::two_concurrent_admin_removals_cannot_strand_a_group failing on an unrelated PR
closed_findings.what: The last-admin guard read rows it did not lock. Folding the admin count into the writing UPDATE put the check and the write in one statement, but an UPDATE takes a row lock on the row it WRITES, not on the rows its WHERE clause READS. Two concurrent removals of a two-admin group write different rows, so neither blocked the other, and each one's EXISTS saw the other admin still live. Both committed and the group was left with zero live admins, which is a permanent lockout: require_group_admin is the only way in and there is no break-glass path.
closed_findings.detail: FIXED IN THIS CHANGE. The transaction now opens with SELECT agent_id FROM group_memberships WHERE group_id = $1 AND revoked_at IS NULL ORDER BY agent_id FOR UPDATE -- the group's whole live roster, which contains both the rows the guard's EXISTS can match and the target row its UPDATE writes. A second removal in the same group therefore cannot reach the guard until the first commits, after which READ COMMITTED re-applies the lock statement's qual to the committed row version and the guard's fresh statement snapshot correctly refuses. LOCK ORDER IS UNCHANGED and that was the deciding constraint: the lock is on group_memberships, the table this transaction already took first, so the order group_memberships -> groups -> group_key_epochs asserted by this function, by CommunityRepository::remove_member and by GroupKeyEpochRepository::rotate_conn stays true and none of those needed changing. Locking the groups row instead was rejected: no site in the codebase takes a groups row lock today, and adding one here would have inverted the order against the second removal path, which holds a group_memberships row while it writes groups for the same id. WITHIN group_memberships the lock statement selects the same rows in the same order as rotate_conn's roster lock -- same table, same predicate, same ORDER BY, the two literals differing only in line breaks, and every group_memberships row this transaction takes is acquired by that one statement -- the guard UPDATE re-takes a lock already held rather than adding an acquisition. The roster rather than the admin rows alone is what makes that true, and the new test the_lock_set_covers_every_live_member_not_only_the_admins is what keeps it true. NO MIGRATION: a count floor cannot be expressed as a uniqueness constraint, and nothing else here needs schema.
closed_findings.provenance: NOT introduced by PR-20. git log -S"OR EXISTS" over the file returns 64290977, which introduced the guard already in this single-statement shape. PR-20 (aebe8a2e) appended the two follow-up UPDATEs (groups.reseal_required_at, group_key_epochs.status) inside the same transaction, widening the window between the decision and COMMIT. It exposed the race; it did not create it.
closed_findings.survey: Obligation to look for the same read-then-write guard shape elsewhere, discharged by a scan for SQL containing both UPDATE and EXISTS across crates/*/src. The scan covered BOTH raw-string and plain double-quoted literals -- an earlier draft of this entry justified a raw-string-only scan by claiming all SQL under repos/ is written r#"..."#, which is false (there are roughly a hundred plain "..." SQL literals under crates/epigraph-db/src/repos/ alone), so the scan was widened rather than the claim kept. A query assembled with format! would still be missed. What the scan establishes is scoped deliberately: it enumerates the sites sharing this guard's shape, not that any of them holds or fails any particular property. Of the sites it found, this one is fixed here; the others in claim.rs are anchored by an earlier FOR UPDATE, in the same transaction, on the row their decision turns on; and the remaining one is already carried as an open entry with an owner (F-PR20-B), whose scope this change neither narrows nor restates. NO NEW FINDING is raised by this change.
closed_findings.verification: The pre-existing concurrent test is kept unweakened and was run ten times in a row (10/10 green), but it is NOT the evidence: it was also measured green 20 runs out of 20 against the DEFECTIVE tree, so a repetition count cannot discriminate. The discriminators are two new deterministic tests, each checked against a deliberately defective tree rather than asserted. the_guard_waits_for_the_admin_rows_its_decision_reads holds the row the decision reads and requires the removal to wait for it: with the lock statement deleted it fails, reporting that the removal returned Ok(Revoked) without waiting. the_lock_set_covers_every_live_member_not_only_the_admins holds a plain reader's row and removes a non-last admin, so it passes only while the lock statement covers the whole roster: with that statement narrowed to role = 'admin' it fails, again with Ok(Revoked). Both probes MEASURE the row lock -- they poll pg_stat_activity for a Lock wait rather than sleeping a fixed interval, and they hold the row on a connection opened outside the #[sqlx::test] pool, because that pool caps at five connections and reaps idle ones after a second, which made an earlier stopwatch-shaped revision report pool behaviour as a guard decision under full-workspace load. two_concurrent_removals_of_different_members_both_succeed is the positive control for removing a non-admin and for two removals not refusing each other; it is deliberately NOT offered as evidence about lock ordering, since two removals of one group request an identical row set and no interleaving of them can acquire anything out of order. LAND-PHASE RE-MEASUREMENT, run rather than inherited: both negative controls were re-executed on this tree by the landing agent. Deleting the lock statement makes the_guard_waits_for_the_admin_rows_its_decision_reads fail (exit 101, reporting that the removal returned Ok(Revoked) without waiting); narrowing that statement to role = 'admin' makes the_lock_set_covers_every_live_member_not_only_the_admins fail (exit 101, same shape). The file was restored by copy after each and its md5 matched the pre-experiment backup. The pre-existing concurrent test was then run TEN TIMES IN A ROW, 10/10 green, so the acceptance clause that asks for repetition is discharged literally as well as by substitution -- while remaining, for the reason above, not the evidence. The lock-ORDER claim was additionally checked outside Rust, on a scratch database created and dropped for the purpose: two sessions replaying the roster acquisition of GroupKeyEpochRepository::rotate_conn against a removal whose target sorts below an admin abort with 40P01 when the lock statement is narrowed to the admin rows, and QUEUE cleanly with the whole-roster statement that ships here -- all three rows acquired in agent_id order, both sessions committing. That is direct evidence for the ordering sentence in this function's doc comment, which is otherwise the kind of claim a comment can assert without anything checking it.

It has also now been executed locally in a SEPARATE target dir (/home/jeremy/.cargo-target-nodb) - a warm shared dir holding default-feature artifacts returns exit 0 on a tree that fails cold, which produced a false green twice on this project.
closed_findings.assigned: none - ci.yml is the standing gate

Scope confirmed on 0f6f8b02: ci.yml gates the not(db) build at lib+bins and says in its own comment that it deliberately omits --all-targets. So this closes for the parity shim it was about, and does NOT close the test-target build, which is F-PR10-no-db-test-cfg-never-compiles / F-PR28-nodb-lib-test-build.

closed_findings.what: A spliced statement binds viewer.group_bind().unwrap_or(&[]) unconditionally, which is a Postgres bind-arity error for a Bypass viewer
closed_findings.detail: Viewer::render_predicate emits a single space for a Bypass shape, so the rendered statement references no $N while the bind is still supplied -> 'bind message supplies N parameters, but prepared statement requires M'. Fail-CLOSED and unreachable today (this path's viewer never comes from a MaintenanceLease). PR-09 converted all NINE sites it introduced or touched to the guarded `if let Some(g) = viewer.group_bind()` form used by ~165 existing sites, and left this pre-existing one alone rather than widening its diff. A Viewer::bind_groups(q) helper that makes the correct thing the only thing would close the class.
closed_findings.disposition_note: NOT REPRODUCIBLE on 0f6f8b02, measured rather than inferred. All 34 group_bind().unwrap_or(&[]) sites sit in fixed-arity statements whose predicate is unconditionally present in the SQL text -- 33 in sqlx::query! macro invocations and one in a static query_as string. The bind-arity hazard requires the array to be bound onto a SPLICED string, where the predicate can be removed while the bind remains; zero sites do that. Spliced sites use the conditional `if let Some(g) = viewer.group_bind()` form instead. A lint in tenancy/fix-lint-robustness keeps this false rather than leaving it to re-measurement.

closed_findings.what: list_webhooks filters on sub.active; get_webhook does not. An inactive subscription would be invisible to list and readable by id.
closed_findings.why_it_matters: Inert today - nothing anywhere sets active = false, so the column only ever holds its DEFAULT TRUE. It becomes a real list/get divergence, with the id-addressed route on the permissive side, the moment a deactivation path is added. Same class as the ownership divergence PR-10 fixed.
closed_findings.suggested_fix: Add the active check to get_webhook in the PR that introduces deactivation.
closed_findings.owner: the PR that adds a webhook deactivation path
closed_findings.disposition_note: MIS-STATED, measured on 0f6f8b02. get_webhook takes RequirePrincipal and refuses when sub.agent_id is not the caller, so it is not readable by an arbitrary caller. What remains true is narrow and not a defect: an owner can read their own inactive subscription by id. There is no deactivation path in the tree, so the state is unreachable, and an owner reading their own deactivated registration is the behaviour one would choose anyway.

closed_findings.what: A transient database failure at startup permanently disables every content tool on the --allow-unauthenticated-http listener for the life of the process
closed_findings.detail: On error the code logs and stores None, which request_viewer turns into a hard refusal until restart. Before PR-09 the same listener resolved lazily per request and would start working again once the database recovered. The fail-closed choice is right; the once-only caching is the problem. Environment-specific weight: reference_postgres_static_ip_boot_race means Postgres losing its address on reboot is a recurring event here, so a co-scheduled MCP restart can land in exactly this window, and the symptom ('token carries no agent principal' from every tool) does not point at a boot-time DB blip. Fix: hold the id behind an Arc<OnceCell<Uuid>> that request_viewer can lazily re-resolve when it is None, keeping the boot attempt as a warm-up plus the loud error log.
closed_findings.disposition_note: CLOSED by tenancy/fix-authz-hygiene. The middleware state is now auth::UnauthenticatedPrincipal -- a boot-time warm-up plus a ServerPrincipalSource consulted whenever the warm-up is absent -- instead of an Option<Uuid> snapshot, so an unresolved id is re-attempted per request rather than being a process-lifetime verdict. The boot attempt and its loud error log are kept. The fail-closed behaviour is unchanged: while unresolved, the injected context carries no principal and content tools refuse. CORRECTION TO THE FINDING'S FIX SITE: the cell cannot live in tools::viewer::request_viewer, which sees only (server, auth) and cannot distinguish an unresolved listener from a real Bearer token carrying no agent principal -- a distinction PR-09 installed as a deliberate hard refusal and locked_decisions.rs::d3_mcp_viewer_acquisition_does_not_flatten_a_client_id pins by source text. request_viewer is therefore untouched. No further caching was added because EpiGraphMcpFull::agent_id already stores only on success and so already retries. tests/http_auth_test.rs::boot_unauth_router passes UnauthenticatedPrincipal::unresolvable() in place of None. Mutation proof: collapsing the warm-up check to `return self.warm;` makes an_unresolved_boot_snapshot_is_retried_on_the_next_request observe no principal on the second request. REVIEW PASS 2026-09-12, same batch: the adversarial review observed that an unbounded per-request retry traded one defect for another. Re-measured and confirmed on this tree: server.rs::EpiGraphMcpFull::agent_id takes agent_db_id.lock().await and HOLDS that guard across every database await inside it, and its not-found arm writes (AgentRepository::create, set_llm_properties, ensure_personal_group). So during exactly the outage the fix exists to survive, concurrent requests on the --allow-unauthenticated-http listener would serialize on one mutex, each paying a pool-acquire timeout, making tail latency N x timeout where the pre-fix behaviour at least answered instantly. FIXED in this batch: UnauthenticatedPrincipal now carries a cooldown (DEFAULT_RESOLUTION_COOLDOWN, 5s) and a shared last_attempt stamp taken BEFORE the source is consulted and cleared on success, so a burst during an outage collapses to roughly one attempt per interval and a healthy resolver is never throttled. The FAIL-CLOSED VERDICT IS UNCHANGED: a throttled request yields the same None an unresolved principal already yielded. The pre-existing retry test now runs with with_cooldown(Duration::ZERO) so it still observes one attempt per request and measures the retry rather than the bound; two tests added -- a_failed_resolution_is_not_retried_again_within_the_cooldown (20 requests, 1 attempt, and every response still carries no principal) and a_succeeding_resolution_is_never_throttled (the over-suppression control). Mutation proof recorded in the PR body.

closed_findings.what: The webhook fan-out treats 'the payload names a claim id with no `claims` row' as visible-and-deliver. routes/batch.rs::batch_create_claims exercises that branch on every request: it inserts only into AppState::claim_store and publishes a ClaimSubmitted per claim, so the claim id, submitting agent id and truth value reach every active subscription with no tenancy decision made.
closed_findings.why_it_matters: hidden_claim_ids' contract ('an id that names no row at all is not returned') is right for PR-09's use - redacting rows already fetched from a viewer-scoped source - and permissive for a delivery decision to an arbitrary external URL. PR-12 will not fix it, because the row still will not exist. NOT a PR-10 regression: before PR-10 every event went to every subscriber unconditionally.
closed_findings.why_not_fixed_in_pr10: Both in-scope fixes are wrong. Suppressing on named-but-absent would suppress nearly everything, because payload_uuids also collects agent, frame and workflow ids. Narrowing the scan to declared claim ids is the key allowlist PR-09 rejected verbatim. The doc now names the branch instead of asserting it away.
closed_findings.suggested_fix: Either make batch_create_claims persist (it has no auth extractor either, so it needs its own PR), or stop it publishing ClaimSubmitted for rows that do not exist.
closed_findings.owner: PR-12 or the PR that authenticates routes/batch.rs
closed_findings.disposition_note: CLOSED by tenancy/fix-authz-hygiene, taking the second of the two fixes the finding endorses. routes/batch.rs::batch_create_claims no longer publishes ClaimSubmitted. MEASUREMENT THE FINDING DID NOT STATE: the handler's only persistence is AppState::claim_store, which nothing drains into claims, and validate_batch_item mints a fresh claim uuid and a fresh AgentId per item -- so "stop publishing for rows that do not exist" reduces here to publishing nothing at all, and an existence query would have been a round trip whose answer is always "none". The other fix (make it persist) stays deferred: it needs SQL in the repo layer, an ownership decision at INSERT under migration 074's require-tenancy guards, and an auth extractor this handler still does not have. No in-process consumer keys on ClaimSubmitted, so the observable effect is that batch-imported ids stop reaching external subscriptions and stop occupying the event-bus history. The filter itself is unchanged and its permissive branch is still documented in routes/webhooks.rs; what changed is the caller that exercised it. The pinned assertion the recon warned about (test_batch_publishes_events_for_each_created_claim) sits in a cfg(all(test, not(feature = "db"))) module that no configuration compiles; it is inverted for honesty, and the live assertion is tests/batch_publish_test.rs. Mutation proof: restoring the publish loop makes a_batch_import_creates_its_claims_and_publishes_no_event observe 2 events.

closed_findings.what: routes/admin.rs::system_stats takes no auth extractor and no check_scopes - only State(state) - and is registered on the `protected` router in both chains, so any authenticated principal with any scope reads the whole SystemStats aggregate, including WebhookStats { webhook_count }.
closed_findings.why_it_matters: PR-10's boot hydration widens webhook_count from a per-process artefact to the cardinality of webhook_subscriptions across every tenant. A count, not content - but it is the one unfiltered path out of AppState::webhook_store, and it falsified the invariant repos/webhook.rs::list_active's doc originally rested its no-Viewer exemption on. That doc is corrected; the route is not.
closed_findings.suggested_fix: Gate system_stats behind claims:admin, or drop webhook_count from SystemStats, or make it count only the caller's rows. Note admin.rs:1017 and :1137 both assert on webhook_count.
closed_findings.disposition_note: CLOSED by tenancy/fix-authz-hygiene. Re-measured: routes/admin.rs::system_stats took State(state) alone. It now takes the RequireScopeAdmin extractor, so claims:admin is required; one definition serves both create_router chains because the handler is not cfg-split. The first of the three fixes the finding offered was taken; narrowing webhook_count per caller would have put a read of webhook_subscriptions in a route handler, and dropping the field would have removed a metric an operator legitimately watches. AVAILABILITY COST, recorded because it is a breaking change: claims:admin is in ADMIN_ONLY_SCOPES, so every epigraph-ro and epigraph-wo token, every agent auto-provisioned by POST /api/v1/agents and every DCR-registered public client now gets 403 here; docs/deploy.md gains a section 1a saying so. The finding's line numbers (admin.rs:1017 and :1137) were stale AND those assertions sit in a cfg(all(test, not(feature = "db"))) module that no configuration compiles, so they were never coverage; the live assertions are tests/admin_stats_scope_test.rs. repos/webhook.rs::list_active's doc, which narrated this gap as open, is corrected. Mutation proof: RequireScopeAdmin -> RequireScopeWrite makes system_stats_with_claims_write_returns_403 observe 200.

closed_findings.what: Viewer::resolve (visibility.rs:269) returns Ok(Viewer{Scoped{group_ids: []}}) for a principal with no `agents` row, because GroupMembershipRepository::list_live_for_agent returns an empty Vec rather than an error. agent_may_receive therefore does NOT fail closed for a deleted agent - it demotes the subscription to a public-only subscriber.
closed_findings.why_it_matters: Combined with the fact that migration 085's ON DELETE CASCADE removes the ROW but nothing evicts AppState::webhook_store, a running process keeps delivering public-visibility claims to a deleted agent's endpoint until it restarts. Wider than it will eventually be: with migration 062 defaulting visibility to 'public' and nothing transcribing ownership until PR-12, 'public-only' is currently close to 'everything'.
closed_findings.suggested_fix: Have agent_may_receive (or Viewer::resolve itself) distinguish 'agent exists with no groups' from 'agent does not exist', and fail closed on the latter. Both branches are now named in agent_may_receive's doc so the 'fails closed' list is honest.
closed_findings.disposition_note: CLOSED by tenancy/fix-authz-hygiene. Re-measured and reproduced. The fix is local to the webhook fan-out, not to Viewer::resolve: routes/webhooks.rs::agent_principal_exists probes AgentRepository::get_by_id and retain_visible_subscriptions drops any subscription whose principal names no agents row, logging a missing principal and a failed probe differently. Viewer::resolve is untouched, because "an empty membership set is not an error" is its documented and correct contract for every other caller, including the nil principal that five test crates resolve. No new SQL (get_by_id exists and takes no Viewer), so no visibility_lint exemption and no .sqlx regeneration. MEASUREMENT THAT NARROWS THE FINDING: the probe is placed alongside the agent_id == None partition, above the payload-names-no-uuid early-out, but relocating it below that early-out was tried and changed no test outcome, because every EpiGraphEvent variant serialises at least one uuid and the early-out is unreachable from any current publisher. The placement is a robustness choice, not an observable difference, and is documented as such rather than claimed. Mutation proof: OR-ing the existence verdict away makes a_subscription_whose_agent_row_is_gone_is_never_delivered_to observe the deleted principal's subscription in the attempted set.

closed_findings.what: register_webhook validates only that the URL is non-empty (and migration 085's `CHECK (btrim(url) <> '')` mirrors exactly that), so any caller with webhooks:write can register a link-local metadata address or a loopback port and have the api POST signed event payloads there.
closed_findings.why_it_matters: Pre-existing and out of PR-10's ledgered scope, but PR-10 changes the blast radius: an SSRF-shaped target was a process-lifetime condition and is now a durable row that boot hydration re-arms on every deploy.
closed_findings.suggested_fix: Scheme allowlist plus a private-range/link-local denylist at registration time.
closed_findings.disposition_note: CLOSED by tenancy/fix-authz-hygiene. Re-measured: register_webhook validated only url.trim().is_empty(). It now also requires an http/https scheme and refuses loopback, link-local, private-range and unspecified IP literals (IPv4-mapped IPv6 unwrapped first), via routes/webhooks.rs::validate_webhook_url. The policy STATES WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER, in the function doc and in tests/webhook_url_policy_test.rs: DNS rebinding is out of scope because the check runs at registration against the supplied literal and resolves nothing; validation applies at registration, so rows already in webhook_subscriptions are grandfathered and re-armed by boot hydration on every deploy; migration 085's CHECK (btrim(url) <> '') is unchanged; and it is a denylist of internal targets, not an allowlist of permitted ones. No new dependency (url 2 was already a direct one). Mutation proof: discarding the validator's verdict makes an_internal_or_non_http_delivery_target_is_refused observe 201 on an IPv4 loopback target. REVIEW PASS 2026-09-12, same batch: the adversarial review observed that a policy judging IP LITERALS only refused the literal spelling of loopback and accepted the ordinary one, and that the new test's own control pinned a loopback NAME at 201 -- recording the gap as intended behaviour, which is worse than the gap. WIDENED: validate_webhook_url now also refuses the names RFC 6761 reserves to loopback (localhost, and anything under .localhost), case-insensitively with a trailing root dot stripped, via a static denylist. This does NOT move the no-resolution boundary: those names are reserved to loopback by definition rather than by a record that could change, so no resolver is consulted and every other name is still accepted on its face. The control fixture was moved to a name under .example (RFC 2606), which never resolves and has no loopback semantics, so it pins 'names are not resolved' and nothing else. Four spellings added to an_internal_or_non_http_delivery_target_is_refused's table. Mutation proof recorded in the PR body. NOT adopted: 100.64.0.0/10, because Ipv4Addr::is_shared is unstable and the 'this is not an allowlist' disclaimer already covers it.

closed_findings.what: routes/community.rs::add_member takes only a ViewerExtractor and State - no scope extractor, no community-admin check, and no requirement that the perspective being added belongs to the caller. remove_member has neither a Viewer nor a scope extractor.
closed_findings.why_it_matters: It routes around the declassification control PR-11 just hardened, for the whole `community` partition. access_control.rs::check_content_access's "community" arm returns ContentAccess::Full to any requester owning a perspective that is a member of the gating community, so instead of calling the now-gated update_partition, any authenticated agent creates a perspective, POSTs it into the gating community, and reads everything behind it. The two existence pre-checks are viewer-filtered, but migration 062 defaults visibility to 'public', so on today's corpus that filter excludes nothing. remove_member is the integrity twin: any authenticated agent can evict any perspective from any community.
closed_findings.suggested_fix: A require_community_admin-shaped membership check plus a scope extractor, mirroring groups::add_member (which takes RequireScopeGroupsAdmin AND calls group_authz::require_group_admin).
closed_findings.owner: PR-16 for the scope extractor and the admin-shaped rule; PR-12 closed the self-service grant and the self-service eviction.
closed_findings.status: SUBSTANTIALLY CLOSED BY PR-12, and PR-12 is why it had to be. Projecting the membership moved the hole out of check_content_access's community arm (which PR-14 deletes) and into the group_memberships / Viewer::resolve control plane, which SURVIVES PR-14 and is armed by PR-17 - i.e. it was on its way from a soon-to-be-deleted ACL bug to a durable tenancy bypass. CommunityRepository::add_member and ::remove_member now enforce CLOSED MEMBERSHIP (the acting agent must hold a live membership in the community's projected group; bootstrap exception only when that group has none, because migration 068 left every projected group with zero administrators by design; remove_member additionally always permits removing your own perspective). remove_member's handler, which previously extracted nothing at all, now takes a ViewerExtractor, and create_community passes the authenticated creator so a community created through the route is never in the bootstrap state. Gating only the PROJECTION would not have worked: 071's shim replays it out of community_members on every community-partitioned ownership write. FULLY CLOSED 2026-09-12 by tenancy/fix-authz-hygiene, which added the one thing PR-12 left: the scope extractor on both membership writes.
closed_findings.residual: The rule is deliberately weaker than the suggested require_community_admin: community groups have no admins to require, so a community whose projected group is genuinely memberless is still open to the first joiner. That is the ONLY surviving residual of this finding, it is a consequence of migration 068 rather than of route authorization, and it is handed to F-PR12-community-groups-still-have-no-admin; owner PR-18. The scope extractor this field previously listed as outstanding was added 2026-09-12 by tenancy/fix-authz-hygiene.
closed_findings.disposition_note: CLOSED by tenancy/fix-authz-hygiene, taking the stated scope-extractor residual only. routes/community.rs::add_member and ::remove_member now take RequireScopeGroupsAdmin, mirroring routes/groups.rs: scope AND membership, never OR, with the membership half staying in CommunityRepository where both writers reach it. groups:admin rather than groups:write because canonical_scopes.rs states that groups:write gates CREATING a group while managing an existing group's membership needs groups:admin plus membership -- and migration 068 projects a community onto a groups row ID-preservingly, so a membership granted here is the same group_memberships row POST /api/v1/groups/:id/members grants. AVAILABILITY COST: groups:admin is in ADMIN_ONLY_SCOPES, so every epigraph-ro and epigraph-wo token and every auto-provisioned agent now gets 403 on both routes. The rejected alternative was minting a communities:write scope, on the precedent routes/webhooks.rs::list_webhooks set when it declined a webhooks:read scope. CORRECTION: the recon's claim that remove_member has neither a Viewer nor a scope extractor is half stale -- PR-12 added ViewerExtractor; only the scope was missing. The memberless-projected-group residual this finding names is NOT closed, is not reachable from route authorization, and stays under F-PR12-community-groups-still-have-no-admin; owner PR-18. (An earlier revision of this note referred to it as 'the second residual', an ordinal that no longer matched the rewritten `residual` field above.) Mutation proof: RequireScopeGroupsAdmin -> RequireScopeGroupsWrite makes add_member_without_groups_admin_returns_403 and remove_member_without_groups_admin_returns_403_and_leaves_the_row observe 204.

closed_findings.what: The fail-open ratchet counts ONE literal spelling of the idiom, so a variant spelling raises no error
closed_findings.detail: The needle is `if let Some(axum::Extension(ref auth)) = auth_ctx`. agents.rs::create_agent uses the same idiom in two forms the needle misses: `= &auth_ctx` (trailing &) and `Some(axum::Extension(auth))` (no ref). The ratchet is therefore monotone only against one transcription. Separately, the register's rationale ('harmless only because a ViewerExtractor earlier in the same signature 401s first') does not hold for create_agent, which has no ViewerExtractor and no other auth extractor - nothing in that handler 401s and the agents:write scope is simply unchecked when AuthContext is absent. NOT FIXED IN PR-07: re-baselining that ratchet in the same PR that re-baselines the content-read register would have meant two simultaneous redefinitions, and the second would have hidden the first.
closed_findings.status: CLOSED 2026-09-12 by tenancy/fix-lint-robustness, with a mutation proof in both directions.
closed_findings.assigned: PR-16, which owns the write-path fail-opens the ratchet tracks
closed_findings.disposition_note: CLOSED by tenancy/fix-lint-robustness, in two halves with different verdicts. MECHANISM: CONFIRMED and fixed. `AUTH_CTX_NEEDLE` became `AUTH_CTX_NEEDLES`, four spellings, every one anchored on `if let`. Measured effect, tree unchanged: verbatim total 33 -> 35; FAIL_OPEN_SCOPE_SITES agents.rs 1 -> 2 (sum 23 -> 24); AUTH_OPTIONAL_PROVENANCE_SITES unchanged at 10. This is the scanner's vision changing, not the tree. The widening also produced one block fitting neither register, which `AuthCtxBlock::Unclassified`'s own doc already required be classified deliberately: a third category `AuthOptionalWrite` and a third register `AUTH_OPTIONAL_WRITE_SITES` were added, and `unclassified == 0` was KEPT rather than relaxed to 1 -- relaxing it would have switched off the sentinel that caught the case. NOT WIDENED to a bare `Some(axum::Extension(`: routes/ holds ~50 occurrences of that substring, ~18 of them the PRESCRIBED `let ... else { return Err(Unauthorized) }` shape, so that selector would charge the correct fix into a fail-open register. A new test `the_needle_set_finds_every_spelling_and_nothing_prescribed` pins all three properties over synthetic fixtures. SEVERITY CLAIM: NOT REPRODUCED, and closed as a measurement rather than fixed. The finding states that nothing in create_agent 401s and that agents:write is simply unchecked when AuthContext is absent. Re-measured: POST /agents and POST /api/v1/agents are on the `protected` router in routes/mod.rs::create_router, which is layered with bearer_auth_middleware -- a total function whose every arm either injects an AuthContext or returns Unauthorized. The two-route public allowlist does not include them and public_router_allowlist.rs pins that over both router variants. So auth_ctx is always Some when that handler runs and the scope check is unconditional in effect. SEPARATE CORRECTION, recorded because it makes the posture stronger rather than weaker: FAIL_OPEN_SCOPE_SITES' own rationale attributed its safety to 'a ViewerExtractor earlier in the same signature 401s first', which makes an authz control depend on axum parameter ORDER. Measured against the router table, the actual control for every row in both registers is the router-level middleware layer, which is order-independent. CORRECTED IN PLACE AFTER REVIEW: an earlier revision of this batch wrote that correction into AUTH_OPTIONAL_WRITE_SITES' doc comment only, ~770 lines from the register whose stated rationale was wrong, and this note claimed 'the doc now says so'. The text a contributor actually reads is fail_open_scope_check_sites_do_not_increase's FAILURE MESSAGE, which prints when any of the 8 still-registered rows reddens and which still prescribed the parameter-order reading -- so a contributor could 'fix' a row by reordering axum extractors and change nothing. That message now carries the router-level statement itself, and AUTH_OPTIONAL_WRITE_SITES' doc is now the cross-reference rather than the only copy. Two doc comments under src/routes/ (crud.rs, webhooks.rs) still carry the superseded framing; they are pre-existing, outside this batch's four findings, and are recorded as a follow-up so the correction is not later assumed complete. This batch deliberately touches zero files under any src/, which is what makes 'every count movement is scanner vision, not a tree change' provable by construction. MUTATION PROOF: a real scope block spelled `if let Some(axum::Extension(auth)) = &auth_ctx` planted in routes/papers.rs fails `fail_open_scope_check_sites_do_not_increase` with the four-needle set; with the needle set narrowed back to the single original spelling and the registers restored to their pre-widening values, THE SAME PLANTED FAIL-OPEN PASSES -- the old ratchet was blind to it. File restored byte-identically. REVIEW FOLLOW-UP, FIXED IN THE SAME BRANCH: the widened needle set was sound but unbounded from outside itself. A completeness census now pins it -- see decisions_taken.lint_robustness_needle_completeness_census. The finding stays CLOSED: its mechanism was confirmed and fixed, its severity claim was measured and not reproduced, and the census is hardening of that fix rather than a residual of it.

closed_findings.what: viewer_route_table_lint.rs::measure_fail_open_scope_sites is a raw `src.matches(needle).count()` with NO comment stripping, so it cannot distinguish a fail-open site from a doc comment QUOTING one. PR-10 fixed both webhooks.rs sites and then re-registered one by documenting the removed idiom verbatim in delete_webhook's doc comment; the ratchet went red with 'webhooks.rs: expected 0, found 1 [REGRESSION]'.
closed_findings.workaround_taken: The doc comment spells the idiom without the `axum::` path segment, and says why in place.
closed_findings.why_it_matters: Every one of the eight remaining FAIL_OPEN_SCOPE_SITES rows is assigned to PR-16, and each will hit this identically the moment its fix is documented. Compare no_bypass_in_handlers.rs, which strips `//` comments for exactly this reason - the two lints in the same repo disagree about whether a comment counts.
closed_findings.suggested_fix: Apply no_bypass_in_handlers.rs::strip_line_comments to the source before counting, in the PR that next lowers a row.
closed_findings.disposition_note: CLOSED by tenancy/fix-lint-robustness. `viewer_route_table_lint.rs::route_files` now returns comment-stripped source, so every scanner in the file -- both auth_ctx registers, the verbatim idiom total, ROUTE_LAYER_WRITES and the inline-read map -- reads code rather than prose. The helper is `no_redaction_sentinel.rs::strip_comments`, REUSED rather than re-written as the disposition required: it was lifted into `tests/lint_text/mod.rs` and both binaries declare it, so the diff that added the second consumer added no second implementation. CORRECTED AFTER REVIEW: an earlier revision said 'epigraph-api still holds exactly ONE copy of this logic', which is false -- no_bypass_in_handlers.rs::strip_line_comments is a second, narrower stripper in the same crate's tests/, and it is the very helper this finding's own suggested_fix names. Adopting lint_text there would have been a free same-crate consolidation; it was left deliberately (outside the four findings, moves no register) and both facts are now written in lint_text/mod.rs. The full inventory F-PR28-viewer-fixture-duplication inherits is FIVE strippers: 2 x strip_comments (epigraph-api, epigraph-mcp) and 3 x strip_line_comments (epigraph-api/tests/no_bypass_in_handlers.rs, epigraph-db/tests/locked_decisions.rs, epigraph-db/tests/no_anonymous_viewer.rs). The older `suggested_fix` field named `no_bypass_in_handlers.rs::strip_line_comments` instead; not taken, because it truncates at the first `//` including inside a string literal, while `strip_comments` tracks string state and also handles `/* */`. `tests/common/mod.rs` could not host it -- that module builds an axum app and needs the `db` feature, and these lints touch no database. RE-MEASURED: the finding's `where` line is stale in spelling only. PR-16/16b refactored `measure_fail_open_scope_sites` into `measure_auth_ctx_sites` + `classify_auth_ctx_block`, a `find` loop feeding a classifier; the raw-substring mechanism is unchanged and the classifier inherited it. NO NUMBER MOVED: every quantity these tests compare is byte-identical over stripped and unstripped source, so this closes a hazard without re-baselining a ratchet.
