closed_findings.what: tool_viewer_coverage.rs::viewer_acquisition_lives_in_server_rs_not_in_the_tool_modules does a raw `contains("request_viewer")` over src/tools/*.rs, so a DOC COMMENT naming the helper fails the test.
closed_findings.why_it_matters: It cost this PR a red shard: a doc paragraph in perspectives.rs explaining which principal the stdio transport resolves tripped it, and the fix was to reword prose rather than change any code. Same class as F-PR10-fail-open-lint-counts-comments. A lint that a comment can break trains contributors to avoid naming the thing they are documenting.
closed_findings.suggested_fix: Strip comments before scanning, or match `request_viewer(` at a call position rather than the bare identifier.
closed_findings.disposition_note: CLOSED by tenancy/fix-lint-robustness, and the fix covers a SECOND site in the same file that the finding does not name. The named site, `viewer_acquisition_lives_in_server_rs_not_in_the_tool_modules`, now scans comment-stripped source for the CALL position `request_viewer(` -- both of the finding's `suggested_fix` options, taken together rather than either alone, because stripping removes prose and the parenthesis narrows a bare-identifier mention to one that also writes the call's open parenthesis. It also sorts its result before comparing against a `Vec`; with one match that was unobservable, with two it would have compared against `read_dir` order. The UNNAMED site is `tools`, whose acquisition predicate classified each `#[tool(` span by the same raw substring. Its failure direction is the opposite one and it was fixed in the same change: the named site fails LOUDLY on prose, while a misclassification in `tools` reports that a viewer was acquired when none was. Fixing the reported half and leaving the other in the same function would not have been defensible. A cross-crate copy of `strip_comments` was required -- epigraph-mcp had no stripper at all -- and is recorded as one deliberate copy in `crates/epigraph-mcp/tests/lint_text/mod.rs`; the shape of cross-crate test-helper reuse remains with F-PR28-viewer-fixture-duplication and its batch, and the copy is one file with one dependency-free function so that decision can absorb it. NO NUMBER MOVED: 83 `#[tool(`, 61 Request / 3 Maintenance / 19 None, and the tool-module set ['viewer.rs'] are identical stripped and unstripped. MUTATION PROOF, both directions, same planted tree: a doc paragraph naming the helper at a call position in tools/perspectives.rs leaves the named test GREEN. For the unnamed site, a dispatch body that only MENTIONS the helper while acquiring nothing, with its name removed from EXPECTED_TOOLS_WITHOUT_A_VIEWER to model a newly added tool, makes `every_content_reading_tool_derives_a_viewer` and `the_three_categories_partition_every_tool` FAIL and name it -- while the pre-fix predicate passes ALL FIVE TESTS on that same tree. Both files restored byte-identically. CORRECTION AFTER REVIEW, doc-accuracy only: an earlier revision of this note and of `tools`' doc comment said the parenthesis 'rules out a mention inside a string literal'. It does not -- strip_comments preserves string contents by design, so the call text inside a format string or a #[tool(description = ...)] blob would still classify the span as Request, which is the silent direction. MEASURED: zero such strings exist -- all 61 request_viewer occurrences in server.rs are real calls, and both non-call maintenance_viewer hits are doc comments, which stripping removes. So the population is clean and the residual is now STATED in `tools`' doc rather than denied. Blanking string contents as well as comments is the fix and would move this crate's registers, so it is not folded in beside a doc correction.

A harvester_fragments row written before the harvester_claim_provenance row that links it to its claim now inherits that claim's tenancy at the moment the link is inserted. closed_findings.detail: RE-MEASURED BEFORE BEING FIXED, and it reproduced. On a throwaway database at migration head (max(version)=91), in rolled-back transactions: an undeclared fragment insert lands (public, <seed group>) on migration 074's epigraph_root_require_tenancy seed arm; a fragment declaring (public, <world>) lands there; and in BOTH cases inserting the provenance row for a group-private claim left the fragment exactly as found. CORRECTION TO THE BATCH SPEC, WHICH WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE SHIPPED A NO-OP: the spec's predicate named the world sentinel alone, mirroring tenancy_backfill.rs::backfill_harvester_fragments, which was written before 074 made harvester_fragments a parentless root. At head the undeclared case is SEED-stamped, not world-stamped, so a world-only predicate leaves it untouched. QUALIFIED ON REVIEW, because the unqualified form is a claim later runs would quote as fact: 074's seed arm is gated on pg_has_role(session_user, 'epigraph_seed', 'MEMBER') and otherwise RAISEs 23502, so the seed-stamped shape arises on a seed-member session - which the superuser test harness satisfies, and so does a deployment that has not done plan 9.2's week-11d credential split. On a session that is NOT a seed member there is no undeclared-insert case at all. Both sentinel spellings are named because both are REACHABLE, not because world is unreachable; the finding's own 'keeps (public, world) permanently' was itself the pre-074 spelling. 089 names both sentinels on the target side. That is not the widening the spec forbids: 062's harvester_fragments_group_needs_real_group CHECK defines exactly this pair as non-owners, because both groups are memberless by design. The source-side clause (c.owner_group_id <> world) is unchanged from the backfill; extending it to seed as well would have been narrowing logic the spec also forbids, and is unnecessary because the target side treats seed as unstamped. A SECOND SPEC ITEM WAS UNSATISFIABLE AND WAS SUBSTITUTED, NOT DROPPED. Acceptance asked that the reverse order (provenance row first, fragment second) keep working. That order does not exist: harvester_claim_provenance_fragment_id_fkey is NOT DEFERRABLE (condeferrable=false), so it raises 23503 in any statement order and any transaction - measured. The regression it was reaching for is 070 arm (d), which is what a_claims_tenancy_update_still_propagates_to_the_fragment asserts instead. REVIEW PASS 2026-09-12, SAME BATCH, and it changed no SQL. Four things the first cut asserted were re-measured and found wrong, all of them rationale rather than behaviour, and all of them corrected in place: (1) 'CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION re-grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC' - FALSE on PostgreSQL 16.13; replacement PRESERVES proacl, a first CREATE leaves it NULL (which IS the implicit PUBLIC grant, so the REVOKE is still required), and DROP+CREATE is the shape that restores the grant. The claim had been copied from 086's pre-existing prose, which is corrected in the same change and named as an inherited correction. (2) 'an app-owned definer frame is WITH CHECK-filtered and stamps nothing, silently' - not what happens; see the measurement recorded on F-PR12-ci-runs-as-superuser-so-the-42501-arm-is-untestable. (3) 'verify is the only instrument that reports the guarded-ALTER no-op cluster' - on that cluster the ROLE is absent and verify reports it at its role-existence branch, which returns before the per-function loop; the per-function pg_has_role predicate catches a non-member owner, and passes a superuser-owned body, correctly. (4) backfill_harvester_fragments' own doc comment still said a fragment written before its provenance row 'is therefore never stamped by any trigger' and that new rows in that order 'remain a live gap' - both made false by this very change and both rewritten. AND ONE TEST THAT COULD NOT FAIL: a_public_claim_leaves_its_fragment_public asserted visibility alone, so deleting the source-side c.owner_group_id <> world clause moved the owner seed -> world and left the test green. It now captures the tuple before the link and asserts the whole of it unchanged. MUTATION PROOF for that repair, run not reasoned: with the source-side clause deleted from 089 it FAILS on its own assertion; restored, it passes.
closed_findings.verification: Eight new tests. Six in crates/epigraph-db/tests/tenancy_triggers.rs: the failing order closes (both sentinel spellings, as two cases), an already-owned fragment is NOT re-stamped by a claim in a different group (the no-widening case), a public claim leaves the fragment public, 070 arm (d) still propagates, and the file is safe to re-run (one trigger after a re-apply, PUBLIC still revoked, and the mechanism still stamps). One catalog test in crates/epigraph-db/tests/schema_contract.rs::migration_089_stamping_definer_is_revoked_from_public (SECURITY DEFINER, owned by epigraph_maintenance, explicit non-NULL proacl excluding PUBLIC) - no generic revoked-from-PUBLIC sweep exists in this workspace, so that pin is bespoke, mirroring 086's. The function is added to tenancy_triggers.rs::propagation_function_is_owned_by_the_maintenance_role, which enumerates by name, and to tenancy_backfill.rs::DEFERRED_DEFINER_FUNCTIONS - not DEFINER_FUNCTIONS: 089 is later than the migrations week 11c applies, so an unconditional entry would report "does not exist" and block a correctly-sequenced deploy. That entry is covered by a new crates/epigraph-cli/tests/backfill_idempotence.rs::verify_covers_the_089_stamping_definer_once_its_migration_is_applied, because a presence-gated list entry with no test is a control that can be right in the runbook and vacuous in CI. MUTATION PROOF, TWO DIRECTIONS, BOTH RUN RATHER THAN REASONED. (1) The still-unstamped clause was OR-ed away - "AND (f.owner_group_id IN (world, seed) OR true)", preserving arity so the UPDATE still executed: an_already_owned_fragment_is_not_re_stamped_by_a_later_claim FAILED on its own assertion (the fragment came back owned by the second claim's group) and it was the ONLY failure in that binary - 22 of 23 passed, so the mutation was surgical and the fix is not over-suppressing. (2) The migration file was moved aside entirely: FIVE tests failed, all expected - the two inherit tests on their own assertions (observed (seed, public) and (world, public) respectively, which is also the direct evidence that a world-only predicate would have been a no-op for the seed case), plus every_tenancy_trigger_is_enabled (20 vs 21), migration_089_is_safe_to_re_run (0 triggers vs 1) and propagation_function_is_owned_by_the_maintenance_role (function absent). Note that an_already_owned_fragment_is_not_re_stamped_by_a_later_claim PASSES with the migration absent, vacuously, which is why mutation (1) is the load-bearing proof for that clause. RESTORE PROVED BYTE-IDENTICAL after both mutations by sha256 (5fca4c4d253cd52f5306dc9126206a37d60224843c6604f0c1875b5054bbdfb4); git diff --stat cannot supply that for a file that is still untracked. BOTH APPLICATION ORDERS VERIFIED: 089 applied out of order onto a database already at head 91, and in order on a freshly created database (which then reported max(version)=91 over 89 rows). The throwaway was dropped and recreated before every run that followed an edit to the migration, because _sqlx_migrations stores a per-version checksum and the resulting VersionMismatch surfaces in epigraph-engine/tests/export_prov_o.rs - a shared-database replay - while every #[sqlx::test] binary stays green.

closed_findings.closing_measurement: THE ASYMMETRY IS CLOSED. AppState::assert_tenancy_triggers_armed now carries a THIRD tier, TENANCY_TRIGGERS_089, required only when migration 089's own function epigraph_inherit_fragment_tenancy_stmt is present in pg_proc. THE RECON'S 'THE FIX IS ONE ARRAY ENTRY' IS WRONG ABOUT WHICH ARRAY, and the finding itself says so: an entry in TENANCY_TRIGGERS_070 refuses every pre-089 database -- the plan 9.2 step (i) outage the staged split exists to prevent -- and one in TENANCY_TRIGGERS_074 refuses every database between 074 and 089. Only a tier gated on 089's own marker refuses the right population. THE MARKER IS THE FUNCTION, NOT THE TRIGGER. A gate keyed on the trigger would be vacuous by construction: the state it exists to catch is the trigger's absence, and the marker would vanish with it. 089 installs CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION as well as CREATE TRIGGER, so 'function present, trigger absent' is exactly the refusable state. pg_proc rather than the _sqlx_migrations version-89 row, so a hand-edited migrations table cannot decide a safety check. THE NEW TIER IS ALSO CHAINED INTO THE existing_tables BIND LIST. A relation missing from that list falls to table_absent and WARNS instead of refusing -- i.e. the fix would itself fail open. It happens to be redundant today because 089's relation is already in 070's list; it is spelled anyway so the next tier's relation is not left to that accident. THE RECON'S 'TWO TESTS PIN THE TRIGGER COUNT AT 21 -- EXPECT TO UPDATE THEM' IS FALSE AND WAS NOT ACTED ON. Both pins count pg_trigger rows, not entries in a Rust array; 089's trigger already matches their LIKE pattern and is already inside the 21, and this batch adds no migration, so no trigger is created or dropped. Re-run green and unchanged: tenancy_triggers.rs::every_tenancy_trigger_is_enabled (21), locked_decisions.rs::d1_tenancy_stamping_triggers_are_armed (21), and the third pin the recon does not mention, tenancy_required.rs::a5_every_tenancy_trigger_is_enabled (24, the _require_tenancy subset, unaffected because 089's is an _inherit_tenancy name). Editing 21 to 22 would have failed a correct tree. ACCEPTANCE IS THREE CASES, in epigraph-api/tests/tenancy_trigger_boot_refusal.rs -- there was no test over this function at all before. A database at head boots; the trigger dropped with the function present refuses and names the trigger; the trigger AND function both dropped still boots. The third case is what discriminates a marker-gated tier from an unconditional entry, which would pass the first two and fail it. COST PAID AND RECORDED: the marker probe is a third self.db_pool site in state.rs, so no_unscoped_pool.rs::EXEMPT moves 9 -> 10 with its enumerating reason rewritten. TENANCY_TRIGGERS_070's doc comment recorded the deliberate omission and has been rewritten, because closing this made that paragraph false.
closed_findings.pre_fix_owner_reasoning: An UNCONDITIONAL entry is ruled out by measurement, not by preference: it would refuse every pre-089 database, which is the plan 9.2 step (i) failure the two-tier split exists to prevent. A gate on 089's own function (or on the _sqlx_migrations version-89 row) is available and would not be vacuous - it would catch a manually dropped trigger. That is the reasoning the delivered tier follows.

findings_disposition_2026_09_12.why: All 54 open findings were carried with owners that had gone stale: eleven named PR-16, which is delivered, and a further group named 'the conversion-shard series', which is not a scheduled PR. An owner that does not exist is not an owner, so this pass gives every finding exactly one disposition from a closed vocabulary and says plainly which ones nobody is going to do.

vocabulary.FIX-SCHEDULED: A named branch in this cleanup fixes it, with a mutation proof.
vocabulary.OPERATOR-DECISION: Blocked on a decision only the operator can make. Recorded in the operator's pending-decisions record.
vocabulary.ACCEPTED: Carried deliberately. Needs no owner, and the reason it needs none is stated.
vocabulary.CONVERSION-TAIL: Belongs to the unnumbered conversion tail (the remaining .db_pool call sites that gate FORCE-RLS). That tail is not a scheduled PR and has no owner TODAY, which is what this label records. It is explicitly a CANDIDATE FOR SCHEDULING, not a decision that the work will not be done -- the operator may well schedule it. The label exists so the absence of a current owner is visible instead of being hidden behind an owner that does not exist.
vocabulary.CLOSED: Re-measured on 0f6f8b02 and moved to closed_findings, with the measurement recorded.
vocabulary.EMPTY-NEEDS-RE-DERIVATION: The finding's detail was redacted from this public repository and the private record it points to was never written. The finding is empty and must be re-derived from the code before it can be disposed.

The lesson is that a closed vocabulary needs a check, not just a declaration: nothing in the repository failed when a sixth term appeared, and nothing failed when a fix_batch label outlived its batch. Filed as the reason a future pass should assert both properties.

findings_disposition_2026_09_12.disposition_on_obligations: THE REGISTER'S SCOPE IS WIDENED HERE, EXPLICITLY, BECAUSE IT WAS WIDENED SILENTLY FIRST. `disposition` was absent from all 48 deferred_obligations entries until tenancy/fix-security-track put one on the six it took, importing a findings-register field into the obligations register with nothing saying so. Stated rather than reverted, because the field is useful on an obligation for the same reason it is useful on a finding. TWO rules make the vocabulary mean the same thing in both registers: (a) CLOSED on an OBLIGATION means DISCHARGED IN PLACE, with the measurement recorded on the entry. An obligation is never moved into closed_findings -- that array is the findings register, and moving one there would corrupt both counts. (b) FIX-SCHEDULED is FUTURE TENSE and must not sit beside a status saying the fix has shipped. vocabulary_drift_2026_09_13 already records two entries that carried it past their batch; an entry reading both 'a named branch fixes it' and 'RESOLVED by that branch' is the same defect in one object. Once the branch has shipped, the term is CLOSED if the obligation is discharged, or a term naming what still blocks it if it is not. tenancy/fix-security-track's own entries were corrected to this rule in its land phase: D-PR16-claim-provenance-trace-read-unfiltered -> CLOSED (discharged), D-PR16-recall-events-are-instance-wide -> OPERATOR-DECISION (code half discharged, two residuals named, one of them an operator-run reconciliation pass).

force_preconditions_batch_2026_09_15.land_phase_corrections: SIX OF THIS BATCH'S OWN RECORDED CLAIMS DID NOT SURVIVE THE LAND-PHASE REVIEW. They are corrected in the entries rather than quoted, and listed here because the pattern -- a batch's own report is a claim about the tree on the day it was written -- is what this series keeps hitting. (1) 'The coupling IS enforced by the type' was false: Viewer is Clone, so a deliberate clone still yields an owned bypass. Corrected in five places and the obligation moved CLOSED -> ACCEPTED with the residual named. (2) The new hybrid lint was recorded as DISCHARGING D-PR17-hybrid-shape-lint; its scanner is function-granular and cannot see a mint and spend that straddle a function or a file, which is where the largest residual (epigraph-mcp's three maintenance tools) actually lives. CLOSED -> ACCEPTED, with all three limits stated in the lint file. (3) Migration 090's header said case 2's endpoints become public 'through the admin declassification surface'; that surface re-runs the boundary meet in the same transaction, so it does not produce the state. Restated in the header, the test doc and the ledger. (4) The _returning variant's ON CONFLICT was recorded as converting a 23505 into the correct (existing_id, false); that holds only for a visible conflicting row and has no test. Narrowed. (5) ScopedPool::maintenance_session's doc enumerated 'the privatization job's five sites' as callers minting no viewer; one of the five minted, and it was converted in the land phase so the claim is now true of all four. (6) D-PR17-read-guards-widen-under-rls carried FIX-SCHEDULED in the batch that shipped its fix, which disposition_on_obligations rule (b) forbids; corrected to CONVERSION-TAIL, matching the sibling D-PR17-structural-force-mode-test in the same diff.
